==New Russian cinema==

=== 1990s ===

[[File:Aleksei Balabanov.JPG|thumb|left|200px|[[Aleksei Balabanov]]'s crime film duology ''Brother'' became a defining example of [[cult film|cult cinema]] in Russia.]]

In the 1990s there were much fewer films being made as the cinema industry was experiencing big changes and the economy was uncertain. From 300 in 1990 the number fell to 213 in 1991, 172 in 1992, 152 in 1993, to 68 in 1994, 46 in 1995 and 28 in 1996.<ref name="Richard Taylor, Nancy Wood, Julian Graffy, Dina Iordanova 2019 1923–1927">{{cite book|title=The BFI Companion to Eastern European and Russian Cinema|pages=1923–1927|author1=Richard Taylor|author2=Nancy Wood|author3=Julian Graffy|author4=Dina Iordanova|publisher=Bloomsbury|isbn=978-1838718497|date=2019}}</ref>

In 1990 censorship was abolished on an official level: the state could no longer interfere in the production and distribution of films, except in cases of war propaganda, disclosure of state secrets, and pornography. As part of the abolition of all central Soviet administrative units, the Cinema Committee of the USSR was dissolved in 1991.<ref>{{cite book|title=Historical Dictionary of Russian and Soviet Cinema|author=Peter Rollberg|publisher=Rowman & Littlefield|year=2009|place=US|isbn=978-0-8108-6072-8|page=xxxiv}}</ref>

Russian cinema of the 90s acquired new features and themes, with the [[Chechen–Russian conflict|Chechen war]] also affecting filmmakers. Many films of that time dealt with war and Stalinism.<ref>{{cite book|title=Pop Culture Russia!: Media, Arts, and Lifestyle|author=Birgit Beumers|page=80|isbn=1-85109-459-8|year=2005|publisher=Abc-Clio }}</ref>

[[Kinotavr]] was first held in 1990 in [[Podolsk]], and then in 1991 in [[Sochi]], where it has been held ever since. The [[Nika Award]], which is distributed by the Russian Film Academy, was founded in 1998.<ref name="Richard Taylor, Nancy Wood, Julian Graffy, Dina Iordanova 2019 1923–1927"/>

''[[The Asthenic Syndrome]]'' is a 1989 [[drama film]] directed by [[Kira Muratova]]. The film was entered into the [[40th Berlin International Film Festival]] where it won the [[Jury Grand Prix|Silver Bear – Special Jury Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/1990/03_preistr_ger_1990/03_Preistraeger_1990.html |title=Berlinale: 1990 Prize Winners |access-date=16 March 2011 |work=berlinale.de}}</ref>

''[[Freeze Die Come to Life]]'' is 1989 [[drama film]] directed by [[Vitali Kanevsky]]. It was screened in the [[Un Certain Regard]] section at the [[1990 Cannes Film Festival]], where it won the [[Caméra d'Or]].<ref name="festival-cannes-freeze">{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/151/year/1990.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Freeze Die Come to Life |access-date=8 August 2009|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref> Another Kanevsky's film, ''[[An Independent Life]]'', win the [[Jury Prize (Cannes Film Festival)|Jury Prize]], the third most prestigious award of the event, at the [[1992 Cannes Film Festival]]{{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} and also nominated for the [[Golden Bear]] at the [[42nd Berlin International Film Festival]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1990 [[Pavel Lungin]] won the [[Best Director Award (Cannes Film Festival)|Best Director Award]] for ''[[Taxi Blues]]'', which starred rock musician [[Pyotr Mamonov]] in the lead role, at the [[1990 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite news |date=18 January 1991 |title=Review/Film; Harshness of Soviet Life In Lungin's 'Taxi Blues' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/01/18/movies/review-film-harshness-of-soviet-life-in-lungin-s-taxi-blues.html |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> Subsequent Lungin films, ''[[Luna Park (1992 film)|Luna Park]]'' and ''[[The Wedding (2000 film)|The Wedding]]'', were  screened at [[1992 Cannes Film Festival]] and [[2000 Cannes Film Festival]]  in competition. ''[[Tsar (film)|Tsar]]'' was  screened at [[2009 Cannes Film Festival]] in  [[Un Certain Regard]] section.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cannes Festival |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/1992/inCompetition.html|access-date=29 January 2013}}</ref><ref name="festival-cannes.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/5179/year/2000.html |title=Festival de Cannes: The Wedding |access-date=10 October 2009|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref><ref name="festival-cannes-2009">{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/10877371/year/2009.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Tsar |access-date=17 May 2009|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref>

''[[The Guard (1990 film)|The Guard]]'' is a 1990 [[drama film]]  directed by [[Aleksandr Rogozhkin]]. It was entered into the [[40th Berlin International Film Festival]] where it won the [[Alfred Bauer Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/1990/03_preistr_ger_1990/03_Preistraeger_1990.html |title=Berlinale: 1990 Prize Winners |access-date=19 March 2011 |work=berlinale.de}}</ref>

''[[Satan (1991 film)|Satan]]'' is a 1991 [[thriller film]] directed by [[Viktor Aristov (director)|Viktor Aristov]]. It was entered into the [[41st Berlin International Film Festival]] where it won the [[Jury Grand Prix|Silver Bear – Special Jury Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Berlinale: 1991 Prize Winners |url=http://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/1991/03_preistr_ger_1991/03_Preistraeger_1991.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120118183843/http://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/1991/03_preistr_ger_1991/03_Preistraeger_1991.html |archive-date=18 January 2012 |access-date=26 March 2011 |work=berlinale.de}}</ref>

''[[The Assassin of the Tsar]]'' by [[Karen Shakhnazarov]] and ''[[Anna Karamazoff]]'' by [[Rustam Khamdamov]] was entered into the [[1991 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Festival de Cannes: The Assassin of the Tsar |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/77/year/1991.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004163751/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/77/year/1991.html |archive-date=4 October 2012 |access-date=2009-08-09 |work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Festival de Cannes: Anna Karamazoff |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/82/year/1991.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004075427/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/82/year/1991.html |archive-date=4 October 2012 |access-date=9 August 2009 |work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref> ''[[Comrade Chkalov Crosses the North Pole]]'' by [[Maksim Pezhemsky]] was screened in the [[Un Certain Regard]] section at the same year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/128/year/1991.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Perekhod tovarishcha Chkalova cherez severnyy polyus |access-date=11 August 2009 |work=festival-cannes.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102141322/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/128/year/1991.html |archive-date=2 January 2013}}</ref>

[[Nikita Mikhalkov]] won the [[Golden Lion]] at the [[48th Venice International Film Festival]] for ''[[Close to Eden]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rbth.com/arts/2015/09/04/4_russian_films_that_scooped_the_golden_lion_at_venice_48999.html|work=RBTH|title=4 Russian films that scooped the Golden Lion at Venice|author=Valery Kichin|date=4 September 2015 }}</ref> and [[European Film Award for Best Film]] in 1991 and was nominated for an [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Film]]<ref name="Oscars1993">{{Cite web|url=http://www.oscars.org/oscars/ceremonies/1993 |title=The 65th Academy Awards (1993) Nominees and Winners |access-date=19 September 2015 |work=oscars.org |date=4 October 2014 }}</ref> and a [[Golden Globe Award|Golden Globe]] for  [[Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]].

''[[The Inner Circle (1991 film)|The Inner Circle]]'' is a 1991 [[drama]] film by Russian director [[Andrei Konchalovsky]], telling the story of [[Joseph Stalin]]'s private [[projectionist]] and [[KGB]] officer [[Ivan Sanchin]] (real name Alex Ganchin) between 1939 and 1953, the year Stalin died was nominated for awards at the [[42nd Berlin International Film Festival]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Berlinale: 1992 Programme |url=http://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/1992/02_programm_1992/02_Programm_1992.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050512085854/http://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/1992/02_programm_1992/02_Programm_1992.html |archive-date=12 May 2005 |access-date=2011-05-22 |work=berlinale.de}}</ref>

''[[The Chekist]]'' directed by [[Aleksandr Rogozhkin]] was a drama set in the period of [[Red Terror]] and told the story of a [[Cheka]] leader who gradually becomes unhinged. ''[[Happy Days (1991 film)|Happy Days]]'' directed by [[Aleksei Balabanov]] was his feature film debut. Both film were screened in the [[Un Certain Regard]] section at the [[1992 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Tchekiste |trans-title=The Chekist |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/65/year/1992.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121005005833/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/65/year/1992.html |archive-date=5 October 2012 |access-date=16 August 2009 |work=[[Cannes Film Festival]] |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Festival de Cannes: Happy Days |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/56/year/1992.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121005005704/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/56/year/1992.html |archive-date=5 October 2012 |accessdate=16 August 2009 |work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref>

''[[The Sentimental Policeman]]'' is a 1992 Russian-language Ukrainian (Ukrainian-French production) [[comedy film]] written and directed by [[Kira Muratova]]. It entered the competition at the [[49th Venice International Film Festival]]<ref>{{cite book|last=Jane Taubman|title= Kira Muratova: Kinofile Filmmakers' Companion|date= 26 November 2004|publisher=I.B.Tauris, 2004|isbn=0857714104}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Venezia, Libertà Per Gli Autori |url=https://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1992/07/31/venezia-liberta-per-gli-autori.html?ref=search |access-date=29 April 2014|newspaper=[[La Repubblica]]|date=31 July 1992}}</ref> and won the Special Jury Prize at [[Kinotavr]].

[[Bakhtyar Khudojnazarov]] won a [[Silver Lion]] at the [[50th Venice International Film Festival]] for his film ''[[Kosh ba kosh]]''.<ref>{{cite web
|title=50th Venice Film Festival 1993 – FilmAffinity
|url=https://www.filmaffinity.com/en/awards.php?award_id=venice&year=1993
|access-date=2017-05-28
}}</ref>

The drama ''[[Burnt by the Sun]]'' (1994) by [[Nikita Mikhalkov]] is set in a small countryside community in the time when Stalinism starts to disrupt their idyllic retreat and alter their characters and fates. The film received an [[Academy Award]] for [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] and the [[Grand Prix (Cannes Film Festival)|Grand Prix du Jury]] at the [[1994 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 28, 1995 |title='Burnt By the Sun' Wins Foreign Film Oscar |url=https://apnews.com/article/7ff26d4255e743efc7e2f110d10e09af |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531162345/https://apnews.com/article/7ff26d4255e743efc7e2f110d10e09af |archive-date=2022-05-31 |access-date=2025-12-04 |work=AP NEWS |language=en}}</ref> The sequel, ''[[Burnt by the Sun 2|Burnt by the Sun 2: Exodus]]''  was entered in the [[2010 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref name="hollywoodreporter">{{cite news|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/hr/content_display/world/news/e3i3d82e5b089623802884efcd38a037f67?pn=2 |title=Hollywood Reporter: Cannes Lineup |access-date=2010-04-16 |work=hollywoodreporter |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100422212018/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/hr/content_display/world/news/e3i3d82e5b089623802884efcd38a037f67?pn=2 |archive-date=April 22, 2010 }}</ref> Another sequel, '' [[Burnt by the Sun 3: The Citadel]]'', released on May 5, 2011.

''[[Assia and the Hen with the Golden Eggs]]'' by [[Andrei Konchalovsky]] is a satirical sequel to Konchalovsky's 1966 Soviet film, [[The Story of Asya Klyachina]], taking the characters of the original and placing them in a post-Soviet context. This film was entered into the [[1994 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/2962/year/1994.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Assia and the Hen with the Golden Eggs |access-date=27 August 2009|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref>

''[[Passions (1994 film)|Passions]]'' is a 1994 [[romantic comedy]] by Ukrainian director [[Kira Muratova]] based on the novellas of Boris Dedyukhin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kommersant.ru/doc/72866|publisher=[[Kommersant]]|author=Andrei Plakhov|title=Премьера нового фильма Киры Муратовой|date=1994-05-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://humanities_dictionary.academic.ru/3928/%D0%9C%D1%83%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B0_%D0%9A%D0%B8%D1%80%D0%B0_%D0%93%D0%B5%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%B3=publisher=dictionary.academic.ru|title=Российский гуманитарный энциклопедический словарь}}</ref>
It was screened at the [[Locarno Festival]] in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.pardo.ch/details.do?methodcall=filmDetails&oc=238383|publisher=[[Locarno Festival]]|title=UVLECENJA|access-date=2023-05-29|archive-date=2017-04-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170424001738/http://archive.pardo.ch/details.do?methodcall=filmDetails&oc=238383|url-status=dead}}</ref>
It received two [[Nika Awards]], for Best Picture and Best Director (Muratova).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kino-nika.com/page91749.html|publisher=[[Nika Award]]|title=Лауреаты Национальной кинематографической премии "НИКА" за 1994 год.}}</ref> The picture also won the Special Jury Prize of the [[Kinotavr]] film festival.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kinotavr.ru/ru/history/winners/|publisher=[[Kinotavr]]|title=Призеры 1991-2005 гг.|access-date=2017-04-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023014844/http://www.kinotavr.ru/ru/history/winners/|archive-date=2013-10-23|url-status=dead}}</ref>

''[[The Life and Extraordinary Adventures of Private Ivan Chonkin]]'' directed by [[Jiří Menzel]], [[co-production (media)|international co-production]] between Russia, Czech Republic, the United Kingdom, France and Italy, was entered the competition at the [[51st Venice International Film Festival]], in which it won the President of the Italian Senate's Gold Medal.<ref>Edoardo Pittalis, Roberto Pugliese, ''Bella di Notte'', August 1996.</ref>

''[[A Play for a Passenger]]'' directed by [[Vadim Abdrashitov]] was entered into the [[45th Berlin International Film Festival]], where it won the [[Silver Bear]].<ref name="Berlinale">{{cite web |url=http://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/1995/03_preistr_ger_1995/03_Preistraeger_1995.html |title=Berlinale: 1995 Prize Winners |accessdate=31 December 2011 |work=berlinale.de}}</ref>

''[[A Moslem]]'' is a 1995 Russian [[drama film]] directed by [[Vladimir Khotinenko]]<ref name="NY Times">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/movies/movie/135808/The-Moslem/overview |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325024655/http://www.nytimes.com/movies/movie/135808/The-Moslem/overview |url-status=dead |archive-date=25 March 2016 |department=Movies & TV Dept. |work=[[The New York Times]] |author=Sandra Brennan |date=2016 |title=A Moslem |access-date=4 October 2015 }}</ref> won Special Grand Prix of the jury for "Best film of the year" at 1995 [[Montreal World Film Festival]].

''[[Peculiarities of the National Hunt]]'' directed by [[Aleksandr Rogozhkin]] was screened in Window on Images sectiom at the [[52nd Venice International Film Festival]] and nominated on Crystal Globe at the [[Karlovy Vary International Film Festival]].

In 1996 [[Sergey Bodrov]] was screened the war drama film ''[[Prisoner of the Mountains]]'' based on the 1872 [[Caucasian War]]-era short story "[[The Prisoner of the Caucasus (story)|The Prisoner in the Caucasus]]" by the classic Russian writer [[Leo Tolstoy]]<ref>{{cite book|title=Historical Dictionary of Russian and Soviet Cinema|author=Peter Rollberg|publisher=Rowman & Littlefield|year=2009|place=US|isbn=978-0-8108-6072-8|page=544}}</ref> on 1996 [[Karlovy Vary International Film Festival]] and won a [[Crystal Globe (Karlovy Vary International Film Festival)|Crystal Globe]]. Latef film was nominated for an [[Academy Award]] for [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] (Russia)<ref name="Oscars1997">{{Cite web|url=http://www.oscars.org/oscars/ceremonies/1997 |title=The 69th Academy Awards (1997) Nominees and Winners |access-date=5 October 2015 |work=oscars.org |date=5 October 2014 }}</ref> and a [[Golden Globe Award]] for  [[Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] (Russia).

''[[Three Stories (1997 film)|Three Stories]]'' is a 1997 Russian-Ukrainian [[comedy film]] directed by [[Kira Muratova]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vokrug.tv/product/show/tri_istorii/|publisher=VokrugTV|title=Три истории}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://seance.ru/n/15/rezhisser-film-kritik-3/tri-istorii/|publisher=[[Seance]]|title=Сеансу отвечают: Три истории}}</ref> It was entered into the [[47th Berlin International Film Festival]]. The picture won the Special Jury Prize at [[Kinotavr]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kinotavr.ru/ru/history/winners/|publisher=[[Kinotavr]]|title=Призеры 1991-2005 гг.}}</ref>

In the context of the Russian World War II history [[Pavel Chukhrai]] filmed ''[[The Thief (1997 film)|The Thief]]'' (1997), a movie about a mother who becomes romantically involved with a criminal who impersonates an officer. The film was awarded with 6 national prizes [[Nika Award|Nika]], got a special prize in [[54th Venice International Film Festival]] and was nominated on [[European Film Award for Best Film]], [[Academy Award]] for [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] and [[Golden Globe Award]] for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]].<ref>{{cite book|title=The BFI Companion to Eastern European and Russian Cinema|page=1938|author1=Richard Taylor|author2=Nancy Wood|author3=Julian Graffy|author4=Dina Iordanova|publisher=Bloomsbury|isbn=978-1838718497|date=2019}}</ref>

One of the first commercially successful post-Soviet films was the crime drama ''[[Brother (1997 film)|Brother]]'' directed by [[Aleksei Balabanov]]. It was screened as part of the [[Un Certain Regard]] section at the [[1997 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4848/year/1997.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Traveling Companion |access-date=2009-09-26|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref> He also directed the sequel ''[[Brother 2]]'' in 2000.

[[Valery Todorovsky]]'s ''[[The Country of the Deaf]]'' (1998), a comedy film based on the screenplay by [[Renata Litvinova]] parodied Russia of the 90s. It described the journey of two female friends caught in the fight of two clans – the deaf and the hearing. It was entered in the [[48th Berlin International Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/1998/02_programm_1998/02_Programm_1998.html |title=Berlinale: 1998 Programme |access-date=22 January 2012 |work=berlinale.de}}</ref>

In 1997 [[Aleksandr Sokurov]] had his international breakthrough with the arthouse drama ''[[Mother and Son (1997 film)|Mother and Son]]'', the first part of family relationships dilogy. It won the Special Silver St. George at the [[20th Moscow International Film Festival]] in 1997.  The second part, ''[[Father and Son (2003 film)|Father and Son]]'', Russian drama film that was entered into feature film competition at the [[2003 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref name="festival-cannes-father-son">{{cite web|url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4081438/year/2003.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Father and Son |access-date=7 November 2009 |work=festival-cannes.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121010052155/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4081438/year/2003.html |archive-date=10 October 2012 }}</ref>

1998 film ''[[Khrustalyov, My Car!]]'' directed by [[Aleksei Yuryevich German|Aleksei German]] described the last days of Stalinist Russia. It was entered in the [[1998 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4915/year/1998.html|title=Festival de Cannes: Khrustalyov, My Car!|access-date=30 September 2009|website=[[Cannes Film Festival|Festival de Cannes]]}}</ref>

In 1998 at the [[Locarno Film Festival]] ''[[Time of a Dancer]]'', directed by [[Vadim Abdrashitov]], won Special Jury Prize.

[[Nikita Mikhalkov]]'s international co-production ''[[The Barber of Siberia]]'' was screened out of competition at the [[1999 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/5307/year/1999.html |title=Festival de Cannes: The Barber of Siberia |access-date=2009-10-11|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref> The film featured English and Russian actors. It was the first post-Soviet big budget feature film; the film cost 35 million dollars.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rbth.com/arts/328599-12-russian-european-movies|work=RBTH|title=12 Russian-European movies you must watch before you die|author=Boris Egorog|date=25 June 2018 }}</ref>

''[[Moloch (1999 film)|Moloch]]'', the first part of tetrology of power directed by [[Alexander Sokurov]] portrays [[Adolf Hitler]] living life in an unassuming manner during an abrupt journey to the [[Bavarian Alps]], was entered into the [[1999 Cannes Film Festival]] and won the  [[Best Screenplay Award (Cannes Film Festival)|Best Screenplay Award]].<ref name="festival-cannes-moloch">{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/5313/year/1999.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Moloch |work=festival-cannes.com|access-date=2010-12-21}}</ref> The second part portraying [[Vladimir Lenin]], ''[[Taurus (2001 film)|Taurus]]'', was entered into the [[2001 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref name="festival-cannes-tau">{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/2001813/year/2001.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Taurus |access-date=18 October 2009|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref> The third part ''[[The Sun (2005 film)|The Sun]]'' depicting [[Emperor of Japan|Japanese Emperor]] Shōwa ([[Hirohito]]) during the [[End of World War II in Asia|final days]] of [[World War II]], was entered in the [[55th Berlin International Film Festival]].

Internationally co-produced film ''[[East/West]]'' (1999) starring [[Sandrine Bonnaire]] and [[Catherine Deneuve]] told the story of an emigre family living in Stalinist USSR. The film was nominated as  [[Academy Award]] for [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] and [[Golden Globe Award]] for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]], [[National Board of Review]], and received four nominations at the [[César Award]]s.

The satiric melodrama of [[Dmitry Meskhiev]], ''[[Women's Property]]'' (1999) describes a love affair between a young student and an older actress who is incurably ill. Her death leads the protagonist to face bitter loneliness. The film starred [[Yelena Safonova]] and featured actor [[Konstantin Khabensky]] in an early lead role.

Cult crime comedy ''[[8 ½ $]]'' (1999), directorial debut of Grigori Konstantinopolsky, starring [[Ivan Okhlobystin]] and [[Fyodor Bondarchuk]] was a satiric take on 1990s Russia. It told the story of a [[television advertisement]] director who becomes romantically involved with a gangster's girlfriend.<ref name="afisha"/>

[[Svetlana Baskova]] directed the low-budget independently made [[Exploitation film|exploitation]] shock-horror film ''[[The Green Elephant]]'' in 1999.<ref name="afisha"/> Baskova noted that the film was conceived as a protest against the Chechen war.<ref>{{cite web|work=Cult of Cinema|url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=mO45Pkq_XzQ|title=Svetlana Baskova in the TV program Cult of Cinema | date=23 June 2011 }}</ref> In 2022 the film has been banned in Russia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://meduza.io/news/2022/05/06/v-peterburge-sud-zapretil-film-zelenyy-slonik|title=В Петербурге суд запретил фильм "Зеленый слоник"|work=[[Meduza (website)|Meduza]]}}</ref>

=== 2000s ===
[[File:Timur Bekmambetov (6852155728).jpg|thumb|200px|[[Timur Bekmambetov]], a director of Kazakh origin, directed three of highest grossing Russian movies of the 2000s, including the famous ''[[Night Watch (2004 film)|Night Watch]]'' and ''[[Day Watch (film)|Day Watch]]''.]]

The film ''[[His Wife's Diary]]'' (2000) by [[Aleksei Uchitel]] won awards at both [[Kinotavr]] and [[Nika Award]]. The biographical film was about the last love affair of writer [[Ivan Bunin]]. Uchitel's 2005 film ''[[Dreaming of Space]]'' won the Golden George at the [[27th Moscow International Film Festival]].<ref name="Moscow2005">{{cite web|url=http://www.moscowfilmfestival.ru/miff34/eng/archives/?year=2005 |title=27th Moscow International Film Festival (2005) |access-date=13 April 2013 |work=MIFF |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130403124619/http://moscowfilmfestival.ru/miff34/eng/archives/?year=2005 |archive-date=3 April 2013}}</ref>

[[Roman Kachanov (film director)|Roman Kachanov]] directed the absurdist comedies ''[[Demobbed (2000 film)|Demobbed]]'' (2000) and ''[[Down House (film)|Down House]]'' (2001), which were both co-written with actor [[Ivan Okhlobystin]] who also starred in the films. Both are considered to be cult films in Russia.<ref name="afisha">{{cite web|url=http://mag.afisha.ru/stories/100-glavnyh-russkih-filmov/zelenyy-slonik/|title=100 главных русских фильмов: 1992—2013|work=Afisha}}</ref> [[FIPRESCI]] awarded a special mention to the film ''Demobbed'' at the 2000 [[Kinotavr]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kinoreporter.ru/a-pomnite-vy-vchera-tovarishha-generala-za-pogon-ukusili-20-faktov-o-dmb/|title="А помните, вы вчера товарища генерала за погон укусили?": 23 факта о "ДМБ"|work=Kinoreporter |date=23 February 2021 }}</ref>

''[[The Romanovs: An Imperial Family]]'' is a 2000 Russian [[historical drama]] film about the last days of [[Tsar Nicholas II]] and his family. The film premiered at the 22nd annual [[Moscow Film Festival]].

[[Karen Shakhnazarov]]'s 2001 film 
''[[Poisons or the World History of Poisoning]]'' was awarded the Grand Prix at the [[Kinotavr]] film festival in [[Sochi]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kinotavr.ru/en/history/winners/|title=Winners 1991–2005|work=[[Kinotavr]]|access-date=2017-01-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202032212/http://www.kinotavr.ru/en/history/winners/|archive-date=2017-02-02|url-status=dead}}</ref> At the [[Karlovy Vary International Film Festival]] the picture was nominated for the Crystal Globe <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kviff.com/en/programme/film/4318014-poisons-or-the-world-history-of-poisoning/|title=Poisons or the World History of Poisoning / Jady ili Vsěmirnaja istorija otravlěnij|work=[[KVIFF]]}}</ref> and was screened at the [[51st Berlin International Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vokrug.tv/product/show/yady_ili_vsemirnaya_istoriya_otravlenii/|publisher=VokrugTV|title=Яды, или Всемирная история отравлений}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://russia.tv/brand/show/brand_id/5745/|publisher=[[Russia-1]]|title=Яды, или Всемирная история отравлений. Х/ф|access-date=2023-05-28|archive-date=2020-11-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120212011/https://russia.tv/brand/show/brand_id/5745/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Another Shakhnazarov films, ''[[The Rider Named Death]]'', ''[[Vanished Empire]]'' and ''[[Ward No. 6 (film)|Ward Number 6]]'', released in 2004, 2008 and 2009 respectively.

''[[The Cuckoo (film)|The Cuckoo]]'' by [[Aleksandr Rogozhkin]] won multiple awards at the [[24th Moscow International Film Festival]]. The WWII set film starred Finnish actor [[Ville Haapasalo]] as a stranded Finnish sniper.<ref name="Moscow2002"/>

''[[House of Fools (film)|House of Fools]]'' is a 2002 Russian film by [[Andrei Konchalovsky]] about [[psychiatry|psychiatric]] patients and combatants during the [[First Chechen War]]. The film was screened in the competition at the [[59th Venice International Film Festival]] and  won [[Special Jury Prize (Venice Film Festival)|Grand Special Jury Prize]] and [[United Nations Children's Fund|UNICEF]] Award.

[[Egor Konchalovsky]] directed ''[[Antikiller]]'' (2002) starring [[Gosha Kutsenko]] as a police officer turned vigilante proved to be a success among Russian audiences.<ref name="afisha"/>

In 2002 [[Pavel Lungin]] directed the film ''[[Tycoon (2002 film)|Tycoon]]'' about a Russian oligarch. [[Vladimir Mashkov]] played the [[Boris Berezovsky (businessman)|Boris Berezovsky]] inspired lead character.

''[[Chekhov's Motifs]]'' is a 2002 Russian-Ukrainian [[comedy film]] directed by [[Kira Muratova]]. It was entered into the [[24th Moscow International Film Festival]].<ref name="Moscow2002">{{cite web|url=http://www.moscowfilmfestival.ru/miff34/eng/archives/?year=2002 |title=24th Moscow International Film Festival (2002) |access-date=31 March 2013 |work=MIFF |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130328141921/http://moscowfilmfestival.ru/miff34/eng/archives/?year=2002 |archive-date=28 March 2013 }}</ref>

2002 comedy-drama film ''[[In Motion (film)|In Motion]]'' was the directorial debut of [[Filipp Yankovsky]].

Feature film debut by [[Aleksei Alekseivich German|Aleksei German Jr.]] ''The Last Train'' (2003) won the Best Picture and International Film Critics' Awards at Thessaloniki and honorable mention for Little Golden Lion award at the [[60th Venice International Film Festival]] .<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.screendaily.com/the-last-train-poslednyi-poezd/4016335.article|work=Screen Daily|title=The Last Train (Poslednyi Poezd)|author=Dan Fainaru|date=3 December 2003}}</ref> His second film, ''[[Garpastum]]'', was screened in the competition at the [[62nd Venice International Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite news|last1= Deborah Young |title=Review: 'Garpastum'|url=https://variety.com/2005/film/reviews/garpastum-1200523391/|access-date=2 June 2016|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=September 9, 2005}}</ref> For his film ''[[Paper Soldier]]'', Aleksei German Jr. received the [[Silver Lion]] and [[Golden Osella|Golden Osella for Best Cinematography]] from the [[65th Venice International Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rbth.com/articles/2008/09/08/080908_venice.html|work=RBTH|title=Russian film wins award in Venice|date=2008-08-07}}</ref>

[[Andrey Zvyagintsev]]'s ''[[The Return (2003 film)|The Return]]'' (2003), a [[Golden Lion]] award  from the [[60th Venice International Film Festival]] recipient and [[Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Golden Globe Best Foreign Language Film]] and [[César Award for Best Foreign Film]] nominie, shows two brothers' test of life when their father suddenly returns that reaches a deep almost-mystic pitch. ''[[Russian Ark]]'' (2003) by [[Alexander Sokurov]], was filmed in a single 96-minute shot in the Russian [[Hermitage Museum]] is a dream-like narration that tells about classic Russian culture sailing in the Ark. It was screened at the [[2002 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/3157774/year/2002.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Russian Ark |access-date=25 October 2009|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref>

''[[The Tuner]]'' is a 2004 [[Ukraine]]/[[Russia]] mix film of art house grotesque and a sting comedy. At the heart of [[Kira Muratova]]’s film is her characteristic and enduring love of predation—predation for its own sake. The film offers a complex assessment of the human subject, civilization, and the creative act. It premiered out of competition at the [[61st Venice International Film Festival]]

''[[Night Watch (2004 film)|Night Watch]]'' (2004) by [[Timur Bekmambetov]] was one of the first [[Blockbuster (entertainment)|blockbusters]] made after the collapse of the Soviet film industry. The supernatural thriller starred [[Konstantin Khabensky]] and was based on the [[Night Watch (Lukyanenko novel)|eponymous book]] by [[Sergei Lukyanenko]]. It was followed by the sequel ''[[Day Watch (film)|Day Watch]]'' (2006), that nominated on  [[Saturn Award for Best International Film]].

Russian actress [[Renata Litvinova]] debuted as director in 2004 with the film ''[[Goddess: How I fell in Love]]''.

''[[The Italian (2005 film)|The Italian]]'' is a 2005 Russian [[drama film]] directed by [[Andrei Kravchuk]] inspired by a true story, focuses on a young boy's determined search for his Mother. The film won the Grand Prix of the Deutsches Kinderhilfswerk from the International Jury at the [[55th Berlin International Film Festival]], and a Special Mention from their Children's Jury.<ref>{{citation |title=Italianetz |url=https://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/2005/02_programm_2005/02_Filmdatenblatt_2005_20051745.php#tab=boulevard |access-date=17 July 2017 |work=Berlinale Film Archive |date=14 February 2005 }}</ref>

''[[First on the Moon]]'' by [[Aleksei Fedorchenko]] is a 2005 Russian [[mockumentary]] [[science fiction film]] about a fictional 1930s Soviet landing on the [[Moon]] and was directorial debut of Fedorchenko. It was screened at [[62nd Venice International Film Festival]] in Horrizons section and won Best Film Award.

''[[The 9th Company]]'' is a 2005 Russian [[war film]] directed by [[Fedor Bondarchuk]] and set during the [[Soviet–Afghan War]]. The film is loosely based on a real-life battle that took place at [[Battle for Hill 3234|Elevation 3234]] in early 1988, during [[Operation Magistral]], the last large-scale [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] military operation in Afghanistan.
 
The serialised novels by [[Boris Akunin]] set in [[Russian Revolution|pre-Revolutionary Russia]] evolve around fictional Erast Fandorin adventures in three popular movies: ''[[Azazel (film)|The Azazel]]'' (2002) by [[Aleksandr Adabashyan]], ''[[The Turkish Gambit (film)|The Turkish Gambit]]'' (2005) by [[Dzhanik Fayziev]] and ''[[The State Counsellor (film)|The State Counsellor]]'' (2005) by [[Filipp Yankovsky]].

The film ''[[977 (film)|977]]'' by [[Nikolay Khomeriki]] was screened in the [[Un Certain Regard]] section at the [[2006 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref name="cannes-2006.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4359774/year/2006.html |title=Festival de Cannes: 977 |access-date=14 December 2009|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref> Three years later his film ''[[Tale in the Darkness]]'' competed in the same section at the [[2009 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref name="cannes-2009.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/10905046/year/2009.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Tale in the Darkness |access-date=17 May 2009|work=festival-cannes.com}}</ref>

''[[Euphoria (2006 film)|Euphoria]]'' is a 2006 Russian [[drama film|drama]] [[romance film]] directed by dramatist and director [[Ivan Vyrypaev]]. The film was nominated on [[Golden Lion]] at [[63rd Venice International Film Festival]] and won Little Golden Lion.

Life of the Orthodox Monastery and their Christian miracles are described in the film ''[[The Island (2006 film)|The Island]]'' (2006) by [[Pavel Lungin]]. The film was screened out of the competition at the [[63rd Venice International Film Festival]] and received the [[Golden Eagle Award (Russia)|Golden Eagle]] and [[Nika Award|Nika]] awards.

[[Konstantin Lopushansky]] directed the science-fiction film ''[[The Ugly Swans (film)|The Ugly Swans]]'' in 2006, based on the 1967 [[The Ugly Swans|novel]] by [[Arkady and Boris Strugatsky]]. The film received the Best Score award at [[Kinotavr]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tretyakovgallery.ru/cinema/o/gadkie-lebedi-/|work=Tretyakov Gallery|title=Ugly Swans}}</ref>

Psychological drama ''[[The Banishment]]'' by [[Andrey Zvyagintsev]] and war drama ''[[Alexandra (2007 film)|Alexandra]]'' by [[Alexander Sokurov]] was selected in competition section at the [[2007 Cannes Film Festival]] where ''The Banishment'' won the [[Best Actor Award (Cannes Film Festival)|Best Actor Award]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4427494/year/2007.html |title=Festival de Cannes: The Banishment |access-date=18 December 2009 |work=festival-cannes.com |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121012053424/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/4427494/year/2007.html |url-status=live |archive-date = 12 October 2012}}</ref>

''[[12 (2007 film)|12]]'' is a Russian-language remake of ''[[12 Angry Men (1957 film)|12 Angry Men]]'' directed by [[Nikita Mikhalkov]], was screened in the competition at the [[64th Venice International Film Festival]] there won the Special Lion for Mikhalkov and received an [[Academy Award]] nomination for [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]].<ref name="venice">{{cite web|url=http://www.labiennale.org/en/news/cinema/en/78166.html |title=Official Awards at the 64th Venice Film Festival |access-date=2007-12-12 |publisher=www.labiennale.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080417133948/http://www.labiennale.org/en/news/cinema/en/78166.html |archive-date=2008-04-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Kazakh-Russian co-production epic film ''[[Mongol (film)|Mongol]]'' directed by [[Sergey Bodrov]] also received an [[Academy Award]] nomination for [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]].<ref>{{cite press release | title = 80th Academy Awards Nominations Announced | publisher = [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] | date = 2008-01-22 | url = http://www.oscars.org/press/pressreleases/2008/08.01.22.html | access-date = 2008-01-22}}</ref>

''[[Cargo 200 (film)|Cargo 200]]'' is a Russian [[neo-noir]] [[Thriller (genre)|thriller]] directed by [[Aleksei Balabanov]] 
won Best Director Award on 
[[Gijón International Film Festival]].

One of Russia's all-time biggest box-office hits was [[Timur Bekmambetov]]'s romantic-comedy ''[[The Irony of Fate 2]]'', directed in 2007 as a sequel to [[The Irony of Fate|the 1976 film]]. 2008 musical film ''[[Stilyagi (film)|Hipsters]]'',  directed by Valery Todorovsky about the youth lifestyle in the 1950s Soviet Union was a success at the box office. It received the [[Golden Eagle Award (Russia)|Golden Eagle]] and [[Nika Award|Nika]] awards for best picture.

[[Valeriya Gai Germanika]] received the "Special Mention" of the jury of the Camera d'Or competition at the [[2008 Cannes Film Festival]] for her feature debut ''[[Everybody Dies but Me]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/84416/|work=Cineuropa|title=Cantet wins Palme d'Or and Sorrentino, Garrone and Dardenne brothers scoop awards|author=Fabien Lemercier|date=2008-05-25}}</ref><ref name="afisha"/>

At the [[2008 Sundance Film Festival]] [[Anna Melikian]] won the award for best Dramatic Directing for her film ''[[Mermaid (2007 film)|Mermaid]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/498113/2008-sundance-film-festival-award-winners/|work=SlashFilm|title=2008 Sundance Film Festival Award Winners|date=2008}}</ref>

In 2008 was released ''[[Admiral (2008 film)|Admiral]]'', [[biopic]]  about [[Alexander Kolchak]], a [[vice admiral]] in the [[Imperial Russian Navy]] and leader of the [[Anti-communism|anti-communist]] [[White movement]] during the [[Russian Civil War]] directed by [[Andrei Kravchuk]]. Later Kravchuk directed two another films based on  the historic events: ''[[Viking (2016 film)|Viking]]'' and ''[[Union of Salvation (film)|Union of Salvation]]'', released in 2016 and 2019 respectively.

Sci-fi picture ''[[Dark Planet (Russian film)|Dark Planet]]'' (2008–2009) based on the book by [[Arkady and Boris Strugatsky]], directed by [[Fyodor Bondarchuk]], was one of the most expensive Russian films of the 2000s, with its budget of $36.6 million.

''[[Room and a Half]]'' is a 2009 Russian biographical film directed by [[Andrei Khrzhanovsky]] about life of Russian poet [[Joseph Brodsky]]. This film received the Best Film award in the East of the West section at the [[Karlovy Vary International Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kviff.com/img/history/2009/final-press-release-2009.pdf|publisher=[[Karlovy Vary International Film Festival]]|title=Final Press Release (July 11th, 2009) }}</ref>

In 2009 ''[[Tambourine, Drum]]'' by Aleksey Mizgirev won [[Special Jury Prize (Locarno International Film Festival)|Special Jury Prize]], [[Best Direction Award (Locarno International Film Festival)|Best Direction Prize]] and the special prize from the youth jury at 2009 [[Locarno International Film Festival|Locarno Film Festival]].

=== 2010s ===
[[File:Pushkinsky Cinema 00.jpg|thumb|The [[Rossiya Theatre]] hosts the [[Moscow International Film Festival]].]]
[[File:Андрей Звягинцев 2017.jpg|thumb|[[Andrei Zvyagintsev]]'s [[art house]] dramas received many awards, including an [[Academy Award]] nominations in 2015 and 2018.]]

In 2014 censorship of cinematic works was officially introduced with a new and stricter revision of the "screening certificate" ({{langx|ru|прокатное удостоверение|prokatnoye udostovereniye}}) act, without which public film screenings are not allowed and are punishable by law. Curse words in films were banned.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/38425|work=Kremlin|title=Федеральный закон от 05.05.2014 г. № 101-ФЗ}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cinemaplex.ru/2014/05/07/ne-v-mate-delo.html|work=Cinemaplex|title=НЕ В МАТЕ ДЕЛО: ЗАКОН О ЗАПРЕТЕ НЕЦЕНЗУРНОЙ ЛЕКСИКИ РЕГЛАМЕНТИРУЕТ… РАБОТУ ПО ПРОКАТНОМУ УДОСТОВЕРЕНИЮ|date=7 May 2014 |trans-title=Does not have to do with curse words: Law concerning ban of curse words regulates... work concerning the screening certificate}}</ref> The concept of a "screening certificate" first appeared in Russian laws in 1993, when [[Viktor Chernomyrdin]] signed the decree "On the registration of films and videos", the main purpose of which was to combat the spread of pirated content.  For a decade and a half, the document was more or less a formality.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://legalacts.ru/doc/postanovlenie-pravitelstva-rf-ot-17111994-n-1264/|work=Legal Acts|title=Постановление Правительства РФ от 17.11.1994 N 1264 (ред. от 10.03.2009) "Об утверждении Правил по киновидеообслуживанию населения"}}</ref>

In 2010 the comedy anthology film ''[[Yolki]]'' produced by [[Timur Bekmambetov]] was released. It spawned seven sequels, one prequel and one spin-off. ''[[How I Ended This Summer]]'' by [[Alexei Popogrebski]], a film shot in remote [[Chukotka Autonomous Okrug|Chukotka]], won [[Silver Bear for Best Actor]] in [[60th Berlin International Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/2010/03_preistr_ger_2010/03_Preistraeger_2010.html|title=Berlinale. Archive. Prize winners 2010}}</ref> The same year arthouse film ''[[Silent Souls]]'' by [[Aleksey Fedorchenko]] won the [[Golden Osella|Golden Osella for Best Cinematography]] and a [[FIPRESCI]] Award at the [[67th Venice Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.labiennale.org/en/cinema/archive/67th-festival/awards/ |title=La Biennale di Venezia – Official Awards of the 67th Venice Film Festival |publisher=Labiennale.org |access-date=2013-09-12}}</ref>

In 2010 ''[[Jolly Fellows (2009 film)|Jolly Fellows]]'' directed by Felix Mikhailov was screened at the [[60th Berlin International Film Festival]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/jolly-fellows-open-berlin-panorama-19838|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|title='Jolly Fellows' to open Berlin Panorama|author=Scott Roxborough|date=22 January 2010}}</ref> and also was the first Russian picture to be chosen as the opening film of the Panorama section at the festival.<ref name="Коммерсантъ">{{cite news|url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/1319678|title=Веселая разлука|newspaper=[[Kommersant]]|author=Andrei Plakhov|date=12 February 2010|language=ru}}</ref>

''[[Fortress of War]] '' is a 2010 Russian-Belarusian war film directed by [[Alexander Kott]] recounting the June 1941 [[defense of Brest Fortress]] against invading [[Wehrmacht]] forces in the opening stages of [[Operation Barbarossa]], [[Nazi Germany]]'s invasion of the [[Soviet Union]] during [[World War II]]. The film received universal acclaim from Russian critics and auditory.

''[[The Edge (2010 film)|The Edge]]'' by [[Alexei Uchitel]] was nominated for the 2010 [[Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film]].

[[Yury Bykov]] debuted as a director with the film ''[[To Live (2010 film)|To Live]]'' in 2010. His film ''[[The Major (film)|The Major]]'' screened at the [[2013 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/article/cannes-reveals-the-international-critics-week-lineup-aint-them-bodies-saints-makes-the-cut |title=Cannes Reveals International Critics' Week Lineup; 'Ain't Them Bodies Saints' Makes the Cut |work=Indiewire |date=22 April 2013 |access-date=23 May 2013}}</ref> His film ''[[The Fool (2014 film)|The Fool]]'' won the [[Best Actor Award (Locarno International Film Festival)|Best Actor Award]] at the 2014 [[Locarno International Film Festival|Locarno Film Festival]].<ref name="Locarno-prizes">{{cite web |url=http://www.pardolive.ch/dms/2014/pdfs/Palmares67/Palmarès_ENG.pdf |access-date=2015-01-05 |title=Official Awards |publisher=Festival del Film Locarno}}</ref> His film ''[[The Factory (2018 film)|The Factory]] '' screened at the [[2018 Toronto International Film Festival]].<ref name="TIFF">{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2018/08/tiff-2018-additional-titles-mid90s-boy-erased-hold-the-dark-1201993789/ |title=TIFF Adds More High-Profile Titles, Including Jonah Hill's 'Mid90s,' 'Boy Erased,' 'Hold the Dark,' and Many More |work=IndieWire |date=14 August 2018 |access-date=24 August 2018}}</ref>

Drama films ''[[Elena (2011 film)|Elena]]'' by [[Andrey Zvyagintsev]] and ''[[The Hunter (2011 Russian film)|The Hunter]] '' by Baku Bakuradze was selected in the [[Un Certain Regard]] section at the [[2011 Cannes Film Festival]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/article/58041.html |title=Festival de Cannes: Official Selection |access-date=16 April 2011 |work=Cannes |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110515065818/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/article/58041.html |archive-date=15 May 2011}}</ref> where ''Elena'' won the Special Jury Prize.<ref>{{cite news|last=Leffler|first=Rebecca|date=21 May 2011|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/regard-announces-top-prizes-cannes-190886|title=Un Certain Regard Announces Top Prizes (Cannes 2011)|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=21 May 2011}}</ref>

''[[Faust (2011 film)|Faust]]'', the last part of tetralogy by [[Aleksandr Sokurov]], won the [[Golden Lion]] at the [[68th Venice International Film Festival]] .<ref>{{Cite news|last=Vivarelli|first=Nick|date=2011-09-10|url=https://variety.com/2011/film/markets-festivals/faust-wins-golden-lion-at-venice-1118042572/|title='Faust' wins Golden Lion at Venice|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=2011-09-10}}</ref> His follow-up film ''[[Francofonia]]'' received the Mimmo Rotella Award at the [[72nd Venice International Film Festival]] .<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2015/film/news/venice-winner-francofonia-bought-by-music-box-for-u-s-1201601487/|work=Variety|title=Venice Winner 'Francofonia' Bought by Music Box for U.S.|author=Dave McNary|date=24 September 2015 }}</ref>

2011 romantic comedy ''[[Vykrutasy|Lucky Trouble]]'' directed by [[Levan Gabriadze]] and produced by [[Timur Bekmambetov]], starred Hollywood actress [[Milla Jovovich]] who played the female lead opposite [[Konstantin Khabensky]].

''[[Generation P (film)|Generation P]]'' (2011) by [[Victor Ginzburg (director)|Victor Ginzburg]] was an independently produced satiric comedy about advertisement business set in the 1990s. The film was based on [[Victor Pelevin]]'s 1999 [[Generation "П"|novel of the same name]]. The film won Special Jury Mention at the 2011 [[Karlovy Vary International Film Festival]].

''[[Betrayal (2012 film)|Betrayal]]'' by [[Kirill Serebrennikov]] was selected in competition on [[69th Venice International Film Festival]].<ref name="labiennale">{{cite web |url=http://www.labiennale.org/en/cinema/festival/lineup/off-sel/venezia69/ |title=Venezia 69 |access-date=4 August 2012 |work=labiennale |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120728223053/http://www.labiennale.org/en/cinema/festival/lineup/off-sel/venezia69 |archive-date=28 July 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

''[[White Tiger (2012 film)|White Tiger]]'' is a 2012 Russian [[war film]], directed by [[Karen Shakhnazarov]] and co-written with [[Aleksandr Borodyansky]] based on the novel ''Tankist, ili "Belyy tigr"'' (''The Tankman'', or ''The White Tiger'') by Russian novelist Ilya Boyashov. The film is about a badly wounded Soviet tank commander on the [[Eastern Front (World War II)|Eastern Front]] of [[World War II]] who becomes obsessed with tracking down and destroying a mysterious, invincible Nazi tank, which the Soviet troops call the "White Tiger". The Soviets design a new, more powerful [[T-34]] tank and assign the tank commander the job of destroying the White Tiger.

Aleksey Adrianov directed the high-budget [[Boris Akunin]] adaptation ''[[Spy (2012 Russian film)|Spy]]'' in 2012.

A Russian filmmaker who continued to make a name for himself in [[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]] was [[Timur Bekmambetov]], a producer and director of [[Blockbuster (entertainment)|blockbuster films]]. In the United States he directed ''[[Wanted (2008 film)|Wanted]]'' (2008), ''[[Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter]]'' (2012) and ''[[Ben-Hur (2016 film)|Ben-Hur]]'' (2016).

Starting from 2003 Russia's animation industry began to manufacture films which are profitable domestically and abroad. Some of the pictures included [[Voronezh Animation Studio]] projects: ''[[The Snow Queen (2012 film)|The Snow Queen 1]]'', ''[[The Snow Queen 2: The Snow King|2]]'', ''[[The Snow Queen 3: Fire and Ice|3]]'', ''[[The Snow Queen: Mirrorlands|4]]'', ''[[Sheep and Wolves|Sheep and Wolves 1]]'', ''[[Sheep and Wolves: Pig Deal|2]]'', ''[[Secret Magic Control Agency]]''; [[Melnitsa Animation Studio]] projects: ''[[Little Longnose]]'', ''[[The Three Bogatyrs]]'' series (including ''[[Dobrynya Nikitich and Zmey Gorynych]]'' and ''[[Horse Julius and Big Horse Racing]]''), ''[[Luntik]]'', ''[[The Tale of Soldier Fedot, The Daring Fellow]]'', ''[[Ivan Tsarevich and the Gray Wolf (film)|Ivan Tsarevich and the Gray Wolf 1]]'', ''[[Ivan Tsarevich and the Gray Wolf 2|2]]'', ''[[Ivan Tsarevich and the Gray Wolf 3|3]]'', ''[[Fantastic Journey to OZ]]''; projects of other studios: ''[[Prince Vladimir (film)|Prince Vladimir]]'', ''[[Kikoriki]]'', ''[[Space Dogs]]'' and ''[[Space Dogs: Return to Earth]]'', ''[[Masha and the Bear]]'', ''[[A Warrior's Tail]]'', ''[[Hoffmaniada]]''.

War epic ''[[Stalingrad (2013 film)|Stalingrad]]'' directed by [[Fyodor Bondarchuk]] in 2013 set new box-office records in Russia and abroad. After ''Stalingrad's'' success at the box-office, increasingly more films started to be made in Russia about WWII. Other WWII films that were made in Russia included ''[[The Dawns Here Are Quiet (2015 film)|The Dawns Here Are Quiet]]'' (2015), ''[[Battle for Sevastopol]]'' (2015) ''[[Panfilov's 28 Men]]'' (2016), ''[[Sobibor (film)|Sobibor]]'' (2018), ''[[Tankers (film)|Tankers]]'' (2018), ''[[T-34 (film)|T-34]]'' (2019), ''[[Saving Leningrad]]'' (2019), ''[[The Last Frontier (2020 film)|The Last Frontier]]'' (2020), ''[[AK-47 (2020 film)|AK-47]]'' (2020), ''[[A Siege Diary]]'' (2020), ''[[V2. Escape from Hell]]'' (2021), ''[[The Pilot. A Battle for Survival]]'' (2021), ''[[The Red Ghost]]'' (2021) and ''[[First Oscar]]'' (2022).

2013 comedy ''[[Kiss Them All!]]''  by [[Zhora Kryzhovnikov]], produced by [[Timur Bekmambetov]], is the most profitable domestic film in the history of Russian box office, having managed to earn more than 27.3 million dollars on a comparatively modest budget of $1.5 million.<ref name="kb">{{cite web|url=https://www.kinobusiness.com/news/camye-pribylnye-i-ubytochnye-otechestvennye-filmy-v-kinoprokate-rossii-2013-goda/|title=Кинобизнес / Cамые прибыльные и убыточные отечественные фильмы в кинопрокате России 2013 года|publisher=Кинобизнес|language=ru|access-date=2020-03-31}}</ref><ref name="art">{{Cite web|url=http://old.kinoart.ru/archive/2014/03/zakupki-ru-o-mekhanizmakh-gospodderzhki-kinematografii|title=Zakupki.ru. О механизмах господдержки кинематографии|publisher=Искусство кино|language=ru|access-date=2020-03-31}}</ref> The film was followed by ''[[:ru:Горько! 2|Kiss Them All! 2]]'', which became the most profitable film of 2014 in Russia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cinemaplex.ru/2015/03/26/sbornik-kinostatistica.html|title=Количество успешных российских фильмов выросло|author=Михаил Филберт|date=2015-03-26|publisher=Cinemaplex}}</ref>

''[[Hard to Be a God (2013 film)|Hard to Be a God]]'' is a 2013 Russian [[Epic film|epic]] [[Medieval film|medieval]] [[science fiction film]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Close-Up on "Hard to Be a God" and the Medieval in European Cinema |url=https://mubi.com/notebook/posts/close-up-on-hard-to-be-a-god-and-the-medieval-in-european-cinema |access-date=2022-06-29 |website=MUBI |date=4 December 2015 |language=en}}</ref> directed by [[Aleksei Yuryevich German|Aleksei German]] who co-wrote the screenplay with Svetlana Karmalita. It was his last film and it is based on the 1964 novel [[Hard to Be a God|of the same name]] by [[Arkady and Boris Strugatsky]]. ''Hard to Be a God'' was listed by numerous critics' and publications' as one of the top films of 2015 and also been considered one of the top films of the 2010s. 

''[[Chagall — Malevich]]'' is a 2014 Russian [[biographical film|biographical]] [[Drama (film and television)|drama film]] directed by [[Alexander Mitta]] about the [[Vitebsk]] period in the life of the artist [[Marc Chagall]] and his relationship with fellow artist [[Kazimir Malevich]]. It also showed at the 2014 [[Busan International Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.biff.kr/eng/html/archive/arc_history_2_view.asp?pyear=2014&s1=&page=13&m_idx=12592|title=Chagall-Malevich|work=BIFF|access-date=9 February 2022}}</ref>

Film by [[Alexander Veledinsky]], ''[[The Geographer Drank His Globe Away]]'', based on the novel of the same name by [[Alexei Viktorovich Ivanov|Alexei Ivanov]], was awarded the main prize at [[Kinotavr]] 2013.<ref name="afisha"/>

In 2014, [[Andrey Zvyagintsev]]'s ''[[Leviathan (2014 film)|Leviathan]]'' was entered in the [[2014 Cannes Film Festival]], where it won [[Best Screenplay Award (Cannes Film Festival)|Best Screenplay Award]]<ref name="2014Winners">{{cite web|url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/awardCompetition.html |title=Awards 2014 : Competition |work=Cannes Film Festival |access-date=25 May 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023133531/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/awardCompetition.html |archive-date=23 October 2013 }}</ref> and was nominated on four [[European Film Awards]], including Best Film,  [[BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language]] and [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film]] at the [[87th Academy Awards]]. It won the [[72nd Golden Globe Awards|Golden Globe]] for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film|Best Foreign Language Film]].<ref name="dickclark.com">[http://www.dickclark.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/72nd-Annual-Golden-Globes-Nominations.pdf 72ND ANNUAL GOLDEN GLOBE® AWARDS NOMINEES ANNOUNCED]. dickclark.com. Retrieved 11 December 2014</ref> After the film got leaked online and was downloaded by 1.5 million users, domestic distributors decided to make a wide release of the controversial film which was negatively viewed by the Russian authorities due to its gloomy and critical view of Russia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2015/02/04/zvyagintsevs-leviathan-picks-up-6-awards-at-russian-film-ceremony-a43548|work=Moscow Times|title=Zvyagintsev's 'Leviathan' Picks Up 6 Awards at Russian Film Ceremony|date=4 February 2015}}</ref>

''[[Sunstroke (2014 film)|Sunstroke]]'' is a 2014 Russian [[drama film]] directed, produced and written by [[Nikita Mikhalkov]], starring Martinsh Kalita and Viktoriya Solovyova. It is set after the collapse of the [[Russian Empire]] during the [[Red Terror]] in 1920, with flashbacks to 1907, and is loosely based on the story "Sunstroke" and the book ''[[Cursed Days]]'' by [[Nobel Prize winner for literature|Nobel Prize-winning]] [[Russian writer]] [[Ivan Bunin]].

''[[Two Women (2014 film)|Two Women]]'' is a 2014 Russian drama film directed by [[Vera Glagoleva]], starring [[Ralph Fiennes]] and [[Sylvie Testud]]. It is based on [[Ivan Turgenev]]'s 1872 play ''[[A Month in the Country (play)|A Month in the Country]]'' (originally written as ''Two Women'' in 1855). The film won the Best Feature Film award at the [[3rd Hanoi International Film Festival]].

''[[Under the Sun (2015 film)|Under the Sun]] '' is a 2015 Russian [[documentary film]] directed by [[Vitaly Mansky]] won  Best Director Award at the [[Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival]]. The film follows a year in the life of a family in [[Pyongyang]], North Korea as their daughter Zin-mi prepares to join the [[Korean Children's Union]] on the [[Day of the Shining Star]] ([[Kim Jong-il]]'s birthday).<ref name=VarietyReview>{{cite web |last=Harvey |first=Dennis |title=Film Review: 'Under the Sun'|url=https://variety.com/2016/film/reviews/under-the-sun-review-1201767261/|website=Variety|access-date=6 October 2016|date=20 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Kohn|first1=Eric|title=Under the Sun Review: Documentary Goes Inside North Korea|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2016/07/under-the-sun-review-documentary-north-korea-1201703155/|website=IndieWire|date=6 July 2016 |access-date=6 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title='Under The Sun' ('V lutsah solntsa'): Film Review|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/under-sun-v-lutsah-solntsa-842412|website=The Hollywood Reporter|date=20 November 2015 |access-date=6 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Gray |first=Carmen |title=Russian film exposes the workings of North Korea's propaganda machine |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/dec/02/north-korea-under-the-sun-vitaly-mansky-film |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=6 October 2016|date=2 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|title=Under the Sun|url=https://www.newyorker.com/goings-on-about-town/movies/under-the-sun-2 |magazine=The New Yorker |access-date=6 October 2016}}</ref> North Korea permitted only Mansky, cinematographer Alexandra Ivanova, and a sound assistant to visit the country. North Korean authorities objected to the film's screening after discovering that the film crew had smuggled unapproved footage.

''[[Under Electric Clouds]]'' by [[Aleksei Alekseivich German|Aleksei German]] won the Silver Bear for Outstanding Artistic Contribution for Cinematography at the [[65th Berlin International Film Festival]].<ref name="BerlinAwards">{{cite web |url=https://www.berlinale.de/en/das_festival/preise_und_juries/preise_internationale_jury/index.html |title=Prizes of the International Jury |access-date=14 February 2015 | publisher=Berlinale}}</ref> His follow-up film ''[[Dovlatov (film)|Dovlatov]]'' (2018) about writer [[Sergei Dovlatov]], was awarded a Silver Bear for Outstanding Artistic Contribution for costume and production design [[68th Berlin International Film Festival]] .<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.berlinale.de/en/archiv/jahresarchive/2018/03_preistrger_2018/03_preistraeger_2018.html|work=Berlinale|title=Archiv. Prize winners 2018}}</ref>

''[[Battalion (2015 film)|Battalion]]'' is a 2015 Russian war film directed by [[Dmitry Meskhiev]] that relates the story of the [[Women's Battalion|First Battalion of Death]], a women-only Russian combat unit that fought in the First World War. Actress [[Mariya Aronova]] plays the role of real-life heroine [[Maria Bochkareva]]. ''Battalion'' was the biggest winner at the 2015 [[Golden Eagle Award (Russia)|Golden Eagle Awards]], winning four awards out of nine nominations.

He previously received the [[Silver Lion]] for ''[[The Postman's White Nights]]'' at the [[71st Venice International Film Festival]].

''[[Sin (2019 film)|Sin]]'' is a Russian-Italian biographical drama film about the life of the famous sculptor and painter of the Renaissance, [[Michelangelo Buonarroti]] of Florence, in the early 16th century, written and directed by [[Andrei Konchalovsky]], released in October 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vokrug.tv/article/show/andrei_konchalovskii_snimet_film_dorogie_tovarishchi_s_yuliei_vysotskoi_v_glavnoi_roli_i_byudzhetom_v_150_millionov_rublei_67467/|title=Андрей Кончаловский снимет фильм "Дорогие товарищи" с Юлией Высоцкой в главной роли и бюджетом в 150 миллионов рублей|website=Вокруг.ТВ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tvkinoradio.ru/article/article13793-camera-action-chto-proishodit-v-rossijskom-kino|title=Camera! ''[[Why Don't You Just Die!]]'' is a 2018 Russian [[dark comedy]] [[thriller film]] directed by Kirill Sokolov and starring [[Aleksandr Kuznetsov (actor)|Aleksandr Kuznetsov]], Vitaly Khaev, [[Evgeniya Kregzhde]] and [[Yelena Shevchenko (actress)|Yelena Shevchenko]].

2019 comedy film ''[[Serf (film)|Serf]]'' directed by [[Klim Shipenko]] and starring [[Miloš Biković]] set new domestic box-office records. It grossed $42.4 million against a budget of $2.6 million.<ref>[https://ekinobilet.fond-kino.ru/films/detail/111021719/ Холоп] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115162716/http://ekinobilet.fond-kino.ru/films/detail/111021719/ |date=2020-01-15 }}. fond-kino.ru</ref><ref name="BOM">{{cite web |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt11418452/?ref_=bo_se_r_1 |title=The Serf (2019) |website=[[Box Office Mojo]] |access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref> The same year Shipenko directed the psychological thriller ''[[Text (film)|Text]]'' starring [[Alexander Petrov (actor)|Alexander Petrov]], which was also a success at the box-office and received a [[Nika Award|Nika]] and multiple [[Golden Eagle Award (Russia)|Golden Eagle]] awards.<ref>[https://www.interfax.ru/culture/763193 «Текст» и «Глубже» отмечены наградами «Ника» за лучший сценарий] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209202844/https://www.interfax.ru/culture/763193 |date=2021-12-09 }}. ''[[Interfax]]''</ref>

In the following years many Russian films have gotten wide releases in China,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.filmpro.ru/materials/51178|publisher=filmpro|title=Россия и Китай: делаем кино вместе|language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/russias-stalingrad-storms-chinese-box-652842|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|title=Russia's 'Stalingrad' Storms Chinese Box Office|author=Nick Holdsworth|date=4 November 2013 }}</ref> and there has been an increased number of planned Russo-Chinese co-productions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://minsvyaz.ru/ru/events/34116/|publisher=[[Ministry of Telecom and Mass Communications of the Russian Federation]]|title=Россия и Китай договорились о ста совместных проектах в медиасфере }}</ref> A few of the films produced by Russia and China are ''[[Viy (2014 film)|Viy]]'', ''[[Viy 2: Journey to China]]'' starring [[Jackie Chan]] and [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2016/film/global/arnold-schwarzenegger-jackie-chan-movie-viy-2-1201906980/|publisher=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|author=Leo Barraclough|title=Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jackie Chan Join Russian-Chinese Movie 'Viy-2'|date=2 November 2016 }}</ref> ''[[The Snow Queen 3: Fire and Ice]]''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/2015/film/asia/russian-and-chinese-companies-to-co-produce-snow-queen-sequel-1201557792/|publisher=Variety|author=Patrick Frater|title=Russian and Chinese Companies to Co-Produce 'Snow Queen' Sequel|date=6 August 2015 }}</ref> and ''Quackerz''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/russian-animated-film-quackerz-3d-796902|work=The Hollywood Reporter|title=Russian Animated Film 'Quackerz 3D' Gets Investment From China|author=Vladimir Kozlov|date=19 May 2015 }}</ref>

===2020s===
''[[Dau (film)|Dau]]'', the first film of the controversial [[DAU (project)|DAU project]] by director [[Ilya Khrzhanovsky]], which was initially conceived as a biopic of Soviet scientist [[Lev Landau]], premiered in 2019 in Paris. ''[[DAU. Natasha]]'' and ''[[DAU. Degeneration]]'' premiered at the [[70th Berlin International Film Festival]] there first won the Silver Bear for an Outstanding Artistic Contribution for Cinematography.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2020/film/news/berlin-film-festival-2020-award-winners-1203519894/ | title=Berlin Film Festival 2020: There Is No Evil Wins Golden Bear |work=Variety | date=29 February 2020 |access-date=1 March 2020}}</ref> The rest of the films were released on VOD through the official DAU website in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2020/apr/30/dau-degeneration-review-ilya-khrzhanovsky-russia|work=The Guardian|title=DAU. Degeneration review – shocking, six-hour satire of Soviet science|author=Peter Bradshaw|date=30 April 2020 }}</ref>

War drama ''[[Persian Lessons]]'' by [[Vadim Perelman]] premiered at the [[70th Berlin International Film Festival]] .<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2020/film/reviews/persian-lessons-review-1203511856/ |title='Persian Lessons': Film Review |last=Debruge |first=Peter |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]  |date=22 February 2020 |access-date=10 February 2021}}</ref>

In 2020 ''[[:ru:Конференция (фильм)|Conference]]'' directed by [[Ivan Tverdovskiy]] and ''[[The Whaler Boy]]'' directed by [[:ru:Филипп Юрьевич Юрьев|Philipp Yuryev]] was screened at the [[Giornate degli Autori]] section at the [[77th Venice International Film Festival]], where last won Best Film Award of this section.<ref name="медуза">{{Cite web |url=https://meduza.io/feature/2020/09/16/kitoboy-podrostok-s-chukotki-reshaet-pereplyt-beringov-proliv-chtoby-uvidet-svoyu-lyubov-v-detroyte |title=«Китобой»: подросток с Чукотки решает переплыть Берингов пролив, чтобы увидеть свою любовь в Детройте. At the [[77th Venice International Film Festival]], ''[[Dear Comrades!]]'' directed by [[Andrei Konchalovsky]] telling the story of the [[Novocherkassk massacre]], won the [[Special Jury Prize (Venice Film Festival)|Special Jury Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2020/09/venice-film-festival-2020-winners-list-1234585982/ |title=Venice Film Festival 2020 Winners: ''Nomadland'' Takes Golden Lion, Vanessa Kirby Is Best Actress |work=IndieWire |date=12 September 2020 |access-date=12 September 2020}}</ref> The film also received a nomination for [[BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language]].

''[[Sputnik (film)|Sputnik]]'' is a 2020 Russian [[Science fiction film|science-fiction]] [[horror film]] directed by Egor Abramenko in his feature [[directorial debut]].<ref name=lattanzio>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2020/07/sputnik-trailer-ifc-midnight-1234575390/|title='Sputnik' Trailer: A Cosmonaut Brings an E.T. Invasion Back to Earth in Gory 'Alien' Homage|last=Lattanzio|first=Ryan|date=21 July 2020|website=[[IndieWire]]|language=en|access-date=22 July 2020}}</ref> It stars [[Oksana Akinshina]] as a young doctor who is recruited by the Soviet military to assess a [[cosmonaut]] who survived a mysterious space accident and returned to Earth with a dangerous organism living inside him.<ref name=lattanzio /> Alongside Akinshina, the film's cast includes [[Pyotr Fyodorov]] and [[Fyodor Bondarchuk]]. The film was nominated on [[Saturn Award for Best International Film]].<ref>{{cite web | date=March 4, 2021 | last=Hipes | first=Patrick | title=Saturn Awards Nominations: 'Star Wars: Rise Of Skywalker', 'Tenet', 'Walking Dead', 'Outlander' Lead List | website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] | url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/saturn-awards-nominations-2021-nominees-list-1234706492/ | access-date=March 5, 2021}}</ref>

Historic romance film ''[[The Silver Skates (film)|The Silver Skates]]'', by [[Michael Lockshin (film director)|Michael Lockshin]] in his directorial debut, was chosen as the opening film of the 42nd [[Moscow International Film Festival]], where it premiered on October 1, 2020. The rights to the film were acquired by [[Netflix]] on June 16, 2021. ''The Silver Skates'' is the first Russian film to be released on the platform in the Netflix Originals category.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://freemmorpg.top/silver-skates-will-be-the-first-russian-film-in-the-netflix-originals-lineup/ |title=''The Silver Skates'' will be the first Russian film in the Netflix Originals lineup |last=Morg|first=M. |date=March 27, 2021 |access-date=May 8, 2021 |website=FREEMMORPG.TOP |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rbth.com/arts/333762-5-reasons-to-watch-silver-skates-on-netflix |title=5 reasons to watch 'Silver Skates' on Netflix |last=Ryabikova |first=Victoria |date=May 6, 2021 |work=[[Russia Beyond]] |access-date=May 8, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pajiba.com/film_reviews/review-want-to-see-a-russian-titanic-on-ice-silver-skates-has-got-you-covered.php |title=Now On Netflix: Want to see a Russian 'Titanic' on Ice? 'Silver Skates' Has Got You Covered |last=Donaldson |first=Kayleigh |date=June 16, 2021 |website=Pajiba.com |access-date=June 16, 2021}}</ref>

[[Yakut language]] drama ''[[Scarecrow (2020 film)|Scarecrow]]'' by Dmitry Davydov won the main prize at the 2020 [[Kinotavr|Kinotavr film festival]] . [[Comedy drama]] ''[[House Arrest (2021 film)|House Arrest]]'' by [[Aleksei Alekseivich German|Aleksey German Jr.]] and [[Ossetian language]] drama ''[[Unclenching the Fists]]'' by [[Kira Kovalenko]] was selected to compete in the ''[[Un Certain Regard]]'' section at the [[2021 Cannes Film Festival]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2021/06/2021-cannes-film-festival-lineup-1234641655/|last=Sharf|first=Zack|date=10 June 2021|title=Cannes Film Festival 2021 Lineup: Sean Baker, Wes Anderson, and More Compete for Palme d'Or|work=[[IndieWire]]|access-date=16 November 2022}}</ref> there ''Unclenching the Fists'' won [[Un Certain Regard]] Award.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://variety.com/2021/film/festivals/unclenching-the-fists-cannes-un-certain-regard-1235021570/|last=Lodge|first=Guy|title=Russian Drama 'Unclenching the Fists' Takes Top Prize at Cannes Un Certain Regard Awards|magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=16 July 2021}}</ref>

''[[:ru:Последняя «Милая Болгария|The Last Darling Bulgaria]]'' by [[Aleksey Fedorchenko]] premiered at the 2021 [[Moscow International Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.moscowfilmfestival.ru/miff43/films/?id=43010 |title=Основной конкурс / Последняя "Милая Болгария" |trans-title= Last «Dear Bulgaria» / Poslednyaya «Milaya Bolgariya» |language=ru |work= Moscow International Film Festival|date=2021-04-25|access-date=2021-04-25 |archive-date=2021-04-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210424230225/http://www.moscowfilmfestival.ru/miff43/films/?id=43010 }}</ref>
