The Atlantis theme was taken up the same year in a peplum, ''[[Hercules and the Conquest of Atlantis]]'' (''Ercole alla conquista di Atlantide'', 1961) by [[Vittorio Cottafavi]] with [[Reg Park]], [[Enrico Maria Salerno]] and Gian Maria Volonté: the protagonist reaches [[Atlantis]] and discovers the secret of its power, eventually managing to destroy its powers.<ref name="Cinematografo1961ErcoleAtlantide">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/ercole-alla-conquista-di-atlantide-ou3e88sy|title=Ercole alla conquista di Atlantide|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> On the myth of Atlantis the film grafts typical science fiction elements, including an implicit reference to atomic energy, also linking the story to the present through references to [[Nazism]] and to theories of an [[Aryan race]] destined to dominate the world; contemporary critics already judged it a successful work, rich in inventions and capable of maintaining grace and measure despite the irony.<ref name="Cinematografo1961ErcoleAtlantide" /><ref name="Bourget2003Avventura" /><ref name="DellaCasa2004Peplum" />

''[[The Giant of Metropolis]]'' (''Il gigante di Metropolis'', 1961) by [[Umberto Scarpelli]] is set in 20,000 BC in the city of Metropolis, governed by a mad dictator who disposes of an extremely advanced science: intruders are struck by a magnetic storm, and the ruler conducts reckless scientific experiments such as [[Brain transplant|brain transplants]].<ref name="Cinematografo1961Gigante">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/il-gigante-di-metropolis-konvsvdd|title=Il gigante di Metropolis|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Brignoli|2022|pp=134–135}} ''[[Hercules in the Valley of Woe]]'' (''Maciste contro Ercole nella valle dei guai'', 1961), by [[Mario Mattoli]], uses a more explicit science fiction device: the protagonists use a [[time travel|time machine]] with the intention of reaching the future but are transported seven thousand years into the past, where they meet the two heroes of the title.<ref name="Cinematografo1961MacisteErcole">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/maciste-contro-ercole-nella-valle-dei-guai-t5tevwqd|title=Maciste contro Ercole nella valle dei guai|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> In the 1964 film ''[[Hercules Against the Moon Men]]'' (''Maciste e la regina di Samar'', 1964) by [[Giacomo Gentilomo]], the protagonist [[Hercules]] instead has to face an entire army of [[alien invasion|space invaders]] from the [[Moon]], who dominate the kingdom of Samar, impose periodic sacrifices and try to bring their queen back to life.{{sfn|Brioni|Comberiati|2020|pp=70–71}} Also belonging to the strand is ''[[Conqueror of Atlantis]]'' (''Il conquistatore di Atlantide'', 1965) by [[Alfonso Brescia]], in which the protagonist reaches the ruins of Atlantis, where the survivors produce beings without their own will with the intention of conquering the world.<ref name="Cinematografo1965Conquistatore">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/il-conquistatore-di-atlantide-h5vttpwr|title=Il conquistatore di Atlantide|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

=== Italian-style spy-fi ===
{{See also|Eurospy film|Spy-fi (subgenre)}}
[[File:Franco Franchi & Ciccio Ingrassia.jpg|thumb|alt=Franco Franchi and Ciccio Ingrassia.|The comedy duo [[Franco and Ciccio|Franco Franchi and Ciccio Ingrassia]], in the cast of ''[[Dr. Goldfoot and the Girl Bombs]]'' (''Le spie vengono dal semifreddo'', 1966)]]

Italian cinema between 1964 and 1969 was flooded by a wave of [[low-budget film|low-budget]] [[Spy-fi (subgenre)|spy-fi]] films that sought above all to imitate the successful [[Cinema of the United Kingdom|British films]] dedicated to [[James Bond]], Agent 007 created by [[Ian Fleming]].<ref name="CSC2009Spionaggio">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/cinema-trevi-dall%C2%92italia-con-amore-come-imitammo-james-bond-il-cinema-spionistico-italiano-da-james-tont-ad-asso-di-picche/|title=Dall'Italia con amore: come imitammo James Bond. Il cinema spionistico italiano da James Tont ad Asso di Picche|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|date=21 January 2009|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Menarini|2002|p=56}}{{sfn|Missero|2018|pp=135–136}} In the period about 150 titles were made, including [[parody|parodies]], often in collaboration with other European countries and with modest ambitions, shooting quickly and resorting to strongly [[stock character|stereotyped]] formulas based on the Bond model: the heroic [[Espionage|secret agent]] is flanked by [[Bond girl|provocative women]] and faces [[mad scientist]]s or evil [[secret society|secret organizations]] that nurture insane plans for [[world domination]] through science-fictional and improbable [[doomsday device|apocalyptic weapons]].<ref name="CSC2009Spionaggio" />{{sfn|Menarini|2002|p=56}}{{sfn|Missero|2018|pp=135–136}}

''[[Planets Against Us]]'' (''I pianeti contro di noi'', 1962), by Romano Ferrara, grafts science fiction elements onto a spy plot: an individual capable of blocking [[radar]] in areas of atomic interest and of disintegrating an agent turns out to be an artificial being in human form from extraterrestrial regions.<ref name="Cinematografo1962Pianeti">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/i-pianeti-contro-di-noi-ejesvxd8|title=I pianeti contro di noi|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> The strand also lent itself immediately to parody: in ''[[Dr. Goldfoot and the Girl Bombs]]'' (''Le spie vengono dal semifreddo'', 1966) by [[Mario Bava]], an Italian-American co-production with [[Vincent Price]] and the comedy duo [[Franco and Ciccio]], an "[[Computer|electronic brain]]" starts the investigation, a scientist artificially produces young women and the criminal plan culminates in the attempt to seize an atomic aircraft to launch a nuclear device on Moscow; in the United States the film was distributed by [[American International Pictures]].<ref name="Cinematografo1966Spie">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/le-spie-vengono-dal-semifreddo-qq9xdu7c|title=Le spie vengono dal semifreddo|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="AFIGoldfoot1966">{{cite web|url=https://catalog.afi.com/Film/21552-DR-GOLDFOOT-AND-THE-GIRL-BOMBS?cxt=filmography|title=Dr. Goldfoot and the Girl Bombs|publisher=American Film Institute|access-date=19 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> The same comic vein includes ''[[Il vostro super agente Flit]]'' (1966), with [[Raimondo Vianello]]: the protagonist, equipped with an "electronic brain", investigates diplomatic incidents caused by extraterrestrials aiming at [[Nuclear warfare|nuclear war]] and galactic domination.<ref name="CinematografoFlit">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/il-vostro-super-agente-flit-qsz5pdvf|title=Il vostro super agente Flit|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> In the two [[James Tont operazione U.N.O.|James Tont]] films, played by [[Lando Buzzanca]], the parody passes first through a record connected to an explosive charge intended to destroy the UN building and then through the hibernation of the agent and a plan to put into orbit the top sphere of [[St. Peter's Basilica|Saint Peter's dome]] with the basilica's treasure.<ref name="CinematografoTontUNO">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/james-tont-operazione-uno-y69cl2oe|title=James Tont operazione uno|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CinematografoTontDUE">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/james-tont-operazione-due-a071zsx8|title=James Tont operazione due|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> ''[[James Tont operazione U.N.O.]]'' (1965) achieved among the best Italian commercial results in the strand, adapting the formula through already popular comic actors and the use of comedy, while the two films have been re-evaluated for their comic inventions and considered an anticipation of the ''[[Austin Powers]]'' series.{{sfn|Missero|2018|p=139}}{{sfn|Menarini|2002|p=106}}

Among the spy films of the period with particularly explicit science fiction elements, ''[[Operation Counterspy]]'' (''Asso di picche – Operazione controspionaggio'', 1965) by [[Nick Nostro]] presents a secret atomic plant and a global blackmail plan based on nuclear devices.<ref name="CSC2009Spionaggio" /><ref name="ANICAAsso1965">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG1636|title=Asso di picche – Operazione controspionaggio (1965)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=21 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> In ''Matchless'' (1967) by [[Alberto Lattuada]] a ring allows the protagonist to become invisible for twenty minutes every ten hours, while international powers contend for a formula and some vials of a secret liquid.<ref name="Cinematografo1967Matchless">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/matchless-b4z94bs2|title=Matchless|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> The science fiction [[thriller film|thriller]] ''[[Mission Stardust]]'' (''...4..3..2..1...morte'', 1967) by [[Primo Zeglio]] is inspired by [[Perry Rhodan]], protagonist of a German series that had enormous success in its homeland and whose characterization also draws on previous heroes of science fiction adventure such as [[Flash Gordon]]; the plot freely mixes space adventure with a [[spy fiction|spy story]]; in [[West Germany]] the film was released the same year under the title ''Perry Rhodan – SOS aus dem Weltall''.<ref name="Cinematografo1967Perry">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/4-3-2-1-morte-x647c84x|title=...4 ...3 ...2... 1... morte|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="Filmportal1967Perry">{{cite web|url=https://www.filmportal.de/film/perry-rhodan-sos-aus-dem-weltall_233da9fccd764aa08fcbbcfc2e8547ee|title=Perry Rhodan – SOS aus dem Weltall|publisher=filmportal.de|access-date=19 August 2026|language=de}}</ref><ref name="TriestePerry2020">{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencefictionfestival.org/gorgo-1-perry-rhodan-lerede-delluniverso/|title=Perry Rhodan: l'erede dell'universo|publisher=Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|date=9 April 2020|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

=== The masked superheroes ===


Among the first masked [[superhero]]es of Italian cinema are those of ''[[Superargo Versus Diabolicus]]'' (''Superargo contro Diabolikus'', 1966), directed by [[Nick Nostro]], and of ''[[Goldface, the Fantastic Superman]]'' (''Goldface – Il fantastico superman'', 1967) by [[Bitto Albertini]]; they were characters born on the example of Mexican [[lucha libre]] wrestlers and inserted in [[Spy-fi (subgenre)|spy-fi]] plots.{{sfn|Sponzilli|2017|p=62}}<ref name="ANICA1966Superargo">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG1993|title=Superargo contro Diabolikus (1966)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CinematografoGoldface1967">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/goldface-il-fantastico-superman-thpdutbr|title=Goldface il fantastico Superman|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> In ''Superargo contro Diabolikus'' the protagonist is modeled above all on the Mexican wrestler [[El Santo]], who appeared on Italian screens as Argos, while the film is a co-production with Spain; a criminal scientist assaults ships carrying uranium and mercury and uses modern plants to produce an isotope of gold with which he intends to undermine the world economy, in a story that moves from adventure to espionage with science fiction elements, with a comic-strip and ironic tone and artisanally made effects.<ref name="CinematografoSuperargo">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/superargo-contro-diabolikus-sg7ee7mi|title=Superargo contro Diabolikus|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Pergolari|2025|pp=143–144}}

Among the other masked heroes of the period are ''[[Phenomenal and the Treasure of Tutankhamen]]'' ''(Fenomenal e il tesoro di Tutankamen'', 1968), ''[[Flashman (film)|Flashman]]'' (1967) and ''[[Fantabulous Inc.]]'' (''La donna, il sesso e il superuomo'', 1967).<ref name="CSCFattoreK2009">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/cinema-trevi-15-aprile-indipendente-italiano-il-fattore-killing-tra-cinema-e-fumetto-nell%C2%92italia-nera-degli-anni-sessanta-2/|title=Cinema Trevi, 15 aprile: "Indipendente italiano. Il fattore K(illing) tra cinema e fumetto nell'Italia nera degli anni Sessanta"|publisher=Fondazione Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|year=2009|access-date=25 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="ANICAFantabulos1968">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG2318|title=Fantabulos (1968)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=25 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> ''Flashman'' (1967), by Mino Loy and [[Luciano Martino]], presents a serum capable of making people invisible,<ref name="Cinematografo1967Flashman">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/flashman-x00rzlm1|title=Flashman|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> while ''[[Argoman the Fantastic Superman]]'' (''Come rubare la corona d'Inghilterra'', 1967) by [[Sergio Grieco]] presents a superhero, a diamond formed after an atomic explosion and humanoids created with the appearance of politicians.<ref name="Cinematografo1967Argoman">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/come-rubare-la-corona-dinghilterra-nany2v5e|title=Come rubare la corona d'Inghilterra|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Sponzilli|2017|p=64}} The most important series of the strand is that of ''[[The Three Fantastic Supermen]]'' (''I fantastici 3 Supermen'', 1967): the 1967 film, directed by [[Gianfranco Parolini]] as Frank Kramer, started an acrobatic series modeled on the Superargo films and continued with seven sequels of varying success, in which directors, actors and character names changed several times.{{sfn|Hughes|2011|p=174}}<ref name="CinematografoSerieTreSupermen">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/crash-che-botte-strippo-strappo-stroppio-gs3lb2ry|title=Crash! Che botte strippo, strappo, stroppio|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Sponzilli|2017|p=61}} In the first film the three protagonists, endowed with great physical strength and acrobatic qualities, wear bulletproof vests created by a scientist and face a machine capable of duplicating objects and people, maintaining an ironic tone that playfully treats comic-book models for young people.<ref name="Cinematografo1967TreSupermen">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/i-fantastici-3-supermen-oyxjjkdx|title=I fantastici 3 Supermen|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

In 1968 [[Mario Bava]] directed ''[[Danger: Diabolik]]'' (''Diabolik'', 1968), a project entrusted to him by [[Dino De Laurentiis]] and based on the comic by the [[Angela and Luciana Giussani|Giussani sisters]]: it belongs to the producer's series of adaptations of science fiction comics, begun with ''[[Barbarella (film)|Barbarella]]'' and continued with ''[[Flash Gordon (film)|Flash Gordon]]'', with a supercriminal protagonist in the line of [[Fantômas]] but equipped with the technological arsenal of the [[James Bond|007]] films; ''[[The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction]]'' judges it futuristic but only marginally science fiction.<ref name="SFEDiabolik2025">{{cite web|url=https://sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/diabolik|title=Diabolik|publisher=The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction|date=25 August 2025|access-date=5 September 2026|language=en}}</ref>{{sfn|Pezzotta|2025|p=67}} Among the adaptations of the black comic, it stands out for its deliberately glossy look,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.labiennale.org/it/agenda/classici-fuori-mostra-diabolik|title=Classici fuori Mostra – Diabolik|publisher=La Biennale di Venezia|date=4 March 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Pergolari|2025|p=127}} maintaining an Italian identity while adopting foreign genres destined for the international market and recalling [[Pop art]].{{sfn|Pezzotta|2025|p=63}} On screen, however, the masked thief had already arrived in comic form: in 1966 [[Johnny Dorelli]] had launched the character of Dorellik in the television variety show ''Johnny Sera'', a bungling criminal in a bodysuit built as a caricature of Diabolik, brought to the big screen the following year by [[Steno (director)|Steno]] in ''[[How to Kill 400 Duponts]]'' (''Arrriva Dorellik'', 1967), which precedes Bava's film by a year although the latter had been in production since 1964.{{sfn|Muggeo|2025|p=115}} Dorellik's introduction, with its diabolical laugh and a sudden zoom onto the face, is the same formula Bava reuses for his protagonist's first appearance: the "serious" adaptation arrives after the caricatures.{{sfn|Muggeo|2025|pp=115–116}}

== Social science fiction, satire and dystopia ==
Between the late 1960s and early 1970s, with the [[Protests of 1968|1968 movement]] and the strong political and social changes that accompanied it, cinema also showed a growing interest in [[social science fiction]], often using fantastic situations to address contemporary society's problems in a critical or [[satire|satirical]] form.{{sfn|Guidi|1998}}{{sfn|Brioni|Comberiati|2020|p=9}} In these stories the science fiction elements depend above all on the premise of the narrative, rather than on the sets; despite limited means, these films experiment with particularly original visual and narrative solutions.{{sfn|Oppedisano|Rossi|2018|p=97}} Satire and parody are perhaps the only true area in which Italian science fiction cinema has been able to offer original contributions.<ref name="SFEItaly2026" /> Science fiction elements also appear in art cinema: in ''[[L'Eclisse]]'' (1962) and ''[[Red Desert (film)|Red Desert]]'' (''Il deserto rosso'', 1964) by [[Michelangelo Antonioni]], they have been recognized in the almost automatic movements of the characters and in the urban and industrial spaces, described as non-places with a post-atomic appearance; in the second film science fiction also contributes to representing the effects of [[Industrialisation|industrialization]] on the environment and the unease caused by modernization.<ref>{{cite web|author=Diego Battistini|url=https://drammaturgia.fupress.net/recensioni/recensione2.php?id=6229|title=Bianco e nero, a. LXXIV, n. 579, aprile-luglio 2014|publisher=Firenze University Press|date=13 May 2015|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Dimasi|2024|p=39}}

=== Economic miracle and sociopolitical satire ===
[[File:Ugo Gregoretti 1961.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Ugo Gregoretti in 1961.|[[Ugo Gregoretti]] in 1961, two years before ''[[Omicron (film)|Omicron]]'']]
[[File:Alberto Sordi (1962).jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Alberto Sordi in 1962.|[[Alberto Sordi]], director and star of ''[[Catherine and I|Io e Caterina]]'' (1980)]]

A precedent of the social strand is ''[[Omicron (film)|Omicron]]'' (1963), written and directed by [[Ugo Gregoretti]], in which an alien enters the body of a dead worker and ends up inciting the other workers to [[strike action|strike]]; the film thus builds a satire of [[Class struggle|class conflict]], making the alien's strangeness coincide with that of the alienated worker, while the Fordist assembly line and hyper-productivity take on a more threatening character than the extraterrestrial invasion, and science fiction becomes the means to criticize the social transformations of the [[Italian economic miracle]].{{sfn|Menarini|2002|pp=101–102}}{{sfn|Brignoli|2022|pp=135–136}}{{sfn|Brioni|Comberiati|2019|pp=86–88}} ''[[Il disco volante]]'' (internationally released as ''The Flying Saucer'', 1964), directed by [[Tinto Brass]], uses the landing of aliens in a village in the [[Veneto]] countryside as the starting point for a grotesque satire of provincial Italy and the narrow-mindedness of the petty bourgeoisie faced with an incomprehensible phenomenon; the satire also targets [[alcoholism]] and the absence of [[morality]] in the different social classes, from the decadent [[nobility]] to the hypocritical and self-righteous [[bourgeoisie]], up to the [[clergy]].{{sfn|Menarini|2002|pp=101–102}}<ref name="CSCDiscoVolante2012">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/tinto-brass-atto-primo-il-tempo-della-rivolta/|title=Tinto Brass. Atto primo: Il tempo della rivolta|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Borelli|2017|p=93}} The same season includes ''I marziani hanno 12 mani'' (1964) by [[Castellano & Pipolo]], in which four Martians arrive on Earth to study its customs and end up confronting the life and consumption of Italy's economic miracle; the film is a science fiction parody with farcical tones.{{sfn|Menarini|2002|pp=101–103}}<ref name="ANICAMarziani1964">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG+1397|title=I marziani hanno 12 mani (1964)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

Finally, ''[[The 10th Victim]]'' (''La decima vittima'', 1965) by [[Elio Petri]] is loosely based on the short story ''The Seventh Victim'' (1953) by [[Robert Sheckley]], included in the anthology ''The Wonders of the Possible'' edited by [[Sergio Solmi]] and [[Carlo Fruttero]], whose Einaudi edition dates to 1959; starring [[Marcello Mastroianni]] and [[Ursula Andress]], the film imagines a [[Rome]] of an unspecified future in which, wars having disappeared, aggression is channeled into a legalized manhunt in which the winner reaches ten victims, taking from the story the obligatory passage from the role of hunter to that of victim.{{sfn|Boschi|2017|pp=270–271, 274}}<ref name="SBNMeraviglie1959">{{cite web|url=https://opac.bibliotecauniversitaria.pi.it/bid/RAV0065555|title=Le meraviglie del possibile: antologia della fantascienza|publisher=Biblioteca Universitaria di Pisa – SBN|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CSCPopFilmArt2013">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/pop-film-art/|title=Pop Film Art|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|year=2013|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> In the film the game becomes a television show: the killing of the tenth victim is prepared like a commercial to be broadcast live, thus anticipating a dystopian version of reality TV; the satire simultaneously targets new commodities, "American-style" desires and consumption anxiety, accompanied by references to [[hard-edge painting]] and [[Pop art]].{{sfn|Boschi|2017|pp=274–275}}{{sfn|Brioni|Comberiati|2019|p=233}} 

[[Animation]] also participates in the same satirical vein with ''[[VIP my Brother Superman]]'' (''Vip – Mio fratello superuomo'', 1968) by [[Bruno Bozzetto]], a parody of [[superhero]]es and consumerism in which the attempt to conquer the world passes through the suggestions of an electronic brain.<ref name="CinematografoVip1968">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/vip-mio-fratello-superuomo-ynx05n2t|title=Vip, mio fratello superuomo|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Sponzilli|2017|pp=64–65}} The satirical vein resurfaced in 1980 with ''Io e Caterina'', directed and starring [[Alberto Sordi]], where the science fiction element – a robot maid – is at the center of a comic-satirical story; the robot's malfunction arises from the imitation of jealousy and possessive devotion and offers a pessimistic vision of gender relations.<ref name="CinematografoIoCaterina1980">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/io-e-caterina-iweydlw0|title=Io e Caterina|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Bigliardi|2022}} The protagonist's male and class privilege also passes through the exploitation of women's work, which however makes him dependent on their domestic and organizational skills; the isolated house accentuates loneliness and becomes a place of control, while the robot imported from the United States does not solve the problems of the Italian male and exposes his privilege to feminist demands.{{sfn|Brioni|Comberiati|2020|pp=30–31}}

''Colpo di stato''<ref name="ANICAColpoStato1968">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG2555|title=Colpo di Stato (1968)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}} ANICA registers the film as 1968 with the censorship certificate of 19 December 1968.</ref><ref name="CSCColpoStato1968">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/dal-6-al-18-maggio-al-cinema-trevi-grande-retrospettiva-dedicata-al-cinema-di-luciano-salce-autore-che-numerose-iniziative-stanno-mettendo-in-nuova-luce/|title=Dal 6 al 18 maggio al cinema Trevi, grande retrospettiva dedicata al cinema di Luciano Salce|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="TreccaniColpoStato1969">{{cite web|author=Enrico Giacovelli|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/luciano-salce_%28Enciclopedia-del-Cinema%29/|title=Salce, Luciano|publisher=Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana|year=2004|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}} Treccani dates it to 1969.</ref><ref name="CSCColpoStato1969">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/lessico-del-cinema-italiano-2/|title=Lessico del cinema italiano|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}} The Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia also presents it as a film of 1969.</ref><ref name="CSCColpoStatoRassegnaStampa">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/completata-la-catalogazione-della-rassegna-stampa-della-vides-cinematografica-di-franco-cristaldi-2/|title=Completata la catalogazione della Rassegna stampa della Vides Cinematografica di Franco Cristaldi|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}} The CSC includes ''Colpo di stato'' among the films of the Vides press review collection, composed of reviews, news and curiosities published in the press.</ref> is a biting [[political fiction|fantapolitical]] comedy by [[Luciano Salce]] that imagines an Italy in which the [[Italian Communist Party|Communist Party]] wins the elections instead of the [[Christian Democracy (Italy)|Christian Democracy]], triggering panic reactions; opposed by both the [[right-wing politics|right]] and the [[left-wing politics|left]], Salce's film was substantially withdrawn.{{sfn|Verona|2016|p=156}}<ref name="CSCColpoStato">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/comincia-il-3-febbraio-al-cinema-trevi-la-rassegna-piccolo-schermo-grande-scherno-come-il-cinema-italiano-ha-raccontato-la-television/|title=Piccolo schermo, grande scherno. Come il cinema italiano ha raccontato la televisione|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> The supercomputer correctly counts the votes and is introduced in the name of transparency; the satire strikes the inability of men to accept its result.{{sfn|Bigliardi|2022}}

=== Dystopia and catastrophe ===
[[File:Marco Ferreri Cannes.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Marco Ferreri at Cannes.|[[Marco Ferreri]], director of ''[[The Seed of Man]]'' (''Il seme dell'uomo'', 1969)]]

In ''[[The Seed of Man]]'' (''Il seme dell'uomo'', 1969), the only science fiction feature film by [[Marco Ferreri]], the [[Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction|end of the world]] takes on an almost [[metaphysics|metaphysical]] character: a mysterious "plague" has decimated humanity and the survivors confront the possibility of its extinction; the film belongs to the European art science fiction of the 1960s, which addressed in dystopian form themes such as modernization, family, work, state and revolution.<ref name="CSCSemeUomo2017">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/storie-di-ordinaria-follia-i-film-di-marco-ferreri-parte-prima/|title=Storie di ordinaria follia. I film di Marco Ferreri (parte prima)|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|year=2017|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Guaraldo|2023|pp=15–16}}{{sfn|Malvestio|2025|pp=63–64}} The opening in the motorway restaurant and the subsequent domestic museum of consumer objects transform mass products into useless relics, contrasting their short duration with their long persistence as waste and making the catastrophe also a critique of the logic of consumption.<ref name="CSCSemeUomo2017" />{{sfn|Guaraldo|2023|pp=15–16}}{{sfn|Malvestio|2025|pp=63–64}} 

A [[apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction|post-atomic]] scenario also characterizes ''Ecce Homo – I sopravvissuti'' (1969) by Bruno Gaburro, with [[Irene Papas]] and [[Philippe Leroy]] and a soundtrack by [[Ennio Morricone]]: after a nuclear disaster, a family settles by the sea while the arrival of other survivors cracks its equilibrium; the story replaces the usual struggle to rebuild the world with the doubt about the very opportunity to perpetuate the human species, placing the film among the first Italian examples of the post-nuclear strand.<ref name="ANICAEcceHomo1969">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG2578|title=Ecce Homo (1969)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CSCEcceHomo">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/kaboom-variazioni-sull%C2%92italia-post-atomica/|title=Kaboom! – Variazioni sull'Italia post-atomica|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="SFEItaly2026" />

=== Protest and the fantastic-dystopian ===
[[File:I cannibali (film 1970).JPG|thumb|alt=I cannibali by Liliana Cavani.|''[[The Year of the Cannibals]]'' (''I cannibali'', 1969) by [[Liliana Cavani]]]]
[[File:Corrado Farina con il Pardo d'oro.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Corrado Farina with the Pardo d'oro.|[[Corrado Farina]] with the [[Golden Leopard|Pardo d'oro]] won at [[Locarno Film Festival|Locarno]] for ''[[They Have Changed Their Face]]'' (''...hanno cambiato faccia'', 1971)]]

Between the late 1960s and the 1970s some Italian fantastic and dystopian films relied above all on technology and sexuality to question the hopes of social and political change widespread in the left of the time, bringing into art science fiction themes present in contemporary political debate.<ref name="BisoniIRIS2014">{{cite web|author=Claudio Bisoni|url=https://hdl.handle.net/11585/542111|title=Marcuse supera Asimov. Il fantastico distopico nel cinema italiano degli anni settanta|publisher=Alma Mater Studiorum – Università di Bologna|year=2014|access-date=30 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> The film ''[[H2S (film)|H2S]]'' (1969) by [[Roberto Faenza]] tells of the young protagonist's rebellion against a [[technocracy|technocratic]] and [[consumerism|consumerist]] society, to the point of planting a bomb, with a soundtrack by [[Ennio Morricone]].<ref name="ANICAH2S1969">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG2598|title=H 2 S (1969)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Brioni|Comberiati|2020|pp=50–52}} ''H2S'' provoked a harsh reaction from censorship, was seized and involved in legal proceedings, being distributed only in 1971.<ref name="TreccaniFaenza2003">{{cite web|author=Federica De Paolis|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/roberto-faenza_%28Enciclopedia-del-Cinema%29/|title=Faenza, Roberto|publisher=Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana|year=2003|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> Public screening received a favorable opinion with a ban for minors under 14.<ref name="ChangesH2S1969">{{cite web|url=https://filmcensorship.changes.unimi.it/files_detail.php?id=92265|title=Fascicolo 54238: H2S|publisher=Università degli Studi di Milano|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> As in [[Corrado Farina]]'s 1971 film ''...hanno cambiato faccia'', science fiction serves above all to express an openly [[anti-capitalism|anti-capitalist]] social and political critique; in the same year the film won a [[Golden Leopard]] reserved for second works at the [[Locarno Film Festival]].<ref name="CinematografoHannoCambiato1971">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/hanno-cambiato-faccia-sudpu37s|title=Hanno cambiato faccia|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CinematografoFarina2026">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/riflettori/80-film-per-la-repubblica-ma-non-sono-quelli-che-vi-aspettate-yzk5kqb3|title=80 film per la Repubblica (ma non sono quelli che vi aspettate)|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|year=2026|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="Locarno1971Hanno">{{cite web|url=https://www.locarnofestival.ch/it/festival/palmares/1971.html|title=1971 – Palmarès|publisher=Locarno Film Festival|year=1971|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> 

''Eat It'' (1969) by Francesco Casaretti also mixes black fable and science fiction in a grotesque satire of advertising and the reduction of the individual to merchandise, close to Faenza's early films and partly anticipating [[Marcello Aliprandi]]'s ''La ragazza di latta'' and ''...hanno cambiato faccia''; based on a story by [[Roberto Leoni]], the film marks the debut of [[Paolo Villaggio]] and features a soundtrack by Ennio Morricone and over-the-top sets by Giorgio Giovannini (art director also in [[Roberto Faenza]]'s ''[[Escalation (1968 Italian film)|Escalation]]'').<ref name="ANICAEatIt1969">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG2577|title=Eat it (1969)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="ChangesEatIt1969">{{cite web|url=https://filmcensorship.changes.unimi.it/files_detail.php?id=91589|title=Fascicolo 53229: Eat it|publisher=Università degli Studi di Milano|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Bigliardi|2022}} The offices of the producing company are instead minimalist, technologically advanced and automated; ''Eat it'' is a new type of gelatinous brown [[Potted meat|canned meat]].<ref name="CinematografoEatIt1968">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/eat-it-gbpghvwi|title=Eat It|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nocturno.it/movie/eat-it/|author=Pierpaolo De Sanctis|title=Eat it|website=Nocturno.it|access-date=23 April 2020|language=it}}</ref>

''Il tunnel sotto il mondo'', the directorial debut of [[Luigi Cozzi]], later one of the main figures of Italian science fiction cinema, was presented in 1969 at the [[Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|International Science Fiction Film Festival of Trieste]]; it is an experimental film inspired by the 1955 short story of the same name by [[Frederik Pohl]],{{sfn|Bigliardi|2022}} a classic of consumerism satire,<ref name="SFEItaly2026" /> in which an entire community is held prisoner by advertising researchers.<ref name="TriesteTunnel1969">{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencefictionfestival.org/film/il-tunnel-sotto-il-mondo-luigi-cozzi/|title=Il tunnel sotto il mondo|publisher=Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|date=11 August 2021|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="PohlTunnelGutenberg">{{cite web|author=Frederik Pohl|url=https://www.gutenberg.org/files/31979/31979-h/31979-h.htm|title=The Tunnel Under the World|publisher=Project Gutenberg|access-date=28 August 2026|language=en}}</ref>
''[[The Year of the Cannibals]]'' (''I cannibali'', 1969) by [[Liliana Cavani]]<ref name="ANICACannibali1969">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG2776|title=I cannibali (1969)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}} ANICA registers the film as 1969 with the censorship certificate of 22 November 1969.</ref><ref name="ASACCannibali1970">{{cite web|url=https://asac.labiennale.org/attivita/cinema/10061|title=I cannibali|publisher=La Biennale di Venezia – ASAC|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}} The ASAC record of the Biennale indicates 1970.</ref><ref name="CinematografoCannibali1970">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/i-cannibali-fsnn63so|title=I cannibali|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}} The Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo records the Euro International Film distribution in 1970.</ref> relocates [[Sophocles]]' ''[[Antigone (Sophocles play)|Antigone]]'' to [[Milan]], in an unspecified but near future, connecting the myth to the [[1968 movement in Italy|1968 protest]] and entrusting the force of change to young people rather than to [[ideology]]; family, prison and psychiatric hospital become places of control and repression, while the ending keeps the political force of rebellion alive even after the protagonists' death.<ref name="CSCCavaniCannibali">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/al-di-la-del-bene-e-del-male-il-cinema-di-liliana-cavani/|title=Al di là del bene e del male. Il cinema di Liliana Cavani|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Brioni|Comberiati|2019|pp=98–101}}

Social unease is again the protagonist in ''N.P. – Il segreto'' (1971) by [[Silvano Agosti]], with [[Irene Papas]] and [[Francisco Rabal]]: the story of an inventor who is deprived of his industry by the government and socially degraded, discovering that the machines he invented and conceived as instruments of progress are used instead to systematically eliminate opponents of the regime and the "superfluous"; like ''H2S'', the film restates the libertarian ideas of 1968 in science fiction form.<ref name="CinetecaBolognaNP2017">{{cite web|author=Lorenzo Ciofani|url=https://www.cinefiliaritrovata.it/lo-sguardo-alienato-n-p-il-segreto-di-silvano-agosti/|title=Lo sguardo alienato: N.P. Il segreto di Silvano Agosti|publisher=Cineteca di Bologna|date=27 March 2017|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="PorrettaNP2017">{{cite web|url=https://porrettacinema.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/FCP-catalogo-2017.pdf|title=N.P. – Il segreto|publisher=Festival del Cinema di Porretta Terme|year=2017|p=47|access-date=24 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Bigliardi|2022}}

In the 1975 film ''[[The Sex Machine]]'' (''Conviene far bene l'amore'', 1975) by [[Pasquale Festa Campanile]], a future civilization grappling with the energy crisis discovers the system of drawing energy from [[sexual intercourse]], making it an obligation; it is a film close to the [[commedia sexy all'italiana|erotic comedy]], born in the climate of the [[1973 oil crisis]] and the consequent austerity measures, which reworks [[Wilhelm Reich|Reichian]] theories in a paradoxical way.<ref name="CinematografoConviene1975">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/conviene-far-bene-lamore-b4bjs943|title=Conviene far bene l'amore|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Lorenzo Pellizzari|url=https://cineforum.it/rubrica/L_altra_faccia_delle_lune/23_novembre_1973_1993|title=23 novembre 1973–1993|publisher=Cineforum|date=24 November 2013|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Bigliardi|2022}} [[Ugo Tognazzi]] finally tackled sociological science fiction, this time as director, in ''[[I viaggiatori della sera]]'' (1979), an [[art film]] based on the novel of the same name by [[Umberto Simonetta]], set in a [[dystopia]]n future that no longer tolerates the condition of old age and the elderly, who must participate in a "Great Game" that sooner or later decrees their physical elimination.<ref name="TreccaniTognazzi2019">{{cite web|author=Michele Sancisi|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/ugo-tognazzi_res-b1d7c5f4-3616-11ea-9087-00271042e8d9_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/|title=Tognazzi, Ugo|publisher=Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana|year=2019|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CinematografoViaggiatori1979" />

=== Experimental cinema ===
[[File:Mario Schifani.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Mario Schifano.|[[Mario Schifano]], author of ''Umano, non umano'' (1969)]]

In Italian experimental cinema science fiction does not form an autonomous genre: it arises rather from the use of the camera, video and digital techniques to make images of everyday life strange or alien.{{sfn|Catricalà|2014|pp=66–67}} In ''Umano, non umano'' (1969) by [[Mario Schifano]], the burnt film and the final image of the television produce this sense of estrangement through technique itself, while Cioni Carpi's ''I will... I shan't'' builds a mental and non-human journey with animated and abstract images accompanied by mysterious sounds.{{sfn|Catricalà|2014|pp=64–66}}<ref name="CSCUmano1969">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/orizzonti-1960-1978-il-cinema-umano-non-umano-di-mario-schifano/|title=Orizzonti 1960–1978: il cinema umano non umano di Mario Schifano|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> A similar effect recurs in the video ''Io mi chiamo Michele e tu?'' by [[Michele Sambin]], where the video loop multiplies identity until it becomes strange; in ''Non accaduto'' (1968) by [[Gianfranco Baruchello]], instead, reproduction technologies serve to work on time, absence and the sense of estrangement.{{sfn|Catricalà|2014|pp=67–69}}

=== Sexual liberation and existential fantastic ===
[[File:Roger Vadim and Jane Fonda in Rome - May 1967.jpg|thumb|alt=Roger Vadim and Jane Fonda in Rome in May 1967.|[[Roger Vadim]] and [[Jane Fonda]] in Rome in May 1967; Vadim directed ''[[Barbarella (film)|Barbarella]]'' (1968) with Fonda in the title role]]

Between the 1960s and 1970s some science fiction films questioned the roles traditionally attributed to men and women, the couple and the family, while freer sexual behaviors were spreading and the idea that the relationship between man and woman and the traditional family were the only possible models was contested; in the same period art fantastic also tackled existential themes, as in the cinematic debut of [[Emidio Greco]], characterized by architectures both lucid and unreal.{{sfn|Brignoli|2022|pp=139–140}}<ref name="BisoniIRIS2014" /><ref name="TreccaniGreco2003">{{cite web|author=Bruno Roberti|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/emidio-greco_%28Enciclopedia-del-Cinema%29/|title=Greco, Emidio|publisher=Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana|year=2003|access-date=30 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

In ''[[Omicron (film)|Omicron]]'' (1963) the division of the sexes and sexual intercourse for reproductive purposes are presented by the alien as primitive traits, while ''Il tunnel sotto il mondo'' (1969) imagines first a future dominated by women and then an alien world inhabited by a single gender capable of self-reproduction; these motifs express the anxieties aroused by the possible end of binary logic in the climate of [[Sexual revolution|sexual liberation]].{{sfn|Brignoli|2022|p=136}} The fourth episode of ''Marcia nuziale'' (1966), ''La famiglia felice'', instead brings the crisis of the couple to 1999, where rubber spouses and children replace human relationships; the discourse continues in ''[[The Seed of Man]]'' (''Il seme dell'uomo'', 1969), in which the woman's refusal to be reduced to the reproductive role cracks the traditional model of wife and mother and the very continuity of the couple.{{sfn|Brignoli|2022|pp=136–137}} ''[[H2S (film)|H2S]]'' also plays on the ambiguity between masculine and feminine: after escaping from the totalitarian organization, the protagonist is recaptured and forced to marry the institution's hundred-year-old godmother, played by [[Paolo Poli]]; in the finale the godmother prepares the young man for the wedding with a pink blouse, ribbons, bows and a hair clip, bringing to a climax the contrasts between masculine and feminine, old and young, true and false, tragic and comic.{{sfn|Brignoli|2022|pp=137–139}}

Among the films that most clearly express the pop and sensual aesthetic of the 1960s is the lighthearted ''[[Barbarella (film)|Barbarella]]'' (1968), a Franco-Italian co-production made by [[Dino De Laurentiis]] and directed by [[Roger Vadim]], starring [[Jane Fonda]] (who replaced [[Virna Lisi]] after she refused the role) and various Italian actors in the cast; inspired by the [[Barbarella (comics)|comic book character of the same name]], the plot centers on the fascinating heroine of the remote future and her numerous adventures, including [[eroticism|erotic]] ones.<ref name="ANICABarbarella1968">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG2277|title=Barbarella (1968)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CinematografoVirnaLisi2023">{{cite web|author=Simona Busni|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/riflettori/stelle-nostre/la-sublime-annichilente-sconvolgente-virna-lisi-dhqx4j9q|title=La sublime, annichilente, sconvolgente Virna Lisi|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|date=17 May 2023|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="SFEItaly2026" /> In the film the protagonist's sexuality is freed from the institutions of marriage and family and becomes an expression of personal autonomy integrated into social life.{{sfn|Young|2018|p=1}}

In ''[[The Sex Machine]]'' (''Conviene far bene l'amore,'' 1975) sexuality is at the center of a dystopia: sexual intercourse provides energy and thus becomes a productive obligation; technology and sexuality show, in the fantastic-dystopian, the reversal of the utopian hopes of progressive thought with particular evidence.<ref name="BisoniIRIS2014" />

''[[Morel's Invention (film)|Morel's Invention]]'' (''L'invenzione di Morel'', 1974) by [[Emidio Greco]], the director's cinematic debut and adaptation of the [[The Invention of Morel|novel of the same name]] by [[Adolfo Bioy Casares]], instead tackles the fantastic in existential terms through cinematic architectures both lucid and unreal, while the circular repetition of images produces a disturbing effect.<ref name="TreccaniGreco2003" /><ref name="TreccaniBorges2003">{{cite web|author=Altiero Scicchitano|url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/jorge-luis-borges_%28Enciclopedia-del-Cinema%29/|title=Borges, Jorge Luis|publisher=Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana|year=2003|access-date=30 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> The film tells of the relationship between life, death and the desire for immortality through the machine invented by the title character: a castaway finds himself on an island where no one apparently notices his existence and everyone ends up repeating the same gestures and speeches as in an infinite cycle, produced by a machine capable of recording and reproducing integrally what is perceived by the senses but deadly for the recorded subjects.<ref name="CSCGrecoMorel2014">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/in-ricordo-di-emidio-greco/|title=In ricordo di Emidio Greco|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|year=2014|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CinematografoMorel1974">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/linvenzione-di-morel-nmiakngo|title=L'invenzione di Morel|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Bigliardi|2022}} The machine thus offers a form of immortality entrusted to images, while the support of industrialists and the first lethal tests conducted on employees without their consent also introduce a social and political critique.<ref name="CSCGrecoMorel2014" /><ref name="CinematografoMorel1974" />{{sfn|Bigliardi|2022}}

== Festivals, retrospectives and television ==
[[File:Trieste Science+Fiction Festival 2016.jpg|thumb|alt=The Trieste Science+Fiction Festival in 2016.|The [[Trieste Science+Fiction Festival]] in 2016]]

From the 1960s, specialized festivals and retrospectives offered science fiction cinema opportunities for screening and discussion when genre films were still difficult to see; television also contributed to making them known through retrospectives and dedicated programming.{{sfn|Cesaro|2024|pp=375–379}}<ref name="Fantafestival2009p49">{{cite web|url=https://www.fanta-festival.it/wp-content/uploads/2014/06/CatalogoFantafestival2009.pdf|title=Catalogo Fantafestival 2009|publisher=Fantafestival|year=2009|access-date=30 August 2026|language=it}}, p. 49.</ref>

In 1963 the [[Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|International Science Fiction Film Festival]] was born in [[Trieste]], the first festival event in the world dedicated to science fiction cinema; over a twenty-year period, the event also contributed to defining the study of the film genre, while the first edition was inaugurated on 6 July at the San Giusto Castle and the project originated from a group of science fiction writers and experts including Giulio Raiola, Sandro Sandrelli and Piero Zanotto, joined from the outset by collaborators of the [[Venice Film Festival]] such as Gastone Schiavotto and Flavia Paulon.{{sfn|Cesaro|2024|pp=375–376}} The Trieste festival took place in the climate of the space race: some editions coincided with the 1969 Moon landing, the [[Apollo 15]] mission of 1971 and the [[Apollo–Soyuz|Apollo-Soyuz]] rendezvous of 1975, while science fiction writers such as [[Brian Aldiss]] and [[Arthur C. Clarke]] participated in juries and conferences.{{sfn|Cesaro|2024|p=378}}

Television offered another possibility to see genre films, with a [[RAI]] retrospective dedicated to a selection of science fiction films as early as the early 1960s.<ref name="Fantafestival2009p49" /> On the occasion of the [[Apollo 11]] [[Moon landing]] (1969), [[RAI]] for the first time filled its schedule with science fiction films during the "night of the Moon" and in the days preceding the mission; on the ''Programma Nazionale'' channel it also organized ''25 hours on the Moon'', the first RAI television marathon, following live the different phases of the Moon landing.<ref name="Rossi2014RaiLuna">{{cite web|author=Umberto Rossi|url=https://www.fantascienza.com/19575/nuovi-argomenti-urania-451|title=Nuovi Argomenti: Urania 451|publisher=Delos Books|date=16 December 2014|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="RaiTeche1969Luna">{{cite web|url=https://www.teche.rai.it/2018/07/20-luglio-1969-la-notte-della-luna-2/|title=20 luglio 1969, il lungo speciale della Rai sull'allunaggio|publisher=Rai Teche|date=20 July 2018|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="RaiTeche2021ItaliaLuna">{{cite web|url=https://www.teche.rai.it/2021/07/1969-litalia-vista-dalla-luna-sabato-20-luglio-rai-3/|title=1969 – L'Italia vista dalla Luna|publisher=Rai Teche|date=19 July 2021|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

In the 1970s specialized retrospectives also developed outside Trieste. [[Luigi Cozzi]] and Ugo Malaguti organized in 1975 at the Planetario cinema in Rome a retrospective dedicated exclusively to science fiction cinema; initially planned for two weeks, it lasted three months and was repeated elsewhere in Italy, particularly at the Tevere film club in Rome, an initiative from which the Fantafestival later derived.<ref name="Roncaglia2014Planetario">{{cite web|author=Gino Roncaglia|url=https://www.nuoviargomenti.net/note-sulla-percezione-della-fantascienza-in-italia/|title=Note sulla percezione della fantascienza in Italia|website=Nuovi Argomenti|date=15 December 2014|language=it}}</ref><ref name="Fantafestival2009p49" /> In the capital, the annual aerospace technology exhibition held at the [[Palazzo dei Congressi]] already included screenings of science fiction films.<ref name="Roncaglia2014Planetario" /><ref name="Rossi2014RaiLuna" /> The Trieste festival screenings were interrupted in 1982 for lack of funding; in 2000 La Cappella Underground inherited its legacy by founding the [[Trieste Science+Fiction Festival]], adding conferences, debates and initiatives also dedicated to comics, literature and music to the screenings.{{sfn|Cesaro|2024|pp=375, 378–379}}

== Space opera and science fiction horror between the 1970s and 1980s ==
At the end of the 1970s the success of ''[[Star Wars (film)|Star Wars]]'' (1977) by [[George Lucas]] relaunched the space adventure strand and imposed a [[blockbuster (entertainment)|blockbuster]] model also based on the extensive use of special effects, consolidating the dominance of the United States in this market.<ref name="TreccaniFantascienzaCinema" />

=== Space opera after ''Star Wars'' ===
[[File:StarCrash.jpg|thumb|alt=Scontri stellari oltre la terza dimensione by Luigi Cozzi.|right|''[[Starcrash]]'' (''Scontri stellari oltre la terza dimensione'', 1978) by [[Luigi Cozzi]]]]
[[File:Luigi Cozzi.JPG|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Luigi Cozzi.|[[Luigi Cozzi]], director of ''[[Starcrash]]'' (1978) and ''[[Contamination (film)|Contamination]]'' (1980)]]

In Italy, the revival of space adventure was followed above all by low-budget productions and co-productions also aimed at the international market.<ref name="TreccaniFantascienzaCinema" />{{sfn|Brignoli|2022|pp=129–131}}

Between 1977 and 1980 the director [[Alfonso Brescia]], under the pseudonym Al Bradley, made a series of five low-budget films – ''[[Cosmos: War of the Planets]]'' (''Anno zero – Guerra nello spazio'', 1977), ''Cosmo 2000 – Battaglie negli spazi stellari'' (1978), ''[[War of the Robots (film)|War of the Robots]]'' (''La guerra dei robot'', 1978), ''[[Star Odyssey]]'' (''Sette uomini d'oro nello spazio'', 1979) and ''La bestia nello spazio'' (1980) – building a saga of space adventures in the wake of ''Star Wars'', made by reusing part of the cast, sets and special effects; distributed in the United States and Europe, by 2018 the five films were largely forgotten.<ref name="CinematografoFantafestival2018">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/news/festival/e-ancora-fantafestival-cm881e7z|title=E' ancora FantaFestival|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|date=29 November 2018|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="FantafestivalBrescia2018">{{cite web|url=https://www.fanta-festival.it/programma-2018/|title=Programma 2018|publisher=Fantafestival|year=2018|access-date=24 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CSCBrescia2018">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/il-38-fantafestival-al-cinema-trevi-la-fantascienza-di-alfonso-brescia/|title=Il 38° Fantafestival al Cinema Trevi: la fantascienza di Alfonso Brescia|publisher=Fondazione Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|date=1 December 2018|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> ''Cosmos: War of the Planets'' has also been included among the worst science fiction films, with criticism directed in particular at plot, dialogue and acting.<ref name="SFECosmosWarPlanets2024">{{cite web|url=https://sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/cosmos_war_of_the_planets|title=Cosmos: War of the Planets|publisher=The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction|date=25 November 2024|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref>

The Italian director [[Luigi Cozzi]] made in 1978 (under the name Lewis Coates) ''[[Starcrash]]'' (''Scontri stellari oltre la terza dimensione'', 1978), an Italian-American co-production considered a cult film and publicized, one year after ''Star Wars'', as the Italian response to Lucas's great success; although a low-budget film compared to major Hollywood productions, the cast includes [[Christopher Plummer]].{{sfn|Cvijović|Đorgović|2014|p=59}}<ref name="FantafestivalCozziBio">{{cite web|url=https://www.fanta-festival.it/staff/|title=Staff – Luigi Cozzi|publisher=Fantafestival|access-date=27 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="FutureFilmStarcrash2022">{{cite web|url=https://www.futurefilmfestival.it/it/edizione-2022/starcrash-scontri-stellari-oltre-la-terza-dimensione-2/|title=Starcrash – Scontri stellari oltre la terza dimensione|publisher=Future Film Festival|year=2022|access-date=21 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> Although, because of its title, Cozzi's film has often been seen as a "cheap remake" (or [[camp (style)|camp]]) of ''Star Wars'', the plot has only superficial similarities with Lucas's masterpiece and cites numerous other classics of the genre starting from those of the 1930s and 1940s.<ref name="GuardianStarcrash2020">{{cite web|author=Jordan Hoffman|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2020/apr/13/starcrash-david-hasselhoff-film-amazon-prime|title=My streaming gem: why you should watch Starcrash|website=The Guardian|date=13 April 2020|access-date=24 August 2026|language=en}}</ref><ref name="LocarnoStarcrash2025">{{cite web|author=Giona A. Nazzaro|url=https://letterboxd.com/filmfestlocarno/story/in-some-galaxies-far-far-away-a-cosmic-mixtape/|title=In Some Galaxies Far, Far Away: A Cosmic Mixtape of 12 Films|publisher=Locarno Film Festival|date=5 December 2025|access-date=24 August 2026|language=en}}</ref><ref name="SFEStarcrash2017">{{cite web|url=https://sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/starcrash|title=Starcrash|publisher=The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction|date=19 December 2017|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> Among the recognizable references in the film are ''[[Barbarella (film)|Barbarella]]'', [[Perry Rhodan]] and the [[Flash Gordon]] serials of the 1930s and 1940s, as well as intentional homages to the work of [[Ray Harryhausen]].<ref name="SFEStarcrash2017" /> The film's humor and irony also take up the informal and participatory atmosphere of the science fiction retrospectives organized by Cozzi in the 1970s; ''Starcrash'' has thus been read less as an attempt to exploit ''Star Wars'' than as a way of bringing the experience of those retrospectives to the screen.{{sfn|Pollard|2024|pp=3, 10, 12}} 

''[[The Humanoid (film)|The Humanoid]]'' (''L'umanoide'', 1979), by [[Aldo Lado]], continues the Italian space science fiction strand of the period.<ref name="CSCUmanoide2025">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/la-cineteca-nazionale-collabora-con-il-sciencefiction-festival-di-trieste-per-lomaggio-ad-antonio-margheriti/|title=La Cineteca Nazionale collabora con il Science+Fiction Festival di Trieste per l'omaggio ad Antonio Margheriti|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> In a future following nuclear wars, a scientist searches for the Kappatron, a force capable of transforming human beings into indestructible "humanoids", testing the procedure on a pilot.<ref name="CinematografoUmanoide1979">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/lumanoide-df2c8jit|title=L'umanoide|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> In international productions, [[Dino De Laurentiis]] continued his activity in the fantastic and science fiction by producing ''[[Flash Gordon (film)|Flash Gordon]]'' (1980) and carrying forward the development of ''[[Dune (1984 film)|Dune]]'' (1984) by [[David Lynch]], an American film produced by [[Raffaella De Laurentiis]], after Dino De Laurentiis had purchased the rights in 1979.<ref name="BFIFlashGordonDeLaurentiis2026">{{cite web|url=https://www.bfi.org.uk/resources-events-teachers/resources-teachers/sci-fi-classroom/film-7-flash-gordon-1980|title=Film 7: Flash Gordon (1980)|publisher=British Film Institute|access-date=21 August 2026|language=en}}</ref><ref name="AFIDuneDeLaurentiis2026">{{cite web|url=https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/MovieDetails/67647|title=Dune|publisher=American Film Institute|access-date=21 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> In 2001 the producer also received the [[Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award]], relative to the year 2000.<ref name="OscarsThalbergDeLaurentiis2026">{{cite web|url=https://www.oscars.org/governors-awards/irving-g-thalberg|title=Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award|publisher=Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref>

In 1987 space adventure returned in a production born for television and subsequently re-edited and distributed as a film: [[Antonio Margheriti]] shot for Rai, faithfully following a project by the late [[Renato Castellani]], the television miniseries ''[[Treasure Island in Outer Space]]'' (''L'isola del tesoro'', 1987), a science fiction adaptation of [[Robert Louis Stevenson]]'s novel set in space. Co-produced by Raidue, Bavaria Film and TF1, the miniseries was shot with an international cast.<ref name="RaiTecheIsolaTesoro1987">{{cite web|url=https://www.teche.rai.it/sceneggiati-e-fiction-1986-1989/|title=Sceneggiati e Fiction 1986–1989|publisher=Rai Teche|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="SFETreasureIslandOuterSpace2021">{{cite web|url=https://sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/treasure_island_in_outer_space|title=Treasure Island in Outer Space|publisher=The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction|date=28 April 2021|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> The production had extensive means at its disposal, with a cost of over 25 billion [[Italian lira|lire]] and a considerable production effort supported by Rai,<ref name="Fantafestival2015pp34-35">{{cite web|url=https://www.fanta-festival.it/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/CatalogoFantafestival2015.pdf|title=Catalogo Fantafestival 2015|publisher=Fantafestival|year=2015|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}, pp. 34–35.</ref><ref name="RaiPlayIsolaTesoro1987">{{cite web|url=https://www.raiplay.it/programmi/lisoladeltesoro1987|title=L'isola del tesoro (1987)|publisher=RaiPlay|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> without however achieving the hoped-for success and being judged severely by critics, especially for the narrative rhythm, judged at first too slow and then precipitous; it was nevertheless distributed abroad in versions of different durations and subsequent re-edits.<ref name="Fantafestival2015pp34-35" /><ref name="SFETreasureIslandOuterSpace2021" /><ref name="FilmdienstSpacePirates1996">{{cite web|url=https://www.filmdienst.de/film/details/4578/space-pirates|title=Space Pirates|publisher=Filmdienst|date=13 March 1996|access-date=20 August 2026|language=de}}</ref> The work combines spaceships, laser weapons and androids with elements of a still recognizable past; the android, although belonging to a society born after a war between humans and robots, behaves courageously and altruistically and shows emotions.{{sfn|Bigliardi|2021}}

=== Science fiction horror between foreign models and Italian Gothic ===

[[File:Pupi Avati.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Pupi Avati.|[[Pupi Avati]], director of ''[[Zeder]]'' (1983)]]

Between the late 1970s and early 1980s several Italian science fiction horror films took up already established foreign models, while ''[[Zeder]]'' represented one of the few attempts to develop a specifically Italian Gothic and stood out for originality.<ref name="SFEItaly2026" />{{sfn|Curti|2019|p=9}} Among these models there is also an Italian precedent: ''[[Planet of the Vampires]]'' (''Terrore nello spazio'', 1965) by [[Mario Bava]] has been indicated as an antecedent of ''[[Alien (film)|Alien]]'' (1979), which in turn became the model for ''[[Contamination (film)|Contamination]]''.<ref name="SFEItaly2026" />

''[[Island of the Fishmen]]'' (''L'isola degli uomini pesce'', 1979) is a science fiction horror film directed by [[Sergio Martino]], in which a biologist has created fish-men, amphibious beings employed to recover a submerged treasure of Atlantis; the film seems inspired by ''[[The Island of Dr. Moreau (1977 film)|The Island of Dr. Moreau]]'' (1977) by [[Don Taylor (American filmmaker)|Don Taylor]], a film that proved a failure and was in turn a slow and trite remake of ''[[Island of Lost Souls (1932 film)|Island of Lost Souls]]'' (1932).<ref name="CinematografoIsolaPesce1979">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/lisola-degli-uomini-pesce-egflx8xt|title=L'isola degli uomini pesce|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/isola_degli_uomini_pesce_l|title=Isola degli Uomini Pesce, L'|publisher=The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction|date=24 January 2017|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/island_of_dr_moreau_the|title=Island of Dr Moreau, The|publisher=The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction|date=25 May 2026|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref>

The success of ''Alien'' generated in Italy several attempts to take up its formula.<ref name="SFEContamination2021">{{cite web|url=https://sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/contamination_alien_arriva_sulla_terra|title=Contamination: Alien Arriva Sulla Terra|publisher=The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction|date=14 December 2021|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> [[Luigi Cozzi|Cozzi]] wrote and directed in 1980 his last science fiction film, ''[[Contamination (film)|Contamination]]'' (1980), a science fiction horror that follows the [[alien invasion]] model while building its story out of further references: the opening recalls ''[[Zombi 2]]'', while numerous elements derive from ''[[Quatermass 2]]'' (1957).<ref name="FantasyDayCozzi2023">{{cite web|url=https://www.fantasydayfilmfestival.it/files/catalogo2023.pdf|title=Catalogo Fantasy Day Film Festival 2023|publisher=Fantasy Day Film Festival|year=2023|access-date=21 August 2026|language=it}}, p. 46.</ref><ref name="SFEContamination2021" /><ref name="TriesteContamination2021">{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencefictionfestival.org/film/contamination-alien-arriva-sulla-terra-luigi-cozzi/|title=Contamination – Alien arriva sulla Terra|publisher=Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|date=12 August 2021|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> In the same year ''[[Alien 2: On Earth]]'' (''Alien 2 – Sulla Terra'', 1980), directed by [[Ciro Ippolito]] under the pseudonym Sam Cromwell, is an unofficial sequel made to capitalize on the commercial success of Scott's film, shot with very poor means and characterized by an artisanal and gory approach between science fiction and horror; the film was also accused of plagiarism.<ref name="FondazionePradaAlien2_2026">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazioneprada.org/project/incontro-con-ciro-ippolito/|title=Nocturna – Ciro Ippolito|publisher=Fondazione Prada|date=21 February 2026|access-date=27 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="FilmTVAlien2Plagio">{{cite web|url=https://www.filmtv.it/film/9120/alien-2-sulla-terra/|title=Alien 2. Sulla Terra|publisher=FilmTV|access-date=21 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="ANICAAlien2">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG4448|title=Alien 2 sulla Terra (1980)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

With ''[[Zeder]]'' (1983) [[Pupi Avati]] instead followed a different path: in the science fiction horror, set in [[Emilia-Romagna]], [[alchemy|alchemical]] and [[Western esotericism|esoteric]], [[pseudoscience|pseudoscientific]] and [[Conspiracy fiction|conspiracy film]] elements revolve around a particular type of soil that seems capable of making the dead [[resurrection|resurrect]].<ref name="TriesteZeder2021">{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencefictionfestival.org/film/zeder-pupi-avati/|title=Zeder|publisher=Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|date=11 August 2021|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Curti|2019|p=116}} The title character was modeled on the figure of the alchemist and esotericist [[Fulcanelli]], whose life and works Avati had studied for a previous project.{{sfn|Curti|2019|p=115}} Although featuring the dead returned to life, the film rejects the traditional iconography of zombies and explicit [[splatter film|gore]], privileging suspense, anguish and a conspiracy film atmosphere, while the experiments on the return of the dead are presented in pseudoscientific terms through cameras and monitors, used instead of traditional séances.{{sfn|Curti|2019|pp=117–118}}

== The post-atomic and the new barbarians ==
[[File:EnzoG.Castellari.jpg|thumb|alt=Enzo G. Castellari.|[[Enzo G. Castellari]], director of the trilogy formed by ''[[1990: The Bronx Warriors]]'', ''[[The New Barbarians]]'' and ''[[Escape from the Bronx]]'']]
[[File:Ruggero Deodato Cannes 2008 (cropped).JPG|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Ruggero Deodato at Cannes in 2008.|[[Ruggero Deodato]], director of ''[[The Atlantis Interceptors]]'' (''I predatori di Atlantide'', 1983)]]

In the first half of the 1980s a short cycle of [[apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction|post-apocalyptic]] films developed in Italy, born from the tendency of genre cinema to respond rapidly to international successes and inspired above all by the Australian films ''[[Mad Max (film)|Mad Max]]'' (1979) and ''[[Mad Max 2]]'' (1981), by ''[[Escape from New York]]'' (1981) and by the image of anarchy and violence in metropolitan ghettos proposed by ''[[The Warriors (film)|The Warriors]]'' (1979); the cycle was heterogeneous and included cities devastated by nuclear war and pollution, territories dominated by gangs or authoritarian powers and protagonists who also recalled the tradition of the [[Sword-and-sandal|peplum]].{{sfn|Baschiera|2016|p=7}}{{sfn|Koven|2014|pp=208–209}} The Italian productions transformed abandoned industrial plants and other desolate landscapes of the peninsula into cheap but effective sets to describe, in a regressed civilization, the battles of the last survivors of [[nuclear warfare|atomic war]].<ref name="CinemathequeToulouseNuoviBarbari2020">{{cite web|url=https://www.lacinemathequedetoulouse.com/programmation/projections/32120?from=2020-02-07&to=2020-02-15|title=Les Nouveaux Barbares (I nuovi barbari) – Muséum de Toulouse|publisher=La Cinémathèque de Toulouse|year=2020|access-date=18 August 2026|language=fr}}</ref>{{sfn|Andersson|2017}}

The urban side of the cycle includes the trilogy by [[Enzo G. Castellari]] formed by ''[[1990: The Bronx Warriors]]'' (''1990 – I guerrieri del Bronx'', 1982), ''[[The New Barbarians]]'' (''I nuovi barbari'', 1983)<ref name="ANICANuoviBarbari1983">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG4948|title=I nuovi barbari (1983)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> and ''[[Escape from the Bronx]]'' (''Fuga dal Bronx'', 1983),{{sfn|Baschiera|2016|p=7}}<ref name="CinematografoCastellari2026">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/cast/enzo-g-castellari-l91efwsn|title=Enzo G. Castellari – Enzo Girolami|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> together with ''[[2019, After the Fall of New York]]'' (''2019 – Dopo la caduta di New York'', 1983) by [[Sergio Martino]], also from 1983 and signed by the director under the pseudonym Martin Dolman.<ref name="Cinematografo2019NewYork">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/2019-dopo-la-caduta-di-new-york-kbcfjwjc|title=2019 – Dopo la caduta di New York|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Brioni|Comberiati|2020|p=10}} Among these, ''The New Barbarians'' had American distribution,<ref name="UFNewBarbarians1983">{{cite web|url=https://findingaids.uflib.ufl.edu/repositories/2/archival_objects/293479|title=W-2 – Warriors of the Wasteland – 27 x 41 inch one sheet for the 1983 New Line Cinema production|publisher=Special and Area Studies Collections, George A. Smathers Libraries, University of Florida|year=1983|access-date=27 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> while ''1990: The Bronx Warriors'' had strong success in the United States and remained for weeks in fifth place in the American chart published by ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]''.<ref name="CSCCastellariSuccesso1990">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/cinema-trevi-enzo-g-castellari-l%C2%92architetto-dell%C2%92azione/|title=Cinema Trevi: Enzo G. Castellari, l'architetto dell'azione|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> ''Escape from the Bronx'' had great success in several countries.<ref name="MYmoviesFugaSuccesso2015">{{cite web|author=Marco Chiani|url=https://www.mymovies.it/film/1983/fugadalbronx/|title=Fuga dal Bronx|publisher=MYmovies.it|date=30 March 2015|access-date=25 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

Among the productions of the same period, ''[[Endgame (1983 film)|Endgame]]'' (''Endgame – Bronx lotta finale'', 1983), made by [[Joe D'Amato|Aristide Massaccesi]] under the pseudonym Steven Benson and considered one of the director's most ambitious films, stands out for its ability to fuse different themes; Massaccesi (better known as Joe D'Amato) made it in the phase in which, like other Italian filmmakers, he was taking up major American successes, with ''Escape from New York'' as a direct model.<ref name="TitanusEndgameWeb">{{cite web|url=https://titanus.it/en/progetto/cinema/endgame-bronx-lotta-finale/|title=Endgame – Bronx lotta finale|publisher=Titanus|access-date=24 August 2026|language=en}}</ref><ref name="BiennaleEndgame2021">{{cite web|url=https://www.labiennale.org/it/news/inferno-rosso-joe-d%E2%80%99amato-sulla-dell%E2%80%99eccesso|title=Inferno rosso. Joe D'Amato sulla via dell'eccesso|publisher=La Biennale di Venezia|date=5 September 2021|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="FilmarchivDAmato2019">{{cite web|url=https://info.filmarchiv.at/program/retrospective/tribute-to-joe-damato/|title=Tribute to Joe D'Amato|publisher=Filmarchiv Austria|year=2019|access-date=20 August 2026|language=de}}</ref> Also part of the same strand is ''[[2020 Texas Gladiators]]'' (''Anno 2020 – I gladiatori del futuro'', 1984), credited to Kevin Mancuso (Aristide Massaccesi), while [[George Eastman (actor)|George Eastman]] (Luigi Montefiori) assisted Massaccesi in the direction.<ref name="ChangesAnno2020">{{cite web|url=https://filmcensorship.changes.unimi.it/movies_list.php?id=75939|title=Anno 2020 – I gladiatori del futuro|publisher=Università degli Studi di Milano – CHANGES|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/riflettori/in-memoriam/e-morto-george-eastman-cs6qsqq3|title=È morto George Eastman|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|date=20 May 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> Distributed internationally in 1984 as ''2020 Texas Gladiators,''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.classification.gov.au/classification-ratings/latest-classification-decisions?page=199217|title=Latest classification decisions|publisher=Australian Classification|access-date=28 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> the film is a post-apocalyptic exploitation in which, after a sequence of violence, the heroes kill those responsible as a form of retributive justice.{{sfn|Yar|2015|p=82}}

The strand also includes films that combine the post-atomic with adventure or the [[Western (genre)|western]], or make television control the center of the dystopia.{{sfn|Koven|2014|pp=208–209}}{{sfn|Vella|2025|pp=133–134}} In the same 1983 ''[[The Atlantis Interceptors]]'' (''I predatori di Atlantide'', 1983) by [[Ruggero Deodato]] combines the violent adventure of the strand with an explicit science fiction element: during the recovery of a sunken [[nuclear submarine|Soviet nuclear submarine]], nuclear radiation causes the re-emergence of [[Atlantis]].<ref name="CinematografoPredatoriAtlantide1983">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/i-predatori-di-atlantide-p7cn40dp|title=I predatori di Atlantide|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> ''[[Exterminators of the Year 3000]]'' (''Il giustiziere della strada'', 1983), by [[Giuliano Carnimeo]], is set in the year 3000 and is an apocalyptic dystopia that draws on both the ''[[Mad Max]]'' exploitation films and the [[Spaghetti Western]], replacing horses and pistols with cars and modified weapons.<ref name="FilmotecaEspanola2021pp56-57">{{cite web|url=https://www.cultura.gob.es/dam/jcr%3A048addb1-41f6-4b36-8afb-489bc8de483d/programaci-n-de-septiembre-2021---filmoteca-espa-ola.pdf|title=Programa Cine Doré – septiembre 2021|publisher=Filmoteca Española|date=3 September 2021|access-date=18 August 2026|language=es}}, pp. 56–57.</ref> [[Antonio Margheriti]] also tackled this strand with ''[[Yor, the Hunter from the Future]]'' (''Il mondo di Yor'', 1983), co-produced by [[RAI]] and based on the Argentine comic ''Yor, the Hunter'' by [[Juan Zanotto]] and [[Ray Collins (cartoonist)|Ray Collins]], set in an apparently primitive world marked by an atomic catastrophe, where prehistoric monsters, [[Stone Age]] men, ape-like creatures and members of an almost extinct superior civilization coexist.<ref name="CinematografoYor1983">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/il-mondo-di-yor-d50l1rl6|title=Il mondo di Yor|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> The film is an action and adventure work in which the director mixes different genres.<ref name="CSC2013SpaceMen" /> The theatrical version was distributed in the United States by RCA Columbia and entered the top ten of the American box office chart.<ref name="CSC2013SpaceMen" /> The prehistoric monsters were built life-size and animated by operators hidden inside them.<ref name="FantafestivalYor2015">{{cite web|url=https://www.fanta-festival.it/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/CatalogoFantafestival2015.pdf|title=Catalogo Fantafestival 2015|publisher=Fantafestival|year=2015|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}, p. 36.</ref>

[[Lucio Fulci]], with ''[[Warriors of the Year 2072]]'' (''I guerrieri dell'anno 2072'', 1983), presents instead a future society controlled by [[television]], in which the main networks fight by any means to dominate ratings, willing to organize a ruthless fight between [[gladiator]]s to entertain the public.<ref name="ANICAGuerrieri2072">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG5064|title=I guerrieri dell'anno 2072 (1983)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=21 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CinematografoGuerrieri2072">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/i-guerrieri-dellanno-2072-r6anygyb|title=I guerrieri dell'anno 2072|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=21 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> The film stands out from much of the cycle because it does not start from a nuclear war and places the dystopia in a future Rome rather than in the United States; the televised [[gladiator]]ial competition has been read as a critique of the power of large television groups, of [[authoritarianism]] and of the political and economic transformations of 1980s Italy.{{sfn|Vella|2025|pp=133–134}}

== The second half of the 1980s and the crisis ==
