[[File:Giuliano Montaldo - 2012.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Giuliano Montaldo in 2012.|[[Giuliano Montaldo]], director of ''[[Control (1987 film)|Control]]'' (''Il giorno prima'', 1987)]]

In the second half of the 1980s Italian action science fiction developed while genre cinema was going through a wider crisis, with reduced means, few American models of reference and a growing weight of television and [[home video]].<ref name="CSC2018LastActionHeroes">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/last-action-heroes-il-cinema-italiano-d%C2%92azione-degli-anni-80/|title=Last Action Heroes. Il cinema italiano d'azione degli anni 80|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|date=18 September 2018|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Baschiera|2016|pp=19–21}} In these years the international success of ''[[The Terminator]]'' and ''[[RoboCop]]'' fueled a series of low- and very low-budget films centered on [[android (robot)|androids]], [[cyborg]]s and [[time travel]].{{sfn|Del Santo|2010}}<ref name="CSC2018LastActionHeroes" /> In ''[[Vendetta dal futuro]]'' (internationally released as ''Hands of Steel'', 1986) by [[Sergio Martino]] the protagonist is rebuilt with steel and electronic components, programmed to kill but still capable of retaining human traits;<ref name="ANICAVendettaFuturo1986">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=AG5303|title=Vendetta dal futuro (1986)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="CinematografoVendettaFuturo1986">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/vendetta-dal-futuro-x8eh8c4l|title=Vendetta dal futuro|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> in ''[[Robowar (film)|Robowar]]'' (''Robowar – Robot da guerra'', 1988) [[Bruno Mattei]] wanted instead to fuse elements of ''[[Predator (film)|Predator]]'' and ''RoboCop'',<ref name="SitgesDrudiRobowar2025">{{cite web|url=https://sitgesfilmfestival.com/en/logbook/we-remember-rossella-drudi|title=We remember Rossella Drudi|publisher=Sitges Film Festival|date=20 February 2025|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> while ''[[Cyborg - Il guerriero d'acciaio]]'' (1989) by [[Giannetto De Rossi]] has an android as its protagonist.<ref name="ANICACyborg1989">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=DD8603|title=Cyborg, il guerriero d'acciaio (1989)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

In the same period ''[[Control (1987 film)|Control]]'' (''Il giorno prima'', 1987) by [[Giuliano Montaldo]] instead tackled the nuclear threat through an experiment on human reactions: fifteen volunteers are locked for twenty days in a nuclear fallout shelter, where forced coexistence puts their physical and psychological reactions to the test.<ref name="CinematografoGiornoPrima1987">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/il-giorno-prima-j7vekgry|title=Il giorno prima|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="MuseoCinemaGiornoPrima2018">{{cite web|url=https://www.museocinema.it/it/news/6504|title=Il 17° gLocal Film Festival di Piemonte Movie è anche in Bibliomediateca con due serate in omaggio a Flavio Bucci e a Pit Formento|publisher=Museo Nazionale del Cinema|year=2018|access-date=31 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> Conceived and written by [[Piero Angela]], the film builds the experiment around the behavior of a representative sample of society in conditions of isolation.<ref name="MuseoCinemaGiornoPrima2018" />

Towards the end of the decade Italian genre production progressively lost momentum: the crisis of theaters and the new role of television networks changed the production system, while low-budget films faced growing competition and an increasingly wide technical gap compared to major American productions.{{sfn|Baschiera|2016|pp=19–21}} The 1980s closed with ''Alien from the Deep'' (''Alien degli abissi'', 1989), the last dramatic science fiction film directed by [[Antonio Margheriti]] and a science fiction horror with [[environmentalism|ecologist]] themes: the threat to Earth this time arises from polluting human activities, with a company dumping nuclear waste into a volcano and attracting an alien creature with the radioactivity.<ref name="ANICAAlienAbissi1989">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=DD8572|title=Alien degli abissi (1989)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=18 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Bigliardi|2021}} The film also follows the model of ''[[Alien (film)|Alien]]'', especially in the idea of the monster and in the echo of the titles, while the director's projects for other films to be made in the 1990s remained unrealized due to the crisis that hit the sector.{{sfn|Donda|2009–2010|p=105}}<ref name="Margheriti-Alien">{{cite web|url=http://www.antoniomargheriti.com/Tutti_i_suoi_Film/fantascienza/Alien.htm|title=Alien degli abissi|website=Antoniomargheriti.com|access-date=24 October 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110207043630/http://www.antoniomargheriti.com/tutti_i_suoi_film/Fantascienza/Alien.htm|language=it|archive-date=7 February 2011}}</ref>

== The 1990s ==
[[File:Carlo Rambaldi al Giffoni Film Festival 2010 - cropped.jpg|thumb|alt=Carlo Rambaldi at the Giffoni Film Festival 2010.|The special effects creator three-time [[Academy Award for Best Visual Effects|Academy Award winner]] [[Carlo Rambaldi]] ([[Giffoni Film Festival]] 2010)]]
[[File:Gabriele Salvatores - Lucca Comics & Games 2014.JPG|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Gabriele Salvatores in 2014.|[[Gabriele Salvatores]], director of ''[[Nirvana (1997 film)|Nirvana]]'' (1997)]]

In the 1990s the tendency, developed in the previous decade, to make Italian science fiction films destined for the international public came to an end;{{sfn|Malvestio|2025|p=187}} in the now much reduced production, comedy and farce aimed at the domestic market continued above all; in this context ''[[Nirvana (1997 film)|Nirvana]]'' (1997) by [[Gabriele Salvatores]] stands out clearly, the most notable exception of the decade.<ref name="Baccolini2014CRIS">{{cite web|author=Raffaella Baccolini|url=https://cris.unibo.it/handle/11585/317114|title=The Uncomfortable Relationship Between Science Fiction and Italy: Film, Humor, and Gender|publisher=Alma Mater Studiorum – Università di Bologna|year=2014|access-date=31 August 2026|language=en}}</ref>

Among the comedies, ''[[A spasso nel tempo]]'' (1996) by [[Carlo Vanzina]] is a 1996 "[[cinepanettone]]" that uses [[time travel]] as the engine of comic situations{{sfn|O'Leary|2011|p=433}}<ref name="Cinematografo2026ASpassoNelTempo">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/a-spasso-nel-tempo-puy94cfa|title=A spasso nel tempo|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> and achieved strong success on the Italian market.<ref name="MiBACTFUS1999Incassi">{{cite web|url=https://spettacolo.cultura.gov.it/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Relazione-FUS-1999.pdf|title=Relazione sulla Utilizzazione del Fondo Unico dello Spettacolo 1999|publisher=Ministero per i Beni e le Attività Culturali|year=1999|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}, pp. 109–110. The report specifies that the contribution was equal to 13% of the box office gross achieved in the two years following the first screening; the table shows 5,003.3 million lire for ''A spasso nel tempo'' and 1,962.9 million for ''Nirvana''.</ref> In 1997 Vanzina directed its sequel ''[[A spasso nel tempo – L'avventura continua|A spasso nel tempo – L'avventura continua]]'' (1997), which keeps the same protagonists, structure and narrative tone, maintaining the time machine breakdown as the engine of the story.<ref name="Cinematografo2026ASpassoSeguito">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/a-spasso-nel-tempo-lavventura-continua-yvyv890z|title=A spasso nel tempo – L'avventura continua|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> At the end of the decade, the comedy ''[[Fantozzi 2000 – La clonazione|Fantozzi 2000 – La clonazione]]'' (1999) by [[Domenico Saverni]] brings the protagonist back to life through a cloning procedure and ends with the encounter with a Martian.<ref name="CinematografoFantozzi2000">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/fantozzi-2000-la-clonazione-ymbvjmnb|title=Fantozzi 2000 – La clonazione|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

Among the science fiction productions of the decade, ''Nirvana'' has been defined as the swan song of the genre.{{sfn|Malvestio|2025|p=187}} It is an Italian-French co-production with an international cast,<ref name="CannesNirvana1997">{{cite web|url=https://www.festival-cannes.com/en/f/nirvana/|title=Nirvana|publisher=Festival de Cannes|year=1997|access-date=19 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> characterized by the massive use of [[computer-generated imagery|computer-generated special effects]].<ref name="CSCNirvana2014">{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionecsc.it/evento/le-eroine-del-cinema-fantastico-italiano/|title=Le eroine del cinema fantastico italiano|publisher=Centro Sperimentale di Cinematografia|year=2014|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> Set in a near future and shot almost entirely in the [[Portello (district of Milan)|Portello]] district of Milan, in the old [[Alfa Romeo Portello Plant|Alfa Romeo factories]] transformed for the occasion into a gigantic film set, the film presents atmospheres of urban decay that recall those of ''[[Blade Runner]]'' (1982) by [[Ridley Scott]] and combines typical elements of [[cyberpunk]] – [[hacker]]s as protagonists, the domination of [[zaibatsu|mega-corporations]], the degraded [[urban sprawl|sprawl]]-periphery and [[cyberspace]] – with themes of [[Buddhism|Buddhist]] philosophy.{{sfn|Tabanelli|2015|pp=35–36, 38–39}}{{sfn|Chiavini|Pizzo|Tetro|2001|p=124}} The protagonist, played by [[Christopher Lambert]], is a successful [[video game]] programmer of [[virtual reality]] who discovers how, through a [[computer virus|virus]], the character of his latest game, played by [[Diego Abatantuono]], has acquired self-awareness; aware of being a prisoner of a life-death cycle in which he is condemned to repeat every action endlessly, the character begs the programmer to free him by deleting all copies of the video game, while the search unfolds in the most degraded peripheries and leads the protagonist back on the trail of the beloved woman he had lost.{{sfn|Tabanelli|2015|pp=37, 40}}{{sfn|Chiavini|Pizzo|Tetro|2001|p=55}} Although a science fiction film, ''Nirvana'' returns to motifs that recur in Salvatores's cinema, especially escape and male friendship, linking them to the gap between rich and poor areas and to the achievement of self-awareness.{{sfn|Orsitto|2007–2008|p=65}} The film achieved considerable success both in Italy and abroad, while critics were divided, appreciating the ambition to tackle the fantastic, the scenographic spaces, color and camera movements but criticizing the gap between voluntarism and inspiration and the way in which the narrative materials were organized, with other judgments that underlined its spectacularity, involvement and the originality with which it reworked suggestions drawn from cybernetic literature and essays.<ref name="CinematografoNirvanaCritica2026">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/nirvana-q0txxk2o|title=Nirvana|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> ''Nirvana'' was Salvatores's greatest commercial success<ref name="CSCNirvana2014" /> and has been described as the greatest audience success in the history of Italian science fiction cinema.<ref name="TriesteNirvanaSuccesso2013">{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencefictionfestival.org/gabriele-salvatores-urania-dargento-2013/|title=Gabriele Salvatores Urania d'Argento 2013|publisher=Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|date=30 September 2013|access-date=21 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

In the decade other films were released, without the previous production aimed at international markets returning.{{sfn|Malvestio|2025|p=187}} ''[[Jackpot (1992 film)|Jackpot]]'' (1992) by [[Mario Orfini]] proved instead to be a costly failure;{{sfn|Marzaduri|2020}} built as an anti-technological fable, favorable to a return to nature, it was harshly panned by critics<ref name="CinematografoJackpot1992">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/jackpot-ny70fhgt|title=Jackpot|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> and remained the last cinematic appearance of [[Adriano Celentano]].<ref name="CinematografoCelentano2026">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/cast/adriano-celentano-rnd6v9hu|title=Adriano Celentano|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> [[Antonio Margheriti]] returned one last time as director in 1997 with ''[[Virtual Weapon]]'' (''Potenza virtuale'', 1997),<ref name="FilmTVMargheritiPotenza2026">{{cite web|url=https://www.filmtv.it/persona/2014/anthony-m-dawson-antonio-margheriti/|title=Anthony M. Dawson (Antonio Margheriti)|publisher=FilmTV.it|access-date=21 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> a science fiction and crime comedy in which a detective investigates a criminal network that uses explosives activated by ultrasound and, after an attack, survives in holographic form through a computer.{{sfn|Bigliardi|2021|p=6 del PDF}}

== The 2000s ==
In the 2000s independent productions and those made by fans gained prominence, some of which achieved high quality; in the same period comedy and farce aimed mainly at the domestic market continued and, in some cases, humor also served to criticize contemporary Italian politics.{{sfn|Rushing|2015|p=339}}<ref name="Baccolini2014CRIS" />

=== Independent productions and digital ===
[[File:Genova-Massimo Morini Astronauta in Invaxön.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Massimo Morini in an astronaut costume.|Massimo Morini on the set of ''InvaXön – Alieni in Liguria'' (2004)]]

Digital technologies made it possible to contain some production costs and expanded the ways of distributing and viewing films, including through home video and the internet, offering new possibilities to productions made with reduced means.{{sfn|Mastroddi|2008|pp=67, 150}} Among the independent experiences started already at the end of the 1990s was the work of Mariano Equizzi: short films such as ''Syrena'' (1998) and ''AgentZ'' (2000) are very low-cost products, recall cyberpunk and use technologies in an alternative way also as a stylistic choice.{{sfn|Bazzichelli|2008|pp=84–85}}

A production based largely on the free contribution of participants is ''InvaXön – Alieni in Liguria'' (2004) by Massimo Morini and Enzo Pirrone, made for charity in favor of the prevention of fragile X syndrome;{{sfn|Zorzoli|2006|p=25}} 250 non-professional actors, 41,000 extras and 23 personalities from the world of entertainment, sports and culture participated.<ref name="ANICAInvaxon2004">{{cite web|url=https://www.archiviodelcinemaitaliano.it/index.php/scheda.html?codice=FI7524|title=Invaxon – Alieni in Liguria (2004)|publisher=ANICA|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="FantascienzaInvaxon2004">{{cite web|url=https://www.fantascienza.com/5345/invaxon-quando-gli-alieni-atterrano-in-liguria|title=Invaxön, quando gli alieni atterrano in Liguria|publisher=Fantascienza.com|date=15 December 2004|access-date=24 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> The film was made with digital special effects, [[surround sound|surround]] audio and [[THX]] certification, while the processing required seven years of planning, sixty days of shooting and 4,000 hours of work, also relying on the free contribution of participants and on a deliberately "homemade" approach, without the pretension of making a film on the model of ''Star Wars''.<ref name="DiesisInvaxon2004">{{cite web|url=https://www.diesis.it/elenco-articoli/?c=marinastudios|title=InvaXön, il film ligure sugli extraterrestri, da film amatoriale a Dolby Digital e certificazione THX grazie a Marinastudios|publisher=Diesis|date=10 December 2004|access-date=24 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Zorzoli|2006|pp=25–26}}

Other projects reached the public without going through theaters: ''AD Project'' by [[Eros Puglielli]] arrived on [[home video]] in May 2006,<ref name="Prudenzi2006ADProject">{{cite web|author=Angela Prudenzi|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/news/puglielli-sperimentale-k3bej1dy|title=Puglielli sperimentale|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|date=15 March 2006|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="Cinematografo2024ADProject">{{cite web|author=Giulia Lucchini|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/riflettori/cortina-express-lomaggio-al-cinepanettone-di-eros-puglielli-x9t14t2p|title=Cortina Express, l'omaggio al cinepanettone di Eros Puglielli|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|date=19 December 2024|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> while ''Dark Resurrection – Volume 1'' (2007) and the prequel ''Dark Resurrection – Volume 0'' (2011) by Angelo Licata were made for the web and were part of the growth of independent and fan-made productions in the same years.{{sfn|Della Rocca|2020|p=13}}{{sfn|Rushing|2015|p=339}} The two amateur [[fan fiction]]s inspired by the [[Star Wars]] universe involved a production effort comparable to or greater than that of independent films distributed in theaters, also including mass battle scenes made with the contribution of hundreds of volunteers in [[cosplay|costume]].<ref name="DeAndreisDarkResurrection">{{cite web|author=Paolo De Andreis|url=https://xl.repubblica.it/dettaglio/44261.html|title=Dark Resurrection|publisher=la Repubblica XL|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://tentaciones.elpais.com/2011/11/dark-resurrection.html|author=Tommaso Koch|title='Dark Resurrection', o cómo un dentista italiano ha reinventado 'La guerra de las galaxias'|publisher=[[El País]]|date=22 November 2011|access-date=19 December 2013|language=es}}</ref> In 2011 independent productions also included ''[[The Last Man on Earth (2011 film)|The Last Man on Earth]]'' (''L'ultimo terrestre'', 2011) and ''[[The Arrival of Wang]]'' (''L'arrivo di Wang'', 2011).{{sfn|Rushing|2015|p=339}}

=== Comedy and political satire ===
[[File:FascistisuMarte.jpg|thumb|alt=Fascisti su Marte.|''[[Fascisti su Marte]]'' (internationally released as ''Fascists on Mars'', 2006)]]

Comedy and farce continued to be recurring forms of Italian science fiction aimed mainly at the domestic market; ''[[Fascisti su Marte]]'' (2006) relies on humor also to criticize Italian politics.<ref name="Baccolini2014CRIS" /> The film, directed by [[Corrado Guzzanti]] and [[Igor Skofic]], originates from the [[sketch comedy|sketches]] made by Guzzanti for the satirical television program ''Il caso Scafroglia'' on [[Rai 3]].<ref name="RaiTecheScafroglia2021">{{cite web|url=https://www.teche.rai.it/2021/11/corrado-guzzanti-e-il-caso-scafroglia/|title=Corrado Guzzanti e Il caso Scafroglia|publisher=Rai Teche|date=26 November 2021|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> It imagines an expedition of [[Blackshirts|Black Shirts]] to the red planet and, parodying the style of the [[newsreel]]s of the [[Istituto Luce]] of the [[Italian fascism|fascist twenty years]], proposes a [[science fiction|fanta]]-[[historical revisionism|historical revisionism]] that also concerns Italian politics during the [[Second Berlusconi government]].<ref name="FilmItaliaFascisti2006">{{cite web|url=https://filmitalia.org/it/film/37740/|title=Fascisti su Marte|publisher=Cinecittà|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>{{sfn|Jurišić|2011|p=136}}

''[[2061: An Exceptional Year]]'' (''2061 – Un anno eccezionale'', 2007) by [[Carlo Vanzina]] brings the satire of the present into a post-apocalyptic scenario and follows a ramshackle group of patriots who set off from Sicily in an attempt to reunify the peninsula.<ref name="Cinematografo2061">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/2061-un-anno-eccezionale-n8ldiny1|title=2061 – Un anno eccezionale|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> The film is among the few examples of Italian dystopian cinema in comic tones: the depletion of oil resources leads to the disintegration of Italy into several states and brings out separatisms and local rivalries, through which the film also represents the fragility of central institutions.<ref name="Unicatt2061">{{cite web|url=https://ricerca.unicatt.it/uc/atlantedistopiemediali/it/atlante/europe/film/2061---un-anno-eccezionale.html|title=2061 – Un anno eccezionale|publisher=Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore – Atlante delle distopie mediali|access-date=31 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

== From the 2010s ==
From the 2010s Italian science fiction developed in very different forms – [[dystopia]]s, eco-dystopias, [[alternate history|uchronias]] and [[apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction|post-catastrophic]] narratives – addressing the relationships between human beings, technology and the environment; in the same period the genre spread through different media and addressed an audience already accustomed to its mechanisms especially thanks to television series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://presses-universitaires.parisnanterre.fr/index.php/produit/narrativa-n-43-la-fantascienza-nelle-narrazioni-italiane-ipercontemporanee/|title=Narrativa n. 43. La fantascienza nelle narrazioni italiane ipercontemporanee|publisher=Presses universitaires de Paris Nanterre|year=2021|access-date=20 August 2026|language=fr}}</ref>{{sfn|Comberiati|Somigli|2021|p=16}} In cinema, films rework superhero models, recount contemporary social tensions through the encounter with the alien, imagine eco-dystopias and address the way in which technology and control affect individual life.{{sfn|Busi Rizzi|Di Paola|Dal Canto|2024|p=120}}{{sfn|Malvestio|2021|pp=32–33}}{{sfn|Comberiati|Somigli|2021|p=16}}

=== Superheroes and comics ===
[[File:Gabriele Mainetti, September 2017.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Gabriele Mainetti in 2017.|[[Gabriele Mainetti]], director of ''Lo chiamavano Jeeg Robot'' (2016)]]

In Italian superhero films of the 2010s, American models are joined by international references and Italian settings; superpowers are also linked to fears and problems of contemporary Italy.<ref name="Rushing2020Supereroi">{{cite web|author=Robert A. Rushing|url=https://intellectdiscover.com/content/journals/10.1386/jicms_00004_1|title=Italian transnational masculinity: Jeeg Robot, Il ragazzo invisibile and MilzaMan|publisher=Intellect|date=1 January 2020|access-date=31 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> Among these are ''[[The Invisible Boy (2014 film)|The Invisible Boy]]'' (''Il ragazzo invisibile'', 2014) and its sequel, ''[[They Call Me Jeeg]]'' (''Lo chiamavano Jeeg Robot'', 2016) and ''[[Freaks Out]]'' (2021), which take up models and themes close to superhero cinema and comics.{{sfn|Busi Rizzi|Di Paola|Dal Canto|2024|p=120}} Seventeen years after ''[[Nirvana (1997 film)|Nirvana]]'' (1997), [[Gabriele Salvatores]] returned to science fiction with ''Il ragazzo invisibile'' (2014), addressing a teenage audience and choosing a superhero story;<ref name="RaiNewsRagazzoInvisibile2014">{{cite web|url=https://www.rainews.it/archivio-rainews/articoli/ContentItem-7116ff1a-79ec-407a-a14a-8b2fbeaefee0.html|title=Gabriele Salvatores presenta "Il ragazzo invisibile", primo film italiano sui supereroi|publisher=Rai News|date=1 December 2014|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> the film achieved a public success below expectations{{sfn|Venturelli|2015|p=35}} and four years later had a sequel, ''[[The Invisible Boy: Second Generation]]'' (''Il ragazzo invisibile – Seconda generazione'', 2018).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://filmitalia.org/it/film/91845/|title=Il ragazzo invisibile – Seconda generazione|publisher=Cinecittà – Filmitalia|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

With ''Lo chiamavano Jeeg Robot'' (2016), the debut film of [[Gabriele Mainetti]], the superhero model arrives in the Roman periphery: a small-time criminal comes into contact with a radioactive substance and acquires superhuman strength, while a girl believes he is the hero of a cartoon.<ref name="FilmitaliaJeeg2016">{{cite web|url=https://filmitalia.org/it/film/75880/|title=Lo chiamavano Jeeg Robot|publisher=Cinecittà – Filmitalia|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> Taking up themes and stereotypes of the American superhero, the film adapts them to contemporary Italy and combines entertainment with social criticism, setting the story from the outset in a recognizable Rome marked by references to mafia massacres and terrorist attacks, while the suburb and social condition accompany the protagonist's passage from marginality to responsibility towards others.{{sfn|Palladino|2021|pp=259–261}}{{sfn|Brioni|Comberiati|2020|pp=73–76}} Mixing Italian science fiction, Japanese anime and American superhero films, the film addresses different audiences by age and cultural interests and achieves notable public and critical success, with almost 5 million euros at the box office, seven [[David di Donatello]] and two [[Nastro d'Argento|Silver Ribbons]].{{sfn|Comberiati|Somigli|2021|p=16}}<ref name="CinematografoJeegSuccesso2016">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/news/homevideo/lo-chiamavano-jeeg-robot-in-homevideo-e1y87h8g|title=Lo chiamavano Jeeg Robot in homevideo|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|date=12 July 2016|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.daviddidonatello.it/motore-di-ricerca/schedaanno.php?anno=2016|title=Vincitori Premi David di Donatello 2016|publisher=Accademia del Cinema Italiano – Premi David di Donatello|year=2016|access-date=17 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

With ''Freaks Out'' (2021) Mainetti returns to characters endowed with powers, this time setting them in occupied Rome of 1943; the setting, the characters and the language distinguish the film from American models and strengthen its Italian character.<ref>{{cite web|author=Anna Cortelazzo|url=https://ilbolive.unipd.it/it/news/cultura/freaks-out-perturbante-doppio-taglio|title=Freaks out e il perturbante a doppio taglio|publisher=Università degli Studi di Padova – Il Bo Live|date=13 September 2021|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

=== The alien between crisis and peripheries ===
[[File:Manetti Bros Venezia.jpg|thumb|alt=The Manetti Bros. in Venice.|The [[Manetti Bros.]], directors of ''[[The Arrival of Wang]]'' (''L'arrivo di Wang'', 2011)]]

In some films of the 2010s the encounter with the [[extraterrestrials in fiction|alien]] takes place in contemporary Italy and is linked to the economic crisis, fears connected to [[Immigration to Italy|immigration]] and the conditions of the peripheries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencefictionfestival.org/en/film/lultimo-terrestre/|title=L'ultimo terrestre|publisher=Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|date=19 April 2024|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref><ref name="SFEArrivoWang2016">{{cite web|url=https://sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/arrivo_di_wang_l|title=Arrivo di Wang, L'|publisher=The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction|date=7 December 2016|access-date=28 August 2026|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionefarecinema.it/2024/07/09/giovedi-1-agosto-la-guerra-del-tiburtino-iii/|title=La guerra del Tiburtino III|publisher=Fondazione Fare Cinema|date=9 July 2024|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> In ''[[The Last Man on Earth (2011 film)|The Last Man on Earth]]'' (''L'ultimo terrestre'', 2011) by [[Gipi]] the arrival of extraterrestrials takes place in a tired and disillusioned country, in the midst of a severe economic crisis, but the collective event remains in the background while the story focuses on the loneliness and relational difficulties of the protagonist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencefictionfestival.org/en/film/lultimo-terrestre/|title=L'ultimo terrestre|publisher=Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|date=19 April 2024|access-date=20 August 2026|language=en}}</ref> In the same year, in ''[[The Arrival of Wang]]'' (''L'arrivo di Wang'', 2011) by the [[Manetti Bros.]], a secret service agent interrogates with the help of an interpreter an alien who speaks Chinese; the film asks whether humanitarian principles can be applied to a non-human being and recalls fears linked to immigration.<ref name="SFEArrivoWang2016" /> In 2023 ''La guerra del Tiburtino III'' (2023) by Luna Gualano instead brings the alien invasion to the extreme Roman periphery and makes it the means to recount in a paradoxical way inclusion, marginalization and isolation of the neighborhood.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fondazionefarecinema.it/2024/07/09/giovedi-1-agosto-la-guerra-del-tiburtino-iii/|title=La guerra del Tiburtino III|publisher=Fondazione Fare Cinema|date=9 July 2024|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

=== Eco-dystopias and the crisis of the present ===
[[File:Paolo Virzì.JPG|thumb|upright=0.8|alt=Paolo Virzì.|[[Paolo Virzì]], director of ''[[Dry (2022 film)|Dry]]'' (''Siccità'', 2022)]]

Eco-[[dystopia]]s combine post-apocalyptic and dystopian elements to imagine the consequences of the environmental crisis, starting from problems already present and taking them to the extreme until describing credibly worse living conditions.{{sfn|Malvestio|2021|pp=32–33}} ''[[Mondocane]]'' (2021) by [[Alessandro Celli]] is set in a contaminated [[Taranto]] that recalls the situation of the former [[Ilva (company)|Ilva]] and recounts through science fiction the environmental and social degradation.<ref name="Landron2025MondocaneAnna">{{harvnb|Landron|2025|pp=252, 255–256}} Landron puts the film in parallel with the miniseries ''[[Anna (Italian TV series)|Anna]]'' (2021): both are set in southern post-apocalyptic societies populated by children and adolescents without points of reference.</ref><ref name="CinematografoMondocane2026">{{cite web|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/film/mondocane-xi3w55v4|title=Mondocane|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|access-date=21 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

''[[Dry (2022 film)|Dry]]'' (''Siccità'', 2022) by [[Paolo Virzì]] also brings the science fiction scenario close to the present: the Rome where it has not rained for years mixes post-apocalyptic elements and contemporary problems; presenting the climate emergency as a daily condition, the film highlights generational conflicts, political inadequacy and the need to rebuild a community.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://site.unibo.it/multicampus-sostenibile/it/agenda/il-nastro-verde-2024|title=Il Nastro Verde 2024|publisher=Università di Bologna|year=2024|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Telmo Pievani|url=https://ilbolive.unipd.it/en/node/15334|title=L'editoriale. Destini incrociati nella Roma della siccità|publisher=Università degli Studi di Padova – Il Bo Live|date=3 October 2022|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

=== Control, technology and identity ===
Other films of the period show technology as a tool of political or institutional control, as part of the [[Digital transformation|digitalization]] of daily life and as a means to intervene on [[consciousness]] and [[memory]].{{sfn|Comberiati|Somigli|2021|p=16}}<ref name="Cinematografo2047Critica2014">{{cite web|author=Gianfrancesco Iacono|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/recensioni/2047-sights-of-death-puv8r18d|title=2047 – Sights of Death|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|date=23 July 2014|access-date=31 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="UnicattIpersonnia2026">{{cite web|url=https://ricerca.unicatt.it/uc/atlantedistopiemediali/it/atlante/europe/film/ipersonnia.html|title=Ipersonnia|publisher=Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore – Atlante delle distopie mediali|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="FilmitaliaAnotherEnd2026">{{cite web|url=https://filmitalia.org/it/film/176395/|title=Another end|publisher=Cinecittà – Filmitalia|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref>

In 2014 [[Alessandro Capone (director)|Alessandro Capone]] made ''[[2047 - Sights of Death]]'' (2014), a homage to 1980s action cinema with an international cast including [[Danny Glover]], [[Daryl Hannah]], [[Michael Madsen]], [[Stephen Baldwin]] and [[Rutger Hauer]]; written, produced and shot in Italy, it was presented in the original English version and also distributed abroad as a genre production aimed at the international market, openly modeled on American science fiction.<ref name="Trieste2047Omaggio2014">{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencefictionfestival.org/fucili-a-pompa-racchette-da-ping-pong-navicelle-extraterrestri-e-urla-perfette/|title=Fucili a pompa, racchette da ping pong, navicelle extraterrestri e urla perfette|publisher=Trieste Science+Fiction Festival|date=1 November 2014|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="Filmitalia2047">{{cite web|url=https://filmitalia.org/it/film/79054/|title=2047. Sights of Death|publisher=Cinecittà – Filmitalia|access-date=19 August 2026|language=it}}</ref><ref name="Cinematografo2047Critica2014" /> The film is set in a dystopian future dominated by a repressive government, against which a rebel agent acts.<ref name="Trieste2047Omaggio2014" /><ref name="Filmitalia2047" />

''[[Hypersomnia]]'' (''Ipersonnia'', 2022) by Alberto Mascia imagines in a near future a penitentiary system that addresses overcrowding, worsening conditions of prisoners and difficulties of reintegration by keeping the convicted in deep sleep for the entire sentence.<ref name="UnicattIpersonnia2026" /> ''Il migliore dei mondi'' (2023) by [[Maccio Capatonda|Marcello Macchia]], Danilo Carlani and Alessio Dogana instead recounts in the form of comedy the complete digitalization of daily life, making a technology-dependent man fall into an alternative 2023 that has remained stuck in the 1990s.<ref>{{cite web|author=Lorenzo Ciofani|url=https://www.cinematografo.it/recensioni/il-migliore-dei-mondi-xxtgslyb|title=Il migliore dei mondi|publisher=Fondazione Ente dello Spettacolo|date=17 November 2023|access-date=20 August 2026|language=it}}</ref> ''[[Another End]]'' (2024) by [[Piero Messina (director)|Piero Messina]], finally, speaks of identity and [[mourning]] through a technology capable of transferring for a short time the consciousness of a dead person into the body of another and thus offering the living a limited time to face separation.<ref name="FilmitaliaAnotherEnd2026" />

======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: List of dystopian films
======================================================================

{{Short description|None}}
{{distinguish|List of apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2020}}
This is a '''list of [[Dystopian film genre|dystopian films]]'''. [[Dystopia|Dystopian societies]] appear in many speculative fiction works and are often found within the science fiction and fantasy genres.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duque |first=Isabel |title=LibGuides: Dystopias & Utopias: Dystopias |url=https://libraryguides.mdc.edu/c.php?g=957851&p=6914808 |access-date=2022-09-14 |website=libraryguides.mdc.edu |language=en}}</ref> ''Dystopias'' are often characterized by [[dehumanization]],<ref name="Merriam">{{cite web|work=Merriam-Webster|publisher=Merriam-Webster, Inc.|title=Definition of "dystopia"|year=2012|url=http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/dystopia}}</ref> [[Authoritarianism|authoritarian]] governments, ruthless [[megacorporation]]s, [[environmental disaster]]s,<ref name="Oxford">{{cite web|work=Oxford Dictionaries|publisher=Oxford University Press|title=Definition of "dystopia"|year=2012|url=http://oxforddictionaries.com/definition/english/dystopia?q=dystopia|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130514124830/http://oxforddictionaries.com/definition/english/dystopia?q=dystopia|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 May 2013}}</ref> or other characteristics associated with a dramatic decline in society.

| ''[[The World, the Flesh and the Devil (1959 film)|The World, the Flesh and the Devil]]''
| 1959

======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: List of film noir titles
======================================================================

{{Short description|Film genre list}}
{{lists of films}}

[[Film noir]] is not a clearly defined [[genre]] (see [[film noir|here]] for details on the characteristics). Therefore, the composition of this list may be controversial. To minimize dispute the films included here should preferably feature a footnote linking to a [[WP:RS|reliable, published source]] which states that the mentioned film is considered to be a film noir by an expert in this field, e.g.{{listref|a}}{{listref|b}}{{listref|c}}{{listref|d}}

The terms which are used below to subsume various periods and variations of film noir are not definitive and are meant as a navigational aid rather than as critical argument. Because the 1940s and 1950s are universally regarded as the "classic period" of American film noir, films released prior to 1940 are listed under the caption "Precursors / early noir-like films". Films released after 1959 should generally only be listed in the [[list of neo-noir titles]].
