office|sixth-highest-grossing film of 2010 in North America]],<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?yr=2010&p=.htm |title=2010 Domestic Grosses |website=Box Office Mojo |access-date=September 6, 2010 |archive-date=April 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190417195206/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?yr=2010&p=.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> and the [[2010 in film#Highest-grossing films|fourth-highest-grossing film of 2010]], behind ''[[Toy Story 3]]'', ''[[Alice in Wonderland (2010 film)|Alice in Wonderland]]'' and ''[[Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 1]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 Worldwide Box Office |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2010/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200520103758/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2010/ |archive-date=May 20, 2020 |access-date=May 27, 2024 |website=[[Box Office Mojo]]}}</ref> Its ''[[The Dark Knight Rises]]'' and ''[[Oppenheimer (film)|Oppenheimer]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/people/chart/?view=Director&id=christophernolan.htm|title=Christopher DiCaprio]]—behind ''[[Titanic (1997 film)|Titanic]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://boxofficemojo.com/people/chart/?view=Actor&id=leonardodicaprio.htm |title=Leonardo DiCaprio |website=Box Office Mojo |access-date= November 15, 2010 |archive-date=November 19, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101119171843/http://boxofficemojo.com/people/chart/?view=Actor&id=leonardodicaprio.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Critical response ===
{{Anchor|Critics}}On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], ''Inception'' holds an approval rating of 87% based on 363 reviews, with an average rating of 8.40/10. The website's critical consensus reads: "Smart, innovative, and thrilling, ''Inception'' is that rare summer blockbuster that succeeds viscerally as well as intellectually."<ref name="tomatoes">{{cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/inception/|title=Inception (2010)|work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]| publisher= [[Fandango Media]]|access-date=January 22, 2021|archive-date=December 15, 2017|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171215212221/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/inception/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], another review aggregator, assigned the film a weighted average score of 74 out of 100, based on 42 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="metacritic">{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/inception |title=Inception |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |work=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=July 27, 2010 |archive-date=July 31, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170731135208/http://www.metacritic.com/movie/inception |url-status=live }}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Andrew|last=Stewart|title='Inception' tops weekend box office|url=https://variety.com/2010/biz/box-office/inception-tops-weekend-box-office-1118021880/|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=July 18, 2010|access-date=August 18, 2010|archive-date=September 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200917170505/https://variety.com/article/VR1118021880.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Peter Travers]] of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' called ''Inception'' a "wildly ingenious chess game," and concluded "the result is a knockout."<ref>{{Cite news| last= Travers |first= Peter |title= ''Inception'' |magazine= Rolling Stone|date=July 12, 2010|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/reviews/17388/180225|access-date=July 14, 2010|archive-date=July 15, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715051320/http://www.rollingstone.com/movies/reviews/17388/180225|url-status=dead}}</ref> Justin Chang of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' praised the film as "a conceptual [[wikt: tour de force|tour de force]]" and wrote, "applying a vivid sense of procedural detail to a fiendishly intricate yarn set in the [[labyrinth]] of the [[unconscious mind]], the writer-director has devised a heist thriller for [[surrealist]]s, a [[Jung]]ian's ''[[Rififi]]'', that challenges viewers to sift through multiple layers of (un)reality."<ref name="variety-review">{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Justin|title=''Inception''|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 5, 2010 |url=https://www.variety.com/review/VE1117943114.html |access-date=July 5, 2010}}</ref> Jim Vejvoda of ''[[IGN]]'' rated the film as perfect, deeming it "a singular accomplishment from a filmmaker who has only gotten better with each film."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Vejvoda |first=Jim |title= Inception Review: Christopher Nolan follows up The Dark Knight with his best film yet |work= [[IGN]].com |date=July 5, 2010 |url= http://movies.ign.com/articles/110/1103912p1.html |access-date=July 5, 2010 |archive-date=July 9, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100709073510/http://movies.ign.com/articles/110/1103912p1.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Relevant (magazine)|''Relevant'']]'s David Roark called it Nolan's "greatest accomplishment", saying, "Visually, intellectually and emotionally, ''Inception'' is a masterpiece."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Roark |first=David |title=''Inception'' |work=[[Relevant Magazine]] |date=July 12, 2010 |url= http://www.relevantmagazine.com/culture/film/reviews/22278-inception |access-date=July 14, 2010 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100721011123/http://www.relevantmagazine.com/culture/film/reviews/22278-inception |archive-date=July 21, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In its August 2010 issue, ''[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]]'' gave the film a full five stars and wrote, "it feels like [[Stanley Kubrick]] adapting the work of the great sci-fi author [[William Gibson]] [...] Nolan delivers another true original: welcome to an undiscovered country."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pierce |first=Nev |title=''Inception'' |work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] |date=June 7, 2010 |url=https://www.empireonline.com/reviews/reviewcomplete.asp?FID=136118 |access-date=July 7, 2010 |archive-date=April 20, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110420044940/http://www.empireonline.com/reviews/reviewcomplete.asp?FID=136118 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]''{{'}}s Lisa Schwarzbaum gave the film a B+ grade and wrote, "It's a rolling explosion of images as hypnotizing and sharply angled as any in a drawing by [[M. C. Escher]] or a state-of-the-biz video game; the backwards splicing of Nolan's own ''Memento'' looks rudimentary by comparison."<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Schwarzbaum |first=Lisa |title=''Inception'' |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |date=July 12, 2010 |url=https://www.ew.com/ew/article/0%2C%2C20401172%2C%2000.html |access-date=July 13, 2010 |archive-date=July 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100714161259/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20401172, |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Roger Ebert]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' awarded the film a full four stars and said that ''Inception'' "is all about process, about fighting our way through enveloping sheets of reality and dream, reality within dreams, dreams without reality. It's a breathtaking juggling act."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Ebert|first=Roger|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/inception-2010|title=''Inception''|date=July 14, 2010|work=Chicago Sun-Times|access-date=July 15, 2010|url-status=live|author-link=Roger Ebert|archive-date=April 18, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130418102245/http://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/inception-2010}}</ref> [[Richard Roeper]], also of the ''Sun-Times'', gave ''Inception'' an "A+" score and called it "one of the best movies of the [21st] century."<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.richardroeper.com/reviews/inception.aspx |title=''Inception'' Review |last=Roeper |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Roeper |work=Chicago Sun-Times |access-date=July 21, 2010 |archive-date=July 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100718103707/http://www.richardroeper.com/reviews/inception.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref> [[BBC Radio 5 Live]]'s [[Mark Kermode]] named ''Inception'' as the best film of 2010, stating that "''Inception'' is proof that people are not stupid, that cinema is not trash, and that it is possible for blockbusters and art to be the same thing."<ref name="Kermode">{{cite video |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/markkermode/2010/12/my_top_five_films_of_the_year.html |access-date=February 9, 2011 |date=December 24, 2010 |first=Mark |last=Kermode |author-link=Mark Kermode |title=Kermode Uncut: My Top Five Films of the Year |publisher=BBC |time=5: 05 |archive-date=April 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190409014641/https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/markkermode/2010/12/my_top_five_films_of_the_year.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Michael Phillips (critic)|Michael Phillips]] of the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' gave the film 3 out of 4 stars and wrote, "I found myself wishing ''Inception'' were weirder, further out [...] the film is Nolan's labyrinth all the way, and it's gratifying to experience a summer movie with large visual ambitions and with nothing more or less on its mind than (as [[Shakespeare]] said) a dream that hath no bottom."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Phillips |first=Michael |title=''Inception'' |work=Chicago Tribune |date=July 15, 2010 |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/movies/sc-mov-0713-inception-20100715%2C%200%2C6233986.column |access-date=July 15, 2010 |archive-date=August 11, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100811161957/http://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/movies/sc-mov-0713-inception-20100715, |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Time (magazine)|''Time'']]'s [[Richard Corliss]] wrote that the film's "noble intent is to implant one man's vision in the mind of a vast audience [...] The idea of movie going as communal dreaming is a century old. With ''Inception'', viewers have a chance to see that notion get a state-of-the-art update."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Corliss|first=Richard|author-link=Richard Corliss|title=''Inception'': Whose Mind Is It, Anyway?|magazine=Time|date=July 14, 2010|url=http://www.time.com/time/arts/article/0%2C8599%2C2003808%2C00.html|access-date=July 15, 2010|archive-date=July 18, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100718231754/http://www.time.com/time/arts/article/0,8599,2003808,00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Kenneth Turan]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' felt that Nolan was able to blend "the best of traditional and modern film making. If you're searching for smart and nervy popular entertainment, this is what it looks like."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Turan|first=Kenneth|author-link=Kenneth Turan|title=''Inception''|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=July 16, 2010|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/news/la-et-inception-20100716%2C%200%2C5478728.story|access-date=July 16, 2010|archive-date=July 28, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100728123450/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/news/la-et-inception-20100716,|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''[[USA Today]]''{{'s}} Claudia Puig gave the film three-and-a-half out of four stars and felt that Nolan "regards his viewers as possibly smarter than they are—or at least as capable of rising to his inventive level. That's a tall order. But it's refreshing to find a director who makes us stretch, even occasionally struggle, to keep up."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Puig|first=Claudia|title=You definitely won't sleep through complex thriller ''Inception''|work=[[USA Today]]|date=July 15, 2010|url=https://www.usatoday.com/life/movies/reviews/2010-07-15-inception15_ST_N.htm|access-date=July 16, 2010|archive-date=July 17, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100717231619/http://www.usatoday.com/life/movies/reviews/2010-07-15-inception15_ST_N.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

Not all reviewers gave the film positive reviews. ''[[New York (magazine)|New York]]'' magazine's [[David Edelstein]] said in his review that he had "no idea what so many people are raving about. It's as if someone went into their heads while they were sleeping and planted the idea that ''Inception'' is a visionary masterpiece and—hold on ... Whoa! I think I get it. The movie is a metaphor for the power of delusional hype—a metaphor for itself."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Edelstein|first=David|title=Dream a Little Dream|work=[[New York (magazine)|New York]]|date=July 11, 2010|url=https://nymag.com/movies/reviews/67155/|access-date=July 13, 2010|archive-date=July 14, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100714165640/http://nymag.com/movies/reviews/67155/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The New York Observer]]''{{'}}s [[Rex Reed]] said the film's development was "pretty much what we've come to expect from summer movies in general and Christopher Nolan movies in particular ... [it] doesn't seem like much of an accomplishment to me."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Reed |first=Rex |title=Can Someone Please Explain ''Inception'' to Me? |work=[[The New York Observer]] |date=July 13, 2010 |url=http://www.observer.com/2010/culture/can-someone-please-explain-inception-me |access-date=July 14, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715052057/http://www.observer.com/2010/culture/can-someone-please-explain-inception-me |archive-date=July 15, 2010}}</ref> [[A. O. Scott]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' commented "there is a lot to see in ''Inception'', there is nothing that counts as genuine vision. Mr. Nolan's idea of the mind is too literal, too logical, and too rule-bound to allow the full measure of madness."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Scott |first=A. O. |author-link=A. O. Scott |title=This Time the Dream's on Me |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 15, 2010 |url=https://movies.nytimes.com/2010/07/16/movies/16inception.html |access-date=July 15, 2010 |archive-date=July 17, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100717195917/http://movies.nytimes.com/2010/07/16/movies/16inception.html |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The New Yorker]]''{{'}}s [[David Denby]] considered the film to be "not nearly as much fun as Nolan imagined it to be", concluding that "''Inception'' is a stunning-looking film that gets lost in fabulous intricacies, a movie devoted to its own workings and to little else."<ref name="Denby">{{cite news|last=Denby|first=David|author-link=David Denby (film critic)|title=Dream Factory|url=https://www.newyorker.com/arts/critics/cinema/2010/07/26/100726crci_cinema_denby|access-date=February 10, 2011|newspaper=[[The New Yorker]]|date=July 26, 2010|archive-date=February 22, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110222212521/http://www.newyorker.com/arts/critics/cinema/2010/07/26/100726crci_cinema_denby|url-status=live}}</ref>

While some critics have tended to view the film as perfectly straightforward, and even criticize its overarching themes as "the stuff of torpid platitudes", online discussion has been much more positive.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Nick |last=Schager |title=Inception |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/inception/4898 |work=[[Slant (magazine)|Slant]] |date=July 14, 2010 |access-date=May 27, 2011 |archive-date=August 8, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110808134156/http://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/inception/4898 |url-status=live }}</ref> Heated debate has centered on the ambiguity of the ending, with many critics like Devin Faraci making the case that the film is self-referential and tongue-in-cheek, both a film about film-making and a dream about dreams.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Devin|last=Faraci|title=Never Wake Up: The Meaning and Secret of Inception|url=https://www.chud.com/24477/never-wake-up-the-meaning-and-secret-of-inception/| website= Chud.com|date=July 19, 2010|access-date=May 27, 2011|archive-date=May 12, 2011|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110512083955/http://www.chud.com/24477/NEVER-WAKE-UP-THE-MEANING-AND-SECRET-OF-INCEPTION/|url-status=live}}</ref> Yet other critics, such as [[Kristin Thompson]], see less value in the ambiguous ending of the film and more in its structure and novel method of storytelling, highlighting ''Inception'' as a new form of narrative that revels in "continuous exposition".<ref name= Bordwell2 />

Several critics and scholars have noted the film has many striking similarities to the 2006 [[anime]] film ''[[Paprika (2006 film)|Paprika]]'' by [[Satoshi Kon]] (and [[Yasutaka Tsutsui]]'s 1993 [[Paprika (novel)|novel of the same name]]), including plot similarities, similar scenes, and similar characters, arguing that ''Inception'' was influenced by ''Paprika''.<ref name="Drazen" /><ref name="Wardlow">{{cite web |last=Wardlow |first=Ciara |title=The Synergy of 'Inception' and 'Paprika' |url=https://filmschoolrejects.com/the-synergy-of-inception-and-paprika-ffefd0973f12/ |website=[[Film School Rejects]] |date=March 2, 2017 |access-date=November 27, 2018 |archive-date=November 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129123846/https://filmschoolrejects.com/the-synergy-of-inception-and-paprika-ffefd0973f12/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="IGN">{{cite web |last=Rizzo-Smith |first=Julian |title=An Ode to Anime Auteur Satoshi Kon |url=https://in.ign.com/paprika/127083/feature/an-ode-to-anime-auteur-satoshi-kon |website=[[IGN]] |date=August 24, 2018 |access-date=November 27, 2018 |archive-date=November 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129124525/https://in.ign.com/paprika/127083/feature/an-ode-to-anime-auteur-satoshi-kon |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Steven |title='Inception': As eye-catching, and as profound, as an Usher concert |url=https://www.politico.com/states/new-york/albany/story/2010/07/inception-as-eye-catching-and-as-profound-as-an-usher-concert-067223 |access-date=January 24, 2019 |work=[[Politico]] |date=July 16, 2010 |archive-date=October 26, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171026182739/https://www.politico.com/states/new-york/albany/story/2010/07/inception-as-eye-catching-and-as-profound-as-an-usher-concert-067223 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Emerson |first1=Jim |title=Inception: Has Christopher Nolan forgotten how to dream? |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/scanners/inception-has-christopher-nolan-forgotten-how-to-dream | website=[[RogerEbert.com]] |date=July 17, 2010 |access-date=January 24, 2019 |archive-date= September 20, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130920030258/https://www.rogerebert.com/scanners/inception-has-christopher-nolan-forgotten-how-to-dream |url-status=live }}</ref> Several sources have also noted plot similarities between the film and the 2002 [[Scrooge McDuck|Uncle Scrooge]] comic ''[[The Dream of a Lifetime]]'' by [[Don Rosa]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Brown|first=Damon|title=Was 'Inception' inspired by Donald Duck?|url= http://www.cnn.com/2010/TECH/web/08/10/inception.donald.duck/index.html|publisher=CNN|access-date=December 29, 2011|date=August 11, 2010|archive-date=February 5, 2012|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120205131026/http://www.cnn.com/2010/TECH/web/08/10/inception.donald.duck/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Gornstein |first= Leslie |title=Did Inception Really Rip Off Scrooge McDuck? |url=http://www.eonline.com/news/ask_the_answer_bitch/did_inception_really_rip_off_scrooge/193794 |work=[[E!#E! Online|E! Online]] |access-date=December 29, 2011 |date=August 4, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120206031007/http://www.eonline.com/news/ask_the_answer_bitch/did_inception_really_rip_off_scrooge/193794 |archive-date=February 6, 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Sean |first=O'Neal |title=The "Inception ripped-off Scrooge McDuck" theory that will briefly amuse you |url=https://www.avclub.com/the-inception-ripped-off-scrooge-mcduck-theory-that-w-1798221139 |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |access-date=December 29, 2011 |date=August 4, 2010 |archive-date=January 9, 2012 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120109122833/http://www.avclub.com/articles/the-inception-rippedoff-scrooge-mcduck-theory-that%2C43814/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The influence of [[Andrei Tarkovsky]]'s ''[[Solaris (1972 film)|Solaris]]'' on ''Inception'' was noted as well.<ref>{{cite web | url= https://screencomment.com/2010/07/the-other-view-bowen-sounds-off-on-inception/ | website= screencomment.com | title= Inception – The Other View | first= Kevin | last= Bowen | date= January 16, 2020 | access-date=  | archive-date= December 10, 2020 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201210211304/https://screencomment.com/2010/07/the-other-view-bowen-sounds-off-on-inception/ | url-status= live }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal| first= Thorsten |last= Bothz-Bornstein |title= The Movie as a Thinking Machine| journal= Inception and Philosophy: Ideas to die for| year= 2011 |isbn= 978-0-8126-9733-9| page= [https://books.google.com/books?id=q62dW7vEjE0C&pg=PA205 205]}}</ref>

=== Year-end and all-time lists ===
''Inception'' appeared on over 273 critics' lists of the top ten films of 2010, being picked as number-one on at least 55 of those lists.<ref name="criticstop10">{{Cite web |url=http://criticstop10.com/best-of-2010/ |title=Home Page – Best of 2010 |publisher=CriticsTop10 |access-date=May 4, 2011 |archive-date=January 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120185542/http://criticstop10.com/best-of-2010/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was the second-most-mentioned film in both the top ten lists and number-one rankings, only behind ''[[The Social Network]]'' along with ''[[Toy Story 3]]'', ''[[True Grit (2010 film)|True Grit]]'', ''[[The King's Speech]]'', and ''[[Black Swan (film)|Black Swan]]'' as the most critically acclaimed films of 2010.<ref name="criticstop10" /> Author [[Stephen King]] placed ''Inception'' at No. 3 in his list of top 10 best films of the year.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Stephen King: The best films of 2010|url=https://ew.com/article/2010/11/26/stephen-king-best-films-2010/|last=King|first=Stephen|date=May 2, 2020|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929183213/https://ew.com/article/2010/11/26/stephen-king-best-films-2010/|archive-date=September 29, 2020}}</ref> Film maker [[Denis Villeneuve]] cited it as among his favorite films of all time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Denis Villeneuve's Favorite Movies: 29 Films the Director Wants You to See |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/denis-villeneuve-favorite-movies/ |access-date=17 March 2025|work=IndieWire |date=26 February 2023 }}</ref> In 2025, the film ranked number 55 on ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century" and number 24 on the "Readers' Choice" edition of the list.<ref name="Times"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |website=The New York Times |date=July 2, 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref>

Critics and publications who ranked the film first for that year included [[Richard Roeper]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'', [[Kenneth Turan]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' (tied with ''[[The Social Network]]'' and ''[[Toy Story 3]]''), Tasha Robinson of ''[[The A.V. Club]]'', ''[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]]'' magazine, and Kirk Honeycutt of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]''.<ref name=metacritictopten>{{cite web |last1=Dietz |first1=Jason |title=2010 Film Critic Top Ten Lists |url=https://www.metacritic.com/feature/film-critic-top-ten-lists |website=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=20 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928044828/https://www.metacritic.com/feature/film-critic-top-ten-lists |archive-date=28 September 2011 |date=9 December 2010}}</ref>

In March 2011, the film was voted by [[BBC Radio 1]] and [[BBC Radio 1Xtra]] listeners as their ninth-favorite film of all time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/radio1movies/ |title=Radio 1 Movies Blog |publisher=BBC |access-date=July 23, 2013 |archive-date=April 24, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110424023704/http://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/radio1movies/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Producer [[Roger Corman]] cited ''Inception'' as an example of "great imagination and originality".<ref>{{cite web|title=Roger Corman CORMAN'S WORLD Interview|url=https://collider.com/roger-corman-cormans-world-interview/|work=Collider|date=December 12, 2011|access-date=June 4, 2020|archive-date=June 4, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200604102451/https://collider.com/roger-corman-cormans-world-interview/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2012, ''Inception'' was ranked the 35th-best-edited film of all time by the [[Motion Picture Editors Guild]].<ref name="editorsguild">{{cite web |url=https://www.editorsguild.com/magazine.cfm?ArticleID=1101 |title=The 75 Best Editied Films |work=CineMontage |access-date=June 1, 2013 |date=Summer 2013 |archive-date=March 17, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150317101140/https://www.editorsguild.com/magazine.cfm?ArticleID=1102 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the same year, ''[[Total Film]]'' named it the most rewatchable movie of all time.<ref name=Rewatchable>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.totalfilm.com/features/50-most-rewatchable-movies/inception-2010 |title=50 Most Rewatchable Movies |magazine=[[Total Film]] |access-date=July 24, 2013 |archive-date=July 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130709161625/http://www.totalfilm.com/features/50-most-rewatchable-movies/inception-2010 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2014, ''Empire'' ranked ''Inception'' the tenth-greatest film ever made on their list of "The 301 Greatest Movies Of All Time" as voted by the magazine's readers,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.empireonline.com/301/list.asp?page=29 |title=The 301 Greatest Movies Of All Time |work=[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]] |access-date=May 29, 2014 |archive-date=July 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140712141743/http://www.empireonline.com/301/list.asp?page=29 |url-status=live }}</ref> while ''Rolling Stone'' magazine named it the second-best science fiction film since the turn of the century.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/lists/the-top-20-sci-fi-films-of-the-21st-century-20140515 |title=The Top 20 Sci-Fi Films of the 21st Century |magazine=Rolling Stone |access-date=August 14, 2014 |archive-date=August 11, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811124359/http://www.rollingstone.com/movies/lists/the-top-20-sci-fi-films-of-the-21st-century-20140515 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Inception'' was ranked 84th on ''Hollywood's 100 Favorite Films'', a list compiled by ''The Hollywood Reporter'' in 2014, surveying "Studio chiefs, Oscar winners and TV royalty".<ref>{{cite web|access-date=June 22, 2015|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/gallery/100-greatest-films-all-time-714192/84-inception|title=Hollywood's 100 Favorite Films|work=The Hollywood Reporter|archive-date=June 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623002214/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/gallery/100-greatest-films-all-time-714192/84-inception|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2016, ''Inception'' was voted the [[BBC's 100 Greatest Films of the 21st Century|51st-best film of the 21st Century]] by [[BBC]], as picked by 177 film critics from around the world.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=August 23, 2016|url=http://www.bbc.com/culture/story/20160819-the-21st-centurys-100-greatest-films?ocid=twcul|title=The 21st Century's 100 Greatest Films|work=BBC| date=August 23, 2016 |archive-date=August 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160823184121/http://www.bbc.com/culture/story/20160819-the-21st-centurys-100-greatest-films?ocid=twcul|url-status=live}}</ref> The film was included in the [[Visual Effects Society]]'s list of "The Most Influential Visual Effects Films of All Time".<ref>{{cite web|access-date=September 16, 2017|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2017/09/visual-effects-society-top-70-vfx-films-star-wars-blade-runner-citizen-kane-1201875595/|title=Visual Effects Society: The Top 70 VFX Films of All Time Include 'Star Wars,' 'Blade Runner,' and 'Citizen Kane'|work=Indiewire|date=September 12, 2017|archive-date=September 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170916014933/http://www.indiewire.com/2017/09/visual-effects-society-top-70-vfx-films-star-wars-blade-runner-citizen-kane-1201875595/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2019, ''Total Film'' named ''Inception'' the best film of the 2010s.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/decade-best-movies-2010-2019/4/ |title=The 100 best movies of the decade |work=[[Total Film]] |date=December 16, 2019 |access-date=December 17, 2019 |archive-date=December 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217201655/https://www.gamesradar.com/decade-best-movies-2010-2019/4/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Many critics and media outlets included ''Inception'' in their rankings of the best films of the 2010s.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=The 100 Greatest Movies Of The 21st Century: 10 – 1|magazine=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]|date=January 11, 2020|url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/features/best-movies-century-page-10/|access-date=January 11, 2020|archive-date=January 20, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200120131242/https://www.empireonline.com/movies/features/best-movies-century-page-10/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=September 5, 2019|url=https://mashable.com/article/best-films-of-2010s-decade/|title=The 15 best films of the 2010s|work=mashable.com|archive-date=November 18, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118143953/https://mashable.com/article/best-films-of-2010s-decade/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://screenrant.com/best-movies-decade-2010s-list/|title=Best movies of 2010s decade|last=Leadbeater|first=Alex|website=[[Screen Rant]]|date=2 March 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302082204/https://screenrant.com/best-movies-decade-2010s-list/|archive-date=March 2, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 5, 2019|url=https://www.avclub.com/the-100-best-movies-of-the-2010s-1839846306|title=The 100 best movies of the 2010s|work=The A.V. Club|archive-date=December 10, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210045220/https://film.avclub.com/the-100-best-movies-of-the-2010s-1839846306|url-status=live}}</ref> The film was included in ''[[Forbes]]'' magazine's list of ''Top 150 Greatest Films of 21st Century''.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Hughes|first1=Mark|title=The Top 150 Greatest Films of 21st Century|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/markhughes/2021/05/31/the-top-150-greatest-films-of-the-21st-century/|website=Forbes|date=31 May 2021|access-date=August 19, 2021|archive-date=August 19, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210819060817/https://www.forbes.com/sites/markhughes/2021/05/31/the-top-150-greatest-films-of-the-21st-century/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In April 2014, ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' placed the title on its top ten list of the most overrated films. ''Telegraph''{{'}}s Tim Robey stated, "It's a criminal failing of the movie that it purports to be about people's dreams being invaded, but demonstrates no instinct at all for what a dream has ever felt like, and no flair for making us feel like we're in one, at any point."<ref>{{cite web |first1=Tim |last1=Robey |title=10 most overrated films of all time |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/film/10767345/10-most-overrated-films-of-all-time.html |website=The Telegraph |date=April 21, 2014 |access-date=June 1, 2014 |archive-date=June 1, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140601192923/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/film/10767345/10-most-overrated-films-of-all-time.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The film won an informal poll by the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' as the most overrated movie of 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/movies/2010/12/inception-christopher-nolan-overrated.html |title='Inception' wins informal poll as most overrated movie of 2010 (Part 2) |date=December 30, 2010 |access-date=June 2, 2014 |first1=Steven |last1=Zeitchik |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |archive-date=June 7, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140607010933/http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/movies/2010/12/inception-christopher-nolan-overrated.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2021, members of [[Writers Guild of America West]] (WGAW) and [[Writers Guild of America, East]] (WGAE) ranked its screenplay 37th in WGA's 101 Greatest Screenplays of the 21st Century (So Far).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pedersen |first=Erik |date=2021-12-06 |title=101 Greatest Screenplays Of The 21st Century: Horror Pic Tops Writers Guild's List |url=https://deadline.com/2021/12/greatest-screenplays-of-21st-century-list-writers-guild-get-out-1234885622/ |access-date=2025-12-25 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=101 Greatest Screenplays of the 21st Century (*so far) |url=https://www.wga.org/writers-room/101-best-lists/101-best-screenplays-of-the-21st-century-so-far/list |access-date=2025-12-25 |website=www.wga.org}}</ref>

In 2026, ''Inception'' was selected for preservation in the United States [[National Film Registry]] by the [[Library of Congress]] as being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Loving |first=Casey |date=2026-01-29 |title=National Film Registry Adds 'The Grand Budapest Hotel,' 'Inception,' 'The Incredibles' and More |url=https://www.thewrap.com/creative-content/movies/national-film-registry-2025-incredibles-inception/ |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Accolades ==
{{Main|List of accolades received by Inception}}

The film won many awards in technical categories, such as [[Academy Awards]] for [[Academy Award for Best Cinematography|Best Cinematography]], [[Academy Award for Best Sound Editing|Best Sound Editing]], [[Academy Award for Best Sound|Best Sound Mixing]], and [[Academy Award for Best Visual Effects|Best Visual Effects]],<ref name=oscars>{{cite web |url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/83/nominees.html |title=Nominees for the 83rd Academy Awards |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=January 28, 2011 |archive-date=September 4, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120904121804/http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/83/nominees.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and the [[British Academy Film Awards]] for [[BAFTA Award for Best Production Design|Best Production Design]], [[BAFTA Award for Best Special Visual Effects|Best Special Visual Effects]] and [[BAFTA Award for Best Sound|Best Sound]].<ref name="BAFTA">{{cite web |url=http://www.bafta.org/awards/film/2011-film-awards%2C1572%2CBA.html |title=2011 BAFTA Awards Nominees |publisher=[[British Academy of Film and Television Arts]] |access-date=January 28, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110110061729/http://www.bafta.org/awards/film/2011-film-awards%2C1572%2CBA.html |archive-date=January 10, 2011 }}</ref> In most of its artistic nominations, such as Film, Director, and Screenplay at the Oscars, BAFTAs and [[Golden Globes]], the film was defeated by ''[[The Social Network]]'' or ''[[The King's Speech]]''.<ref name=oscars /><ref name=BAFTA /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goldenglobes.org/nominations/year/2010 |title=68th Annual Golden Globe Awards Nominations |publisher=[[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] |access-date=January 28, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120911090824/http://www.goldenglobes.org/nominations/year/2010/ |archive-date=September 11, 2012 }}</ref> However, the film did win the two highest honors for a science fiction or fantasy film: the 2011 [[Bradbury Award]] for best dramatic production<ref name= Nebulas>{{cite web |url=http://www.tor.com/blogs/2011/05/2011-nebula-award-winners |title=2011 Nebula Award winners |date=May 22, 2011 |publisher=[[Tor.com]] |access-date=October 16, 2011 |archive-date=October 27, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111027030429/http://www.tor.com/blogs/2011/05/2011-nebula-award-winners |url-status=live }}</ref> and the 2011 [[Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation#Long Form|Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation (Long Form)]].<ref name=Hugos>{{cite web |url=http://www.thehugoawards.org/2011/08/2011-hugo-award-winners/ |title=2011 Hugo Award winners |date=August 21, 2011 |publisher=[[Hugo Awards]] |access-date=October 16, 2011 |archive-date=April 1, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160401000112/http://www.thehugoawards.org/2011/08/2011-hugo-award-winners/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== In popular culture ==
Numerous pop and hip hop songs reference the film, including [[Common (rapper)|Common]]'s "Blue Sky", [[N.E.R.D.]]'s "[[Hypnotize U]]", [[XV (rapper)|XV]]'s "The Kick", [[Black Eyed Peas]]' "[[Just Can't Get Enough (Black Eyed Peas song)|Just Can't Get Enough]]", [[Lil Wayne]]'s "[[6 Foot 7 Foot]]", [[Jennifer Lopez]]'s "[[On the Floor]]", and [[B.o.B]]'s "[[Strange Clouds (song)|Strange Clouds]]", while [[T.I.]] had ''Inception''-based artwork on two of his mix-tapes. An instrumental track by [[Joe Budden]] is titled "Inception".<ref>{{cite web |first=Aaron |last=Zorgel |title=Why do rappers love the movie Inception so much? |url=http://www.aux.tv/2012/03/why-do-rappers-love-the-movie-inception-so-much/ |work=AUX.TV |date=March 8, 2012 |access-date=December 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160611062544/http://www.aux.tv/2012/03/why-do-rappers-love-the-movie-inception-so-much/ | archive-date=June 11, 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref> The animated series ''[[South Park]]'' parodies the film in the show's tenth episode of its [[South Park season 14|fourteenth season]], titled "[[Insheeption]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Hill|first1=Scott T.|title=South Park Satirizes Inception's Mind-Wipe|url=https://www.wired.com/2010/10/south-park-inception/|magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]|access-date=November 15, 2017|date=October 21, 2010|archive-date=November 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116090714/https://www.wired.com/2010/10/south-park-inception/|url-status=live}}</ref> The film was also an influence for [[Ariana Grande]]'s video for "[[No Tears Left to Cry]]".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Willman |first1=Chris |title=Song Review: Ariana Grande's 'No Tears Left to Cry' |url=https://variety.com/2018/music/news/ariana-grande-no-tears-left-to-cry-review-1202770171/ |website=Variety |access-date=July 6, 2018 |date=April 19, 2018 |archive-date=July 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180714170349/https://variety.com/2018/music/news/ariana-grande-no-tears-left-to-cry-review-1202770171/ |url-status=live }}</ref> "[[Lawnmower Dog]]", the second episode of the animated comedy show ''[[Rick and Morty]]'', parodied the film.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldberg |first1=Lesley |title=Adult Swim's 'Rick and Morty' Takes On 'Inception' |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/adult-swims-rick-morty-takes-661896 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |date=December 6, 2013 |access-date=January 19, 2020 |archive-date=May 13, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200513145350/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/adult-swims-rick-morty-takes-661896 |url-status=live }}</ref> In an episode of ''[[The Simpsons]]'', named "[[How I Wet Your Mother]]", the plot spoofs ''Inception'' with various scenes parodying moments from the film.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2012/03/when-the-simpsons-went-inception-48463/|title=When 'The Simpsons' Went 'Inception'|last=Willmore|first=Alison|date=March 27, 2020|website=[[Indiewire]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327074123/https://www.indiewire.com/2012/03/when-the-simpsons-went-inception-48463/|archive-date=March 27, 2020}}</ref> The showrunners of the television series ''[[The Flash (2014 TV series)|The Flash]]'' said its season 4 finale was inspired by ''Inception''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2423571/the-flash-showrunner-explains-how-the-finale-is-inspired-by-inception|title=The Flash Showrunner Explains How The Finale Is Inspired By Inception|last=Venable|first=Nick|date=February 7, 2020|magazine=Cinemablend|access-date=April 2, 2020|archive-date=July 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711081429/https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2423571/the-flash-showrunner-explains-how-the-finale-is-inspired-by-inception|url-status=live}}</ref> In February 2020, American singer-songwriter [[Taylor Swift]] released a lyric video for her single "[[The Man (Taylor Swift song)|The Man]]", which featured visuals bearing resemblance to the film. The song also mentions DiCaprio in its lyrics.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://popcrush.com/taylor-swift-the-man-lyric-video/|title=Taylor Swift's 'The Man' Lyric Video Features a Subtle Nod to Leonardo DiCaprio|last=Reda|first=Natasha|date=February 7, 2020|magazine=[[PopCrush]]|access-date=February 9, 2020|archive-date=February 8, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200208183705/https://popcrush.com/taylor-swift-the-man-lyric-video/|url-status=live}}</ref> Kpop boy group [[Ateez]], also released a song titled "Inception" in 2020, serving as their title track for their fifth EP, [[Zero: Fever Part.1]]. The song is heavily inspired by Nolan's film, with the concept, music video and lyrics containing references to core concepts of "dream in a dream" and distorted realities that are present in the film.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rowley |first=Glenn |date=2020-07-30 |title=Ateez Dance Through a Dream in Explosive 'Inception' Video: Watch |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/ateez-inception-video-9427022/ |access-date=2026-07-01 |website=Billboard |language=en-US}}</ref>

The film's title has been [[Colloquialism|colloquialized]] as the word ''inception''<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2011 |title=inception |url=https://neologisms.rice.edu/word/44552 |access-date=February 8, 2026 |website=Rice University Neologisms Database <!-- from https://neologisms.rice.edu/aboutus -->}}</ref> and the [[Portmanteau|splinter]]<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Lepic |first=Ryan |title=Motivation in Morphology: Lexical Patterns in ASL and English |date=2015 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=University of California, San Diego |isbn=978-1-339-09169-3 |pages=213–214 |id={{ProQuest|1732684214}} (order no. 3725206)}}</ref> suffix ''[[wiktionary:-ception|-ception]]''<ref>{{cite web |date=November 25, 2013 |orig-date=Source of citation: Internet, July 2010 |title=-ception |url=https://neologisms.rice.edu/word/40915 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170705153941/http://neologisms.rice.edu/index.php?a=term&d=1&t=17573 |archive-date=July 5, 2017 |website=Rice University Neologisms Database}}</ref>, which refer to layering, [[Nesting (computing)|nesting]], or [[recursion]], in reference to the movie's key element of a "dream within a dream".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sherlock |first=Ben |date=August 4, 2024 <!-- 6:20 AM EDT --> |title=What Is Inception? Christopher Nolan Movie Title Meaning Explained |url=https://screenrant.com/inception-movie-title-meaning-explained/ |access-date=February 8, 2026 |website=ScreenRant |publisher=Valnet |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Heiden |first=Matt |date=February 17, 2012 |title=A translating tool for the modern "convo" |url=http://www2.portnet.k12.ny.us/SchreiberTimes/2011-2012/2012-2-17.pdf#page=13 |access-date=February 8, 2026 |work=The Schreiber Times |department=Features |publisher=the student body of Paul D. Schreiber High School |page=14 |publication-place=Port Washington, NY}}</ref> The normal meaning of ''inception'' is 'beginning', and the title refers to causing the inception of an idea within someone's mind.<ref>{{Cite web |last=L. |first=Naomi |date=January 21, 2015 |title=Four Words That Don't Mean What You Think They Do |url=https://jaycwolfe.com/2015/01/21/four-words-that-dont-mean-what-you-think-they-do/ |access-date=February 8, 2026 |website=The Wolfe's (Writing) Den |language=en-US}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: List of 20th-century films considered the worst
======================================================================

{{about|films considered the worst from the 20th century|21st-century films considered the worst|List of 21st-century films considered the worst|other uses|Lists of films considered the worst}}
{{protection padlock|reason=Persistent [[WP:Disruptive editing|disruptive editing]]|small=yes}}

{{Use American English|date=March 2023}}
{{Dynamic list}}
[[File:Reefer Madness (1936).jpg|220px|thumb|''[[Reefer Madness]]'' (1936), one of the earliest films to garner particularly negative reviews<ref name="psmag">{{cite magazine|last=Lincoln|first=Kevin|title=The Benefits of Being the Worst Movie Ever Made|url=https://psmag.com/economics/benefits-worst-movie-ever-made-84813|access-date=October 23, 2017|magazine=[[Pacific Standard]]|date=July 2, 2014|archive-date=October 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023115728/https://psmag.com/economics/benefits-worst-movie-ever-made-84813|url-status=live}}</ref>]]

The [[film]]s listed below have been ranked by a number of critics in varying media sources as being among the worst films ever made in the 20th century. Examples of such sources include [[Metacritic]], [[Roger Ebert]]'s list of most-hated films, ''[[The Golden Turkey Awards]]'', ''[[Leonard Maltin's Movie Guide]]'', [[Rotten Tomatoes]], [[pop culture]] writer [[Nathan Rabin]]'s ''[[My Year of Flops|My World of Flops]]'', the [[Stinkers Bad Movie Awards]], the cult TV series ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'' (alongside spinoffs ''[[Cinematic Titanic]]'', ''[[The Film Crew]]'' and ''[[RiffTrax]]''), and the [[Golden Raspberry Awards]] (aka the "Razzies"). Films on these lists are generally [[feature film|feature-length films]] that are [[commerce|commercial]]/[[art film|artistic]] in nature (intended to turn a profit, express personal statements or both), professionally or independently produced (as opposed to [[amateur]] productions, such as [[home movie]]s), and released in theaters, then on home video. There are 57 films listed below, with 103 across both lists.

== 1930s ==

=== ''Maniac'' (1934) ===
{{Main|Maniac (1934 film){{!}}''Maniac'' (1934 film)}}
[[File:Maniac5.jpg|thumb|''[[Maniac (1934 film)|Maniac]]'' (1934) is one of the many [[pre-Code]] exploitation films from the 1930s featuring sex, violence and drugs.]]
''Maniac'', also known as ''Sex Maniac'', is a [[pre-Code]] [[exploitation film|exploitation]]-[[horror film]] directed by [[Dwain Esper]]. The story is a loose adaptation of the [[Edgar Allan Poe]] story "[[The Black Cat (short story)|The Black Cat]]" and follows a [[vaudeville]] impersonator who becomes an assistant to a [[mad scientist]]. Promoted as a documentary on [[mental illness]], ''Maniac'' was criticized for its gratuitous footage of women undressing and for plagiarizing horror sequences from the 1922 silent film ''[[Häxan]]''. [[Danny Peary]] believes that ''Maniac'' is the worst film ever made, and [[Charlie Jane Anders]] of [[Gawker Media]]{{'}}s ''[[io9]]'' described it as "possibly the worst movie in history."<ref>{{Cite book|last=Peary|first=Danny|author-link=Danny Peary|title=Cult Midnight Movies: Discover the 37 Best Weird, Sleazy, Sexy, and Crazy Good Cinema Classics|publisher=[[Workman Publishing Company]]|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TTsPBAAAQBAJ&q=Maniac+%281934%29+Dwain+Esper|year=2014|isbn=9780761181699|access-date=October 2, 2020|archive-date=October 25, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231025172439/https://books.google.com/books?id=TTsPBAAAQBAJ&q=Maniac+%281934%29+Dwain+Esper#v=snippet&q=Maniac%20(1934)%20Dwain%20Esper&f=false|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://io9.gizmodo.com/did-the-worst-movie-of-all-time-come-out-75-years-ago-5161275 |title=Did The Worst Movie Of All Time Come Out 75 Years Ago? |publisher=[[io9]] |last=Anders |first=Charlie Jane |date=February 26, 2009 |access-date=February 18, 2019 |archive-date=February 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190218201930/https://io9.gizmodo.com/did-the-worst-movie-of-all-time-come-out-75-years-ago-5161275 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Rotten Tomatoes]] placed ''Maniac'' on its list of movies "So Bad They're Unmissable",<ref name="sobad">{{cite web |url=https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/25-movies-so-bad-theyre-unmissable/|title=25 Movies So Bad They're Unmissable |last=Adams |first=Michael |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |date=January 30, 2010 |access-date=January 25, 2015 }}</ref> ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]'' included the film on its list of the 20 worst movies ever and it is featured in [[John J. B. Wilson]]'s book ''[[The Official Razzie Movie Guide: Enjoying the Best of Hollywood's Worst]]''.<ref name="italianvanity">{{cite news|url=https://www.vanityfair.it/show/cinema/2018/02/25/20-film-piu-brutti-di-sempre|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220108083603/https://www.vanityfair.it/show/cinema/2018/02/25/20-film-piu-brutti-di-sempre |work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|title=I 20 film più brutti di sempre|last=Pellegrini|first=Francesca|language=it|date=February 25, 2018|access-date=February 18, 2019|archive-date=January 8, 2022}}</ref>

=== ''Reefer Madness'' (1936) ===
{{Main|Reefer Madness{{!}}''Reefer Madness''}}
[[File:ReeferMadness_13.jpg|thumb|Originally titled ''Tell Your Children'', the anti-[[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] film ''[[Reefer Madness]]'' was called "the grand-daddy of all 'Worst' movies" by [[Leonard Maltin]].]]
''Reefer Madness'' (originally released as ''Tell Your Children'' and sometimes titled or subtitled as ''The Burning Question'', ''Dope Addict'', ''Doped Youth'', and ''Love Madness'') is a 1936 American [[exploitation film]] and [[propaganda|propaganda work]] revolving around the melodramatic events that ensue when high school students are lured by pushers to smoke [[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] and consequently become addicted and involved in various crimes such as a [[Hit and run (vehicular)|hit and run accident]], [[manslaughter]], [[murder]], attempted rape, descent into madness, association with organized crime, and suicide.

''[[Pacific Standard]]'' wrote that ''Reefer Madness'' was "one of the first films ever to be considered transcendentally bad"<ref name="psmag"/> and [[Leonard Maltin]] has called it "the grand-daddy of all 'Worst' movies".<ref name="Maltin01211">{{cite book |last=Maltin |first=Leonard |author-link=Leonard Maltin |title=Leonard Maltin's Movie and Video Guide 2004 |publisher=Signet |year=2003 |isbn=0-451-20940-0 |url=https://archive.org/details/leonardmaltinsmo00leon }}</ref> <!--Dead source, no archive available except the deprecated archive.today, thus [[WP:V|unverifiable]]: ''[[Las Vegas CityLife]]'' named it the "worst ever" runner-up to ''[[Plan 9 from Outer Space]]'',<ref>{{cite news |url=http://archives.lasvegascitylife.com/articles/2009/09/24/ae/stage/iq_31362594.txt |date=September 24, 2009 |last=McKee |first=David |work=Las Vegas CityLife |access-date=November 17, 2013 |title=What's the Worst Movie Ever? }}</ref> and--> [[News.com.au]] considered it a "disastrous flop turned cult classic" due to its "terrible acting and exaggerated drug-addicted stereotypes".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news.com.au/national/nsw-act/when-hollywoods-worst-films-become-cult-classics/news-story/792f3f09aba66809245d65328c73921c|title=When Hollywood's worst films become cult classics|work=[[News.com.au]]|first=Troy|last=Lennon|date=December 7, 2017|access-date=January 20, 2019|archive-date=January 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190121064145/https://www.news.com.au/national/nsw-act/when-hollywoods-worst-films-become-cult-classics/news-story/792f3f09aba66809245d65328c73921c|url-status=live}}</ref> Natalli Amato of ''[[The Daily Dot]]'' included ''Reefer Madness'' on her list of the best worst movies, writing that it "may be one of the worst movies of all time for the fact that it accomplished the exact opposite of its intended goal" by becoming a cult classic among stoners.<ref>{{cite web |last=St-Amand |first=Vanessa |title=Ranked: The best worst movies you need to watch |url=https://www.dailydot.com/upstream/best-worst-movies/ |website=[[The Daily Dot]] |access-date=July 8, 2022 |date=March 29, 2022 |archive-date=June 19, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220619224037/https://www.dailydot.com/upstream/best-worst-movies/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Leafly]]''{{'}}s Danté Jordan also wrote that it may be "the worst movie of all time", criticizing its many inaccuracies regarding marijuana use and calling it "easily one of the most uncreative and [[tone-deaf]] pieces of anti-cannabis propaganda".<ref>{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Danté |title=We watched 'Reefer Madness' to confirm it's still complete garbage |url=https://www.leafly.com/news/lifestyle/reasons-why-reefer-madness-is-complete-garbage |website=[[Leafly]] |access-date=July 8, 2022 |language=en |date=January 27, 2020 |archive-date=July 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708065233/https://www.leafly.com/news/lifestyle/reasons-why-reefer-madness-is-complete-garbage |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''The Terror of Tiny Town'' (1938) ===
{{Main|The Terror of Tiny Town{{!}}''The Terror of Tiny Town''}}
''The Terror of Tiny Town'', directed by [[Sam Newfield]] and produced by [[Jed Buell]], remains the only [[musical film|musical]] [[Western (genre)|Western]] with an all-[[Dwarfism|dwarf]] cast.<ref name="tinyterror"/> The film was pulled from obscurity as a [[camp (style)|camp classic]] after appearing in college and [[midnight film|midnight screenings]] in the early 1970s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Terror of Tiny Town (1938)|url=https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/92598/the-terror-of-tiny-town|access-date=December 16, 2020|website=Turner Classic Movies|language=en|archive-date=June 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210614012516/https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/92598/the-terror-of-tiny-town|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1978, it was included in [[Michael Medved]]'s book ''[[The Fifty Worst Films of All Time]]'',<ref name="tinyterror">{{cite web|url=https://filmthreat.com/uncategorized/the-terror-of-tiny-town-dvd/|title=The Terror of Tiny Town (DVD)|work=Film Threat|date=June 17, 2005|access-date=March 23, 2020|archive-date=March 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200324034956/https://filmthreat.com/uncategorized/the-terror-of-tiny-town-dvd/|url-status=live}}</ref> and it has since been listed as one of the worst films ever made by ''[[Flavorwire]]'',<ref name="Flavorwire"/> Rotten Tomatoes,<ref name="sobad"/> and ''[[The Golden Turkey Awards]]''.<ref name="tinyterror"/> [[Melvin Defleur]] referred to it as "Perhaps the worst film of all time",<ref>{{Cite book|last=Defleur|first=Melvin|author-link=Melvin Defleur|title=Understanding Mass Communication: A Liberal Arts Perspective|publisher=[[Houghton Mifflin Harcourt]]|edition=6|year=1998|page=160}}</ref> and critic Gabriel Ricard listed it as the worst film ever made; stating, "not only is it pretty terrible, but ''Tiny Town'' is also pretty endearing."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://culturedvultures.com/best-worst-movies/|title=20 Best Worst Movies Of All Time|work=Cultured Vultures|last=Richard|first=Gabriel|date=June 5, 2019|access-date=March 23, 2020|archive-date=December 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209080410/https://culturedvultures.com/best-worst-movies/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1986, ''The Terror of Tiny Town'' was the first film featured on ''[[Canned Film Festival]]'', a [[late night television]] show featuring the worst movies ever made.<ref name="cannedfilm">{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-06-20-8602140300-story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220507001443/https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-06-20-8602140300-story.html|title=A 'Terror' Kicks Off World's Worst Film Festival|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|last=Terry|first=Clifford|date=June 20, 1989|access-date=March 23, 2020|archive-date=May 7, 2022}}</ref>

== 1940s ==

=== ''The Babe Ruth Story'' (1948) ===
{{Main|The Babe Ruth Story{{!}}''The Babe Ruth Story''}}
[[File:William_Bendix_1960.JPG|thumb|left|upright|Actor [[William Bendix]], who played The Great Bambino in ''[[The Babe Ruth Story]]'' (1948), cited as one of the worst [[biopics]] ever made]]
''The Babe Ruth Story'' is a 1948 [[baseball film]] biography of [[Babe Ruth]], starring [[William Bendix]], [[Claire Trevor]] and [[Sam Levene]].<ref>{{Citation|last1=Del Ruth|first1=Roy|title=The Babe Ruth story|date=2010|publisher=Warner Home Video|language=en|oclc=694103117|last2=Considine|first2=Bob|last3=Callahan|first3=George|last4=Bendix|first4=William|last5=Trevor|first5=Claire|last6=Bickford|first6=Charles|last7=Frawley|first7=William|last8=Levene|first8=Sam|last9=Allied Artists Productions}}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' describes it as "the ''[[Plan 9 from Outer Space]]'' of baseball biopics".<ref>{{cite news |title=The Babe Ruth Story (1948)|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movies/movie/3535/The-Babe-Ruth-Story/overview |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219200719/http://www.nytimes.com/movies/movie/3535/The-Babe-Ruth-Story/overview |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 19, 2013 |department=Movies & TV Dept.|work=[[The New York Times]]|first=Hal|last=Erickson|author-link=Hal Erickson (author)|date=2013|access-date=November 30, 2013}}</ref> It was rushed into release while Ruth was still alive. One infamous scene features Ruth promising a dying child that he will hit two [[home run]]s; the child is subsequently cured of his ailments after Ruth delivers on the promise.<ref name="homerun"/>

[[Baseball Hall of Fame]]r [[Ted Williams]] believed it to be the worst movie he had ever seen. ''[[The Washington Times]]'' stated that it "stands as possibly the worst movie ever made".<ref>{{cite news |title=Duke as Williams? A Prince of an Idea |first=Dan |last=Shaughnessy |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=XscSAAAAIBAJ&pg=7230,788739&dq=babe+ruth+story+worst+film |newspaper=Spokane Chronicle |date=April 3, 1986 |access-date=November 30, 2013 |archive-date=August 16, 2022 |last=Heller |first=Dick |title=Clinic and reception in the works to honor NBA pioneer Lloyd |newspaper=The Washington Times |date=July 23, 2000 |url-access=subscription "nearly every list of the worst movies ever made" was "with good reason".<ref>{{cite web |last=Apple |first=Charles |title=Some of the worst movies of all-time |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/sep/22/some-worst-movies-all-time/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=September 22, 2020 |archive-date=July 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710190457/https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/sep/22/some-worst-movies-all-time/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Newberry |first=Paul |title=Counting down baseball's worst movie locales |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/2019/08/10/counting-down-baseballs-worst-movie-locales/4492519007/ |website=[[The Providence Journal]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=August 10, 2019 |archive-date=June 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220625165504/https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/2019/08/10/counting-down-baseballs-worst-movie-locales/4492519007/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Newsday]]''{{'}}s Jack Mathews similarly wrote that ''The Babe Ruth Story'' was "what many people consider to be the worst sports movie of all time".<ref>{{cite journal |last=Dunne |first=Michael |title=Post-War Cultural Construction in "The Babe Ruth Story" |journal=Studies in Popular Culture |date=October 1996 |volume=19 |issue=1 |pages=1–7 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23413739 ''[[The A.V. === ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' (1948) ===
{{Main|No Orchids for Miss Blandish (film){{!}}''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' (film)}}
''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'', a British [[gangster film]] adapted from the 1939 [[No Orchids for Miss Blandish (novel)|novel]] by [[James Hadley Chase]], received a very hostile reception from the press. This was mainly due to the film's high (for the time) implied level of violence and rape, but also because its attempt to portray Americans using a largely British cast (including an early role for [[Sid James]])<ref name="goodwin">{{cite book |first=Cliff |last=Goodwin |title=Sid James: A Biography |publisher=Random House |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-7535-4682-6 |pages=67–68 }}</ref> was seen as unconvincing.<ref name="bmc">{{cite book |last=McFarlane |first=Brian |year=1999 |chapter=Outrage: No Orchids for Miss Blandish |title=British Crime Cinema |editor-first=Steve |editor-last=Chibnall |editor-first2=Robert |editor-last2=Murphy |publisher=Routledge |isbn=0-415-16870-8 |pages=37–50 }}</ref>

The British film journal ''[[Monthly Film Bulletin]]'' called it "the most sickening exhibition of brutality, perversion, sex and sadism ever to be shown on a cinema screen".<ref name="bmc"/> The ''[[Sunday Express]]'' film reviewer called ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' "the worst film I have ever seen".<ref name="hfg">{{cite book |title=Halliwell's Film Guide |publisher=HarperPerennial |year=1994 |isbn=978-0-06-273318-4 |page=781 }}</ref> The Australian newspaper ''[[The Age]]'' also gave a harsh review: "''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' is not only a disgrace to the studio that made it, but it also reflects on the British industry as a whole ... the entire production is unpardonable."<ref>{{cite news |title=Question of Propriety for the Censor |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/205685128/19598563 |access-date=2024-12-13 |work=The Age |date=1948-11-27 |location=Melbourne |page=9 |via=Trove}}</ref>

Cliff Goodwin, discussing ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish''{{'}}s initial reception, notes it was "unanimously dubbed 'the worst film ever made{{'"}}.<ref name="goodwin"/> Later reviews of the film were equally antipathetic. ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' was described by British film reviewer [[Leslie Halliwell]] as a "hilariously awful gangster film ... one of the worst films ever made".<ref name="hfg"/> ''[[Leonard Maltin's Movie Guide|Leonard Maltin's Classic Movie Guide]]'' states that ''No Orchids for Miss Blandish'' "aspires to be a Hollywood [[film noir]] and misses by a mile."<ref>{{cite book |last=Maltin |first=Leonard |year=2011 |title=Leonard Maltin's Classic Movie Guide: From The Silent Era Through 1965 |edition=Second |publisher=Penguin |isbn=978-0-452-29577-3 |page=474 }}</ref>

Despite (or because) of the condemnation, the film was commercially successful<ref>"Outrage: No Orchids for Miss Blandish" by Brian McFarlane in ''British Crime Cinema'', edited by Steve Chibnall, Robert Murphy. Routledge, 1999. {{ISBN|0-415-16870-8}} (pg. 37-50).</ref> and broke box office records in Britain in areas where it was not banned.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=xtGIAgAAQBAJ&dq=hungry+hill+film+box+office&pg=PA209 Robert Murphy, ''Realism and Tinsel: Cinema and Society in Britain 1939-48'' 2003 p210]</ref>

== 1950s ==

=== ''Glen or Glenda'' (1953) ===
{{Main|Glen or Glenda{{!}}''Glen or Glenda''}}
''Glen or Glenda'' starred [[Ed Wood]] as Glen, a transvestite who cross-dresses as Glenda. Wood also directed the film. After a [[dream sequence]], Glen undergoes psychotherapy to help "cure" him of his [[transvestism]].

[[Leonard Maltin]] wrote that ''Glen or Glenda'' was worse than Wood's later ''[[Plan 9 from Outer Space]]'' and considered it "possibly the worst movie ever made".<ref name="Maltin01211"/> Julien Allen of ''[[IndieWire|Reverse Shot]]'' similarly wrote that it was "widely considered to be an atrocity" and "the most catastrophic failure of [Wood's] singularly bad career".<ref>{{cite web |last=Allen |first=Julien |title=Simply the Worst: Edward D. Wood Jr.'s 'Glen or Glenda?' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2011/09/simply-the-worst-edward-d-wood-jr-s-glen-or-glenda-224683/ |website=[[IndieWire]] |access-date=July 8, 2022 |language=en |date=September 7, 2011 |archive-date=July 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708193054/https://www.indiewire.com/2011/09/simply-the-worst-edward-d-wood-jr-s-glen-or-glenda-224683/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Richard Barrios described ''Glen or Glenda'' as "one of the funniest and worst movies ever made".<ref>Richard Barrios, ''Screened Out: Playing Gay in Hollywood from Edison to Stonewall'', Psychology Press, 2003, {{ISBN|0-415-92328-X}}, Page 235.</ref>

=== ''Robot Monster'' (1953) ===
{{Main|Robot Monster{{!}}''Robot Monster''}}
''Robot Monster'' is a [[science-fiction film]] produced and directed by [[Phil Tucker]] and originally shot and exhibited in [[3-D film|3D]]. Its title character, which is "a man in a gorilla suit wearing what looks like a diving helmet sprouting TV antennae", was given the Most Ridiculous Monster in Screen History award in ''The Golden Turkey Awards''.<ref name="newcastlerobot"/> It is also featured in ''[[The Book of Lists]]''{{'}} 10 worst movies list,{{sfn|Book of Lists|page=208}} ''The Fifty Worst Films of All Time'' and Michael Sauter's book ''The Worst Movies of All Time''.{{sfn|Sauter|page=326}}<ref name="newcastlerobot">{{cite web |last=Cerabona |first=Ron |title=So bad it's good: retro sci-fi's monster appeal |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/449342/so-bad-its-good-retro-sci-fis-monster-appeal/ |website=[[The Newcastle Herald]] |access-date=July 22, 2022 |language=en-AU |date=October 30, 2012 |archive-date=July 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220722140503/https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/449342/so-bad-its-good-retro-sci-fis-monster-appeal/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Robot Monster'' was featured in an episode of the movie-mocking TV show ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'',<ref name="newcastlerobot"/> as well as ''Canned Film Festival''.<ref name="cannedfilm"/> The film is remembered fondly by horror novelist [[Stephen King]], who quotes, and agrees with, a review in ''[[Castle of Frankenstein]]'' magazine ("certainly among the finest terrible movies ever made", "one of the most laughable [[Poverty Row|poverty row]] quickies").<ref>{{cite book |first=Stephen |last=King |author-link=Stephen King |title=Danse Macabre |year=1981 |publisher=Everest House |location=New York |isbn=978-0-89696-076-3|title-link=Danse Macabre (King book) }}</ref> Chris Barsanti in ''The Sci-Fi Movie Guide'' writes: "[''Robot Monster''] gives ''Plan 9 From Outer Space'' a run as the worst movie of all time."<ref>{{cite book |last=Barsanti |first=Chris |title=The Sci-Fi Movie Guide: The Universe of Film from Alien to Zardoz |date=2014 |publisher=[[Visible Ink Press]] |isbn=978-1578595334 |pages=312}}</ref>

=== ''The Conqueror'' (1956) ===
{{Main|The Conqueror (1956 film){{!}}''The Conqueror'' (1956 film)}}
[[File:The_Conqueror_(1956)_film_poster.jpg|thumb|The 1956 [[epic film|film epic]] ''[[The Conqueror (1956 film)|The Conqueror]]'' featured [[John Wayne]] as Asian warlord [[Genghis Khan]], cited as one of the most miscast roles ever<ref name="terrible10">{{cite web |last=Walters |first=Jack |title=10 Terrible Movies You Don't Have To See To Know They're Bad |url=https://screenrant.com/terrible-movies-not-see-know-bad/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=March 29, 2024 |language=en |date=26 July 2023}}</ref>]]
[[Howard Hughes]] funded ''[[The Conqueror (1956 film)|The Conqueror]]'', an [[epic film]] featuring [[John Wayne]] as [[Mongolia]]n chieftain [[Genghis Khan]] and the redheaded [[Susan Hayward]] as a [[Tatars|Tatar]] princess. The movie was filmed near [[St. George, Utah]], downwind from a [[Nevada Test Site|nuclear testing range]] in [[Nevada]], and is often blamed for the [[cancer]] deaths of many of the cast and crew, including Hayward, Wayne, [[Agnes Moorehead]], [[Pedro Armendáriz]], and director [[Dick Powell]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Cecil |title=Did John Wayne die of cancer caused by a radioactive movie set? |publisher=The Straight Dope |date=October 26, 1984 |url=http://www.straightdope.com/classics/a2_016.html |access-date=March 7, 2011 |archive-date=July 3, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080703225341/http://www.straightdope.com/classics/a2_016.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In addition to filming near the testing range, truckloads of the red sands were transported back to the studios for interior scenes<ref name="telekhan"/> and by 1980, 91 of the 220 (over 41%) cast and crew members had been diagnosed with cancer.<ref name=geng>{{cite news|last=von Tunzelmann|first=Alex|title=The Conqueror: Hollywood gives Genghis Khan a kicking he won't forget|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/filmblog/2013/may/03/the-conqueror-hollywood-genghis-khan|newspaper=The Guardian|date=May 3, 2013|location=London|access-date=December 12, 2016|archive-date=June 23, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130623112047/http://www.guardian.co.uk/film/filmblog/2013/may/03/the-conqueror-hollywood-genghis-khan|url-status=live}}</ref>

The film made the ten-worst list in ''The Book of Lists'',{{sfn|Book of Lists|page=208}} appears in Michael Sauter's ''The Worst Movies of All Time'',{{sfn|Sauter|page=68–71}} and was among those listed in ''The Fifty Worst Films of All Time''. Additionally, the ''[[Aldergrove Star]]'' described ''The Conqueror'' as the worst ever made and ''[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]'' listed it as the worst biopic ever made.<ref>{{cite web |last=Grewal |first=Joti |title=Former Aldergrove Star editor releases book, soon-to-be documentary about 'worst movie ever made' |url=https://www.aldergrovestar.com/home/former-aldergrove-star-editor-releases-book-soon-to-be-documentary-about-worst-movie-ever-made/ |website=[[Aldergrove Star]] |access-date=July 26, 2022 |date=September 27, 2021 |archive-date=March 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230307010926/https://www.aldergrovestar.com/home/former-aldergrove-star-editor-releases-book-soon-to-be-documentary-about-worst-movie-ever-made/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Barone |first=Matt |title=The 10 Worst Biopic Movies Of All Time |work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]] |date=November 12, 2012 |url=http://www.complex.com/pop-culture/2012/11/10-worst-biopic-movies-of-all-time/ |access-date=July 7, 2017 |archive-date=August 13, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813211848/http://www.complex.com/pop-culture/2012/11/10-worst-biopic-movies-of-all-time/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The Guardian]]'' called the choice of Wayne for Khan – a role originally written for [[Marlon Brando]] – "one of the worst casting decisions of all time".<ref name="geng"/> Despite Wayne having lobbied for the lead role after reading the script,<ref>{{cite book |last=Monush |first=Barry |title=Screen World Presents the Encyclopedia of Hollywood Film Actors: From the Silent Era to 1965 |publisher=Hal Leonard Corporation |year=2003 |page=773 |isbn=1-55783-551-9}}</ref> he later lamented having taken it, stating, "Don't make an ass of yourself trying to play parts you are not suited for."<ref name="telekhan">{{cite web |last=Bell |first=Chris |title=The movie so toxic it killed John Wayne: the tragedy of The Conqueror |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/movie-toxic-killed-john-wayne-tragedy-conqueror/ |website=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |access-date=July 23, 2022 |date=January 17, 2017 |archive-date=July 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708152313/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/movie-toxic-killed-john-wayne-tragedy-conqueror/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' writes: "by absolutely every conceivable metric – financially, critically, historically, ethnically, and even body count – it would come to be known as one of the biggest disasters in cinematic history."<ref name="telekhan"/> ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' described the film as the worst decision in movie history.<ref name="50decisions">{{cite magazine |last=Greene |first=Andy |title=The 50 Worst Decisions in Movie History |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-lists/the-50-worst-decisions-in-movie-history-1234824872/the-conqueror-casts-john-wayne-as-genghis-khan-films-on-a-nuclear-testing-site-1234827135/ |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=October 25, 2023 |date=September 25, 2023 |archive-date=October 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001221023/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-lists/the-50-worst-decisions-in-movie-history-1234824872/the-conqueror-casts-john-wayne-as-genghis-khan-films-on-a-nuclear-testing-site-1234827135/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Hughes, one of the world's wealthiest people at the time, had previously produced the successful dramatic films ''[[Hell's Angels (film)|Hell's Angels]]'', ''[[Scarface (1932 film)|Scarface]]'', and ''[[The Outlaw]]''.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/april/5/newsid_4739000/4739940.stm |title=BBC On This Day &#124; 5 &#124; 1976: Billionaire Howard Hughes dies |work=BBC News |date=April 7, 1976 |access-date=November 18, 2013 |archive-date=December 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171216160139/http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/april/5/newsid_4739000/4739940.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> After viewing ''The Conqueror'', Hughes bought every existing print for $12 million and refused to let the film be seen on TV until 1974, reportedly out of guilt over the decision to shoot at such a hazardous location.<ref>{{cite book |title=My Year of Flops |last=Rubin |first=Nathan |year=2010 |publisher=[[Charles Scribner's Sons|Scribner]] |isbn=978-1-4391-5312-3 |url=https://archive.org/details/myyearofflopsavc0000rabi }}</ref> This was the last film Hughes produced.<ref name="telekhan"/>

=== ''Fire Maidens from Outer Space'' (1956) ===
{{Main|Fire Maidens from Outer Space{{!}}''Fire Maidens from Outer Space''}}
''Fire Maidens from Outer Space'', a low-budget British [[space opera]] film (known in the US as ''Fire Maidens of Outer Space''), is about a group of astronauts visiting an all-female society on a moon of [[Jupiter]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dvddrive-in.com/reviews/e-h/firemaidensofouterspaceblu56.htm|title=Fire Maidens of Outer Space|website=dvddrive-in.com|access-date=July 18, 2021|archive-date=June 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603133337/http://dvddrive-in.com/reviews/e-h/firemaidensofouterspaceblu56.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> This film developed a negative reputation for its poor special effects (including a scene on the alien planet in which an automobile is visible driving past).<ref name="dt">{{Cite web |url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/61441/fire-maidens-of-outer-space/ |title=Fire Maidens Of Outer Space |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812024858/https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/61441/fire-maidens-of-outer-space/ |archive-date=August 12, 2020 |work=DVD Talk |date=August 13, 2013 |access-date=January 21, 2014}}</ref> Leslie Halliwell described ''Fire Maidens from Outer Space'' as "a strong contender for the title of the worst movie ever made, with diaphanously clad English gals striking embarrassed poses against cardboard sets".<ref>John Walker (ed.) ''Halliwell's Film and Video Guide 2000'', London and New York; HarperCollins, 1999, {{ISBN|0-06-273645-0}} (p.287).</ref> British film historian I.Q. Hunter included it in his list of candidates for "the worst British film ever made".<ref name="iqh">I. Q Hunter, "From Window Cleaner to Potato Man" in ''British Comedy Cinema'', edited by I.Q. Hunter and Laraine Porter. Routledge, 2012. {{ISBN|0-415-66667-8}}. (p.154)</ref> The [[DVD Talk]] website's review claimed it "may be among the worst-ever professionally produced science fiction films".<ref name="dt"/> Paul Welsh of the ''[[Borehamwood & Elstree Times]]'' wrote that it was "probably the worst [film] ever produced".<ref>{{cite web |last=Welsh |first=Paul |title=The worst film ever made? |url=https://www.borehamwoodtimes.co.uk/news/19747083.fire-maidens-outer-space---worst-film-ever-made/ |website=[[Borehamwood & Elstree Times]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=November 28, 2021 |archive-date=July 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710191835/https://www.borehamwoodtimes.co.uk/news/19747083.fire-maidens-outer-space---worst-film-ever-made/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In his book ''Operation Hollywood: How the Pentagon Shapes and Censors the Movies'', David L. Robb wrote that the film's director [[Cy Roth]] is "widely regarded as one of the worst filmmakers of all time", adding that, out of the three films he made, "the worst was ''Fire Maidens from Outer Space''...which is often cited as one of the ten worst movies ever made".<ref>{{cite book |last=Robb |first=David L. |title=Operation Hollywood: How the Pentagon Shapes and Censors the Movies |date=2004 |publisher=Prometheus Books |location=Amherst, NY |isbn=9781591021827 |page=321 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=j1wbAQAAIAAJ |access-date=July 13, 2022 |archive-date=October 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231025172902/https://books.google.com/books?id=j1wbAQAAIAAJ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''Plan 9 from Outer Space'' (1957) ===
{{Main|Plan 9 from Outer Space{{!}}''Plan 9 from Outer Space''}}
[[Ed Wood]]'s ''Plan 9 from Outer Space'', a [[science fiction]] film about aliens resurrecting the dead, was labeled the "Worst Film Ever" by ''The Golden Turkey Awards'' in 1980.<ref name="Rabin9">{{cite web |last=Rabin |first=Nathan |author-link=Nathan Rabin |title=Control Nathan Rabin 4.0 #126 Plan 9 From Outer Space (1957) |url=https://www.nathanrabin.com/happy-place/2020/9/16/control-nathan-rabin-40-126-plan-9-from-outer-space-1957 |website=Nathan Rabin's Happy Place |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=September 16, 2020 |archive-date=October 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221010212057/https://www.nathanrabin.com/happy-place/2020/9/16/control-nathan-rabin-40-126-plan-9-from-outer-space-1957 |url-status=live }}</ref> Wood had shot only a small amount of unrelated footage featuring top-billed star [[Bela Lugosi]] before Lugosi's death. Wood incorporated the footage into the film and cast [[Tom Mason (actor, born 1920)|Tom Mason]] as Lugosi's [[body double]]; Mason, a personal acquaintance of Wood, bore little resemblance to Lugosi and played his scenes holding the character's cape in front of his face. Although ''Golden Turkey Awards'' author Michael Medved credits Lugosi's top billing with its enduring legacy,<ref>{{cite web |last=Liebenson |first=Donald |title=Plan 9 from Outer Space Lands in TCM Classic Film Festival |url=https://www.tcm.com/articles/Article/021336/plan-9-from-outer-space-lands-in-tcm-classic-film-festival/ |date=May 7, 2021 |access-date=July 10, 2022 |publisher=[[Turner Classic Movies]] |archive-date=July 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710104952/https://www.tcm.com/articles/Article/021336/plan-9-from-outer-space-lands-in-tcm-classic-film-festival/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The Independent]]'' listed various other shortcomings: "A [[UFO]] dangling in the sky has been variously said to be either a car hubcap or a paper plate.
