Maltin]] described the film as being "more like a TV commercial than a movie",<ref name="Maltin01211"/> and Marjorie Baumgarten of the ''[[Austin Chronicle]]'' called it a "shameless ''E.T.'' knockoff".<ref name="rottentomatoes1"/> ''Mac and Me'' is widely regarded as one of the worst films ever made,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://screenrant.com/movies-with-bizarre-weird-source-material/|title=15 Movies With Bizarre Source Material|last=McGranaghan|first=Mike|date=March 21, 2017|website=[[Screen Rant]]|access-date=June 23, 2018|archive-date=June 24, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624035654/https://screenrant.com/movies-with-bizarre-weird-source-material/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://movieweb.com/mac-and-me-movie-alternate-ending-video/|title=Alternate Mac and Me Ending Unearthed and It's Insane|last=Millican|first=Josh|date=August 8, 2018|work=[[MovieWeb]]|access-date=December 15, 2018|archive-date=September 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911081746/https://movieweb.com/mac-and-me-movie-alternate-ending-video/|url-status=live}}</ref> with ''[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]'' reporting that it is "frequently pulled out in 'worst film of all time' arguments".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/2016/07/18/top-aliens-in-the-movies/mac-and-me/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/2016/07/18/top-aliens-in-the-movies/mac-and-me/ |archive-date=January 11, 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Top 20 aliens in the movies|date=December 19, 2017|website=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|access-date=April 27, 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Filmmaker [[Morgan Spurlock]] (responsible for the 2004 Oscar-nominated ''[[Super Size Me]]'') declared it the "worst thing you'll ever see in your entire life", as well as the most egregious example of [[product placement]] in cinema history.<ref name="crow">{{cite news|url=https://movies.yahoo.com/blogs/movie-talk/morgan-spurlock-dubs-mac-worst-movie-ever-sold-060910653.html|date=April 22, 2011|last=Crow|first=Jonathan|work=[[Yahoo! Movies]]|access-date=August 29, 2013|title=Morgan Spurlock Dubs 'Mac and Me' the Worst Film Ever Sold|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120405070102/http://movies.yahoo.com/blogs/movie-talk/morgan-spurlock-dubs-mac-worst-movie-ever-sold-060910653.html|archive-date=April 5, 2012}}</ref> The film was also named the worst ever in the ''[[San Francisco Chronicle]]'',<ref>{{cite news|date=January 22, 2017|title=Mac and Me|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|quote=McDonald's created an 'E.T.' rip-off called 'Mac and Me' in 1988&nbsp;... It's the worst movie ever made.}}</ref> as well as by broadcaster [[Simon Mayo]]<ref name="mayo">{{cite episode|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p03slrls|title=Paul Rudd and Chris Evans interviewed by Simon Mayo|series=Kermode and Mayo's Film Review |date=April 29, 2016|station=[[BBC Radio 5 Live]]|access-date=April 27, 2018|time=10 minutes|quote=''Mac and Me''... we're talking about the worst film ever made.|archive-date=May 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180510202715/https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p03slrls|url-status=live}}</ref> and writer/producer [[Damon Lindelof]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gq.com/story/damon-lindelof-paul-alien-comedy|title=Damon Lindelof's Open Letter to Paul the Alien|last=Lindelof|first=Damon|author-link=Damon Lindelof|date=March 14, 2011|magazine=[[GQ]]|access-date=April 27, 2018|archive-date=April 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428093747/https://www.gq.com/story/damon-lindelof-paul-alien-comedy|url-status=live}}</ref> Michael Hayden of ''[[GQ (Indian edition)|GQ India]]'' referred to it as "hands down the worst family movie in Hollywood history".<ref name="gqindia">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gqindia.com/content/6-best-bad-films/#s-cust0|title=The 6 best bad films|last=Hayden|first=Michael|date=November 10, 2011|magazine=[[GQ (Indian edition)|GQ India]]|access-date=May 11, 2018|archive-date=May 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180512044317/https://www.gqindia.com/content/6-best-bad-films/#s-cust0|url-status=live}}</ref> The film was nominated for four Razzie Awards including Worst Picture and Worst Screenplay, and won two trophies: Worst Director for [[Stewart Raffill]] (tied with [[Blake Edwards]] for ''[[Sunset (1988 film)|Sunset]]'') and Worst New Star for [[Ronald McDonald]] in a cameo. ''Mac and Me'' has however [[Mac and Me#In popular culture|gained a cult following]] and was featured on the second season of the ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'' revival (the only Razzie-winning film ever to be riffed in the history of the show).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thrillist.com/entertainment/nation/mcdonalds-mac-and-me-paul-rudd-movie-et-spinoff|title=How McDonald's Bizarre 'E.T.' Knockoff Got Made|last=Patches|first=Matt|date=April 3, 2017|website=[[Thrillist]]|access-date=December 11, 2017|archive-date=December 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211213637/https://www.thrillist.com/entertainment/nation/mcdonalds-mac-and-me-paul-rudd-movie-et-spinoff|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.nerdist.com/mac-and-me-bottleneck-gallery-figure-pins/|title=Mac and Me Finally (?) Gets Figure and Pin Collection|last=McNally|first=Victoria|date=April 24, 2017|website=[[Nerdist Industries|Nerdist]]|access-date=May 11, 2018|archive-date=May 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180512044315/https://nerdist.com/mac-and-me-bottleneck-gallery-figure-pins/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uproxx.com/tv/mystery-science-theater-3000-mac-and-me-season-2/|title='Mystery Science Theater 3000' Will Tackle 'Mac And Me' In Season 2|website=Uproxx|date=November 12, 2018|access-date=January 3, 2020|archive-date=January 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200103134816/https://uproxx.com/tv/mystery-science-theater-3000-mac-and-me-season-2/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbr.com/mst3k-movies-good-without-the-riffing/|title=10 MST3K Movies You Should Watch Without The Riffing|first=Derek|last=Faraci|date=June 12, 2022|website=CBR|access-date=February 12, 2023|archive-date=February 12, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230212014327/https://www.cbr.com/mst3k-movies-good-without-the-riffing/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== ''Things'' (1989) ===
{{Main|Things (film){{!}}''Things'' (film)}}
''Things'', a 1989 Canadian [[low budget]], [[independent film|independent]], [[shot-on-video film|shot on video]] horror [[exploitation film]], was written and produced by Andrew Jordan and Barry J. Gillis. It cost approximately $35,000 in total to make<ref name="CANUX">{{cite web|url=http://www.canuxploitation.com/review/things.html|title=''Things'' review|website=Canuxploitation|access-date=December 28, 2013|archive-date=September 29, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130929234728/http://www.canuxploitation.com/review/things.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and marked the mainstream film debut of porn star [[Amber Lynn]]. It was ostensibly made as [[Homage (arts)|homage]] to horror icons and films, such as [[George A. Romero]] and his ''[[Night of the Living Dead]]'' franchise.<ref name="CO1">{{cite web|url=http://www.critcononline.com/films_on_the_fringe.htm|title=Films on the Fringe: Things (1989)|website=Critic Online|access-date=June 7, 2009|archive-date=April 15, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090415201758/http://www.critcononline.com/films_on_the_fringe.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> Adam Symchuk of ''Screen Rant'' wrote: "While films like ''[[The Room]]'' and ''[[Birdemic: Shock and Terror|Birdemic]]'' seem to be constant contenders for the best 'so bad it's good' movie, [''Things''] is the true unheralded champion among many [[Cinephilia|cinephiles]]."<ref>{{cite web |title=It Came From The North: 10 Great Monster Movies From Canada |url=https://screenrant.com/great-monster-movies-from-canada/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |last=Symchuk |first=Adam |access-date=July 26, 2022 |date=September 30, 2020 |archive-date=July 26, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220726091201/https://screenrant.com/great-monster-movies-from-canada/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Likewise, Jeff Kirschner of ''[[Dread Central]]'' nominated it as the worst movie ever made and [[Will Pfeifer]] opined that "It's so terrible I can't think of another movie that even comes close."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dreadcentral.com/news/142337/things-worst-movie-ever-made/|title=Things: The Worst Movie Ever Made|date=December 10, 2015|website=[[Dread Central]]|last=Kirschner|first=Jeff|access-date=July 26, 2022|archive-date=December 4, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221204173115/https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/142337/things-worst-movie-ever-made/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Pfeifer |first=Will |author-link=Will Pfeifer |title=Monsters, mullets meet for snoozefest |url=https://www.jacksonnewspapers.com/x1348677046/Will-Pfeifer-Monsters-mullets-meet-for-snoozefest |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210902063835/https://www.jacksonnewspapers.com/x1348677046/Will-Pfeifer-Monsters-mullets-meet-for-snoozefest |newspaper=[[Jackson Herald|Jackson Newspapers]] |access-date=July 26, 2022 |date=October 17, 2008 |archive-date=September 2, 2021 |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, ''RiffTrax'' concluded that ''Things'' was the worst movie that they had ever spoofed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nelson |first1=Mike J. |author-link1=Michael J. Nelson |last2=Murphy |first2=Kevin |author-link2=Kevin Murphy (actor) |last3=Corbett |first3=Bill |author-link3=Bill Corbett |title=Things |url=https://www.rifftrax.com/things |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220305141159/https://www.rifftrax.com/things |website=[[Rifftrax]] |archive-date=March 5, 2022 |access-date=July 26, 2022 |language=en |date=March 4, 2022}}</ref>

== 1990s ==

=== ''Troll 2'' (1990) ===
{{Main|Troll 2{{!}}''Troll 2''}}
Despite its title, ''Troll 2'' does not feature any trolls (the antagonists are actually [[goblin]]s) and has no relation to the [[Troll (1986 film)|original 1986 film]]. ''Troll 2'' was produced under the title ''"Goblins"'', but the title was changed by American distributors.<ref name="GriggsTroll" /> In the film, an American family vacations to the town of Nilbog (goblin spelled backwards), where vegetarian goblins attempt to turn the family into edible plants.<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies"/> It was shot in [[Utah]] and the cast was composed of local amateur actors. A [[language barrier]] developed between the cast and the Italian crew, led by director [[Claudio Fragasso]], who had translated the script to English.<ref name="GriggsTroll">{{cite web |last1=Griggs |first1=Brandon |title=Troll 2: As camp as it gets |url=https://archive.sltrib.com/story.php?ref=/arts/ci_5457861 |website=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]] |date=March 17, 2007 |access-date=December 30, 2024}}</ref> The bad acting and dialogue have become notorious for their [[Camp (style)|camp]] value,<ref name="GriggsTroll" /> with individual scenes having become Internet memes.<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies"/><ref name="collidertroll">{{cite web |last1=Berchtold |first1=Trent |title=The 10 Most Rewatchable Bad Horror Movies, Ranked |url=https://collider.com/bad-horror-movies-rewatchable-ranked/ |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=December 30, 2024 |language=en |date=September 29, 2024}}</ref> In 2009, [[Michael Stephenson (filmmaker)|Michael Stephenson]], the child star of ''Troll 2'', released ''[[Best Worst Movie]]'', a documentary exploring the film's tumultuous production and its unexpected cult following.<ref name="trollbestworst"/>

[[NPR]] reports that it is "known as the worst movie of all time"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=105420828 |title=The Beauty Of The 'Best Worst Movie' |work=NPR |date=June 15, 2009 |publisher=[[NPR]] |access-date=June 15, 2009 |archive-date=June 20, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090620200356/http://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=105420828 |url-status=live }}</ref> while ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' calls it "a popular candidate for the worst film ever made".<ref name="trollbestworst">{{cite web |url=https://avclub.com/article/ibest-worst-movie-iuncovers-the-heartbreaking-psyc-95807 |title=Best Worst Movie uncovers the heartbreaking psychodrama in a memorably insane B-movie |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |last=Rabin |first=Nathan |author-link=Nathan Rabin |date=March 29, 2013 |access-date=March 29, 2013 |archive-date=May 16, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140516063721/http://www.avclub.com/article/ibest-worst-movie-iuncovers-the-heartbreaking-psyc-95807 |url-status=live }}</ref> Likewise, ''[[TV Guide]]'' proclaimed that "''Troll 2'' is really as bad as they come",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/movies/troll-2/review/129231 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170426044557/http://www.tvguide.com/movies/troll-2/review/129231/ |title=Troll 2 Review |work=[[TV Guide]] |archive-date=April 26, 2017 |access-date=March 5, 2014}}</ref> and Ken Hanke of ''[[Mountain Xpress]]'' stated in his review that: "There are movies that are bad. There are movies that are so-bad-they're-good. And then there's ''Troll 2''—a movie that's so bad that it defies comprehension."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mountainx.com/movies/review/troll_2 |title=Movie Review: Troll 2 |work=[[Mountain Xpress]] |last=Hanke |first=Ken |date=July 23, 2008 |access-date=March 5, 2014 |archive-date=October 19, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019171306/http://www.mountainx.com/movies/review/troll_2 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Troll 2'' regularly appears on lists of films considered the worst, including: ''Flavorwire'',<ref name="Flavorwire"/> ''[[Fotogramas]]'',<ref name="fotogramas">{{cite web |last=Rosado |first=Ricardo |title=Las 20 peores películas de la historia del cine: un homenaje |url=https://www.fotogramas.es/noticias-cine/g19447838/20-peores-peliculas-historia/?slide=19 |website=[[Fotogramas]] |access-date=January 26, 2022 |language=es-ES |date=October 1, 2020}}</ref> ''IGN'',<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies"/> Rotten Tomatoes,<ref name="sobad"/> ''Screen Rant'',<ref name="Screen Rant"/> and ''Time Out''.<ref name="timeoutlist"/> Furthermore, ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]'' named it the most rewatchable bad movie of all time.<ref name="collidertroll" />

=== ''Highlander II: The Quickening'' (theatrical version, 1991) ===
{{Main|Highlander II: The Quickening{{!}}''Highlander II: The Quickening''}}
The French-British film ''Highlander II: The Quickening'' is a sequel to the 1986 cult film ''[[Highlander (film)|Highlander]]'', which transitions the [[fantasy]] of the original film into [[science fiction]], and [[retcons]] the mystical warriors of the first film into [[Extraterrestrial life|aliens]]. It received a harsh reception from both critics and audiences, as it has a 0% score on Rotten Tomatoes and appears on its 100 Worst Movies of All Time.<ref name="rt100worst">{{cite web |title=Bad Movies: The 100 Worst Movies of All Time |url=https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/guide/worst-movies-of-all-time/ |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date=March 10, 2024}}</ref> Common criticisms included the lack of motivation for the characters, blatant disregard for backstory from the first film (such as the new and seemingly incongruent origin for the Immortals and the unexplained resurrection of Ramírez), glaring plot holes, a messy and nonsensical story structure, the filmmaker's inability to balance unrelated plots and subplots, and obvious contradictions in the film's internal logic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2000/06/16/highlander-2-renegade-version|title=Highlander 2: Renegade Version|author=I. G. N. Staff|date=June 16, 2000|website=IGN}}</ref> In selecting it as the worst movie sequel of all time, ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' also wrote that "it is typically considered one of the worst films of all time'.<ref>{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Isaac |title=The 10 Worst Movie Sequels Ever, Ranked |url=https://www.cbr.com/worst-movie-sequels-ever/ |publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]] |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=January 5, 2022}}</ref> Roger Ebert named it the worst film of 1991, stating: "If there is a planet somewhere whose civilization is based on the worst movies of all time, ''Highlander 2: The Quickening'' deserves a sacred place among their most treasured artifacts."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/highlander-2-the-quickening-1991 |title=Highlander 2: The Quickening movie review (1991) |first=Roger |last=Ebert |author-link=Roger Ebert |work=Chicago Sun-Times |date=November 1, 1991 |access-date=October 10, 2020}}</ref> An ''[[IGN]]'' review said: "How bad is this movie? Well, imagine if [[Ed Wood]] were alive today, and someone gave him a multi-million dollar budget. See his imagination running rampant, bringing in aliens from outer space with immensely powerful firearms, immortals who bring each other back to life by calling out their names, epic duels on flying skateboards, and a blatant disregard for anything logical or previously established—now you are starting to get closer to the vision of ''Highlander II''."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2000/06/16/highlander-2-renegade-version |title=Highlander 2: Renegade Version Review |work=IGN |date=June 16, 2000}}</ref> ''Screen Rant'' has since included it on its list of the 25 worst films of all time.<ref name="Screen Rant"/>

In 1995, the film's director [[Russell Mulcahy]] made a [[director's cut]] version known as ''Highlander 2: Renegade Version'' and then later released another version simply known as ''Highlander 2: The Special Edition'' for its 2004 DVD release. The film was reconstructed on both occasions largely from existing material, with certain scenes removed and others added back in, and the entire sequence of events changed. The reconstructed film's reception was far better than the original's; it was elevated to a mixed reception.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://joblo.com/horror-movies/news/highlander-ii-there-can-be-only-four-cuts---part-2|title = Highlander II: There can be only four cuts!| work = JoBlo Movie Network|date = November 24, 2010|access-date = March 16, 2013}}</ref>

=== ''Super Mario Bros.'' (1993) ===
{{main|Super Mario Bros. (film){{!}}''Super Mario Bros.'' (film)}}
[[File:Bob hoskins filming ruby blue cropped (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Oscar-nominated actor [[Bob Hoskins]] (pictured in 2006) described ''Super Mario Bros.'' as "the worst thing I ever did" later in his life.]]
The first [[feature-length]] live-action film based on a video game, ''Super Mario Bros.'' was directed by the husband-and-wife team of [[Rocky Morton]] and [[Annabel Jankel]] (known for their work on ''[[Max Headroom (TV series)|Max Headroom]]''). It follows the brothers [[Mario]] ([[Bob Hoskins]]) and [[Luigi (character)|Luigi]] ([[John Leguizamo]]), plumbers who venture into a parallel universe to rescue [[Princess Daisy]] ([[Samantha Mathis]]) from the villainous [[Bowser|King Koopa]] ([[Dennis Hopper]]). The ''[[Super Mario]]'' series' publisher, [[Nintendo]], believed the [[Mario (franchise)|''Mario'' franchise]] was strong enough for experimentation and gave the filmmakers free creative license.<ref name="Wired: MarioSucked">{{cite magazine |last=Russell |first=Jamie |title=Why the Super Mario Movie Sucked |url=https://www.wired.com/2012/04/generation-xbox-super-mario-movie/ |magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=April 23, 2012}}</ref> The finished film bears little resemblance to the games,<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies">{{cite web |last=Bibbiani |first=William |title=The Best Worst Movies Ever Made: The Room, Super Mario Bros. and More |url=https://sea.ign.com/breakin-2-electric-boogaloo/180321/feature/the-best-worst-movies-ever-made-the-room-super-mario-bros-and-more |website=[[IGN]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=December 27, 2021}}</ref> trading their colorful [[Mushroom Kingdom]] for a [[Dystopia|dystopic]] world populated by humanoid dinosaurs.<ref name="Wired: MarioSucked"/><ref name="RiffTrax: Mario"/> ''[[SyFy Wire]]'' wrote: "Some movies are so bad that they're secretly good. ''Super Mario Bros.'' is so bad it crushes your spirit. It's unfathomably terrible."<ref name="SyFy: Mario">{{cite web |last=Grierson |first=Tim |title=This week in genre history: Super Mario Bros. the movie gets an instant 'game over' |url=https://www.syfy.com/syfy-wire/super-mario-bros-movie-genre-history |website=[[SyFy Wire]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=May 26, 2020}}</ref> The film was criticized for its inconsistent tone, complex narrative, and lack of faithfulness to the source material.<ref>{{Cite AV media |last1=Siskel |first1=Gene |last2=Ebert |first2=Roger |date=August 18, 2008 |title=Siskel & Ebert Review 'Super Mario Bros.' |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QbEH66qiwrY |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810150516/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QbEH66qiwrY |archive-date=August 10, 2016 |access-date=November 28, 2016 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Walsh |first=Michael |title=8 Things Fans Want To See In The Super Mario Movie |url=https://collider.com/things-fans-want-super-mario-movie/ |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=June 22, 2022}}</ref> According to ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', ''Super Mario Bros.'' is a mainstay on lists compiling the worst films of all time.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shanfield |first1=Ethan  |title=Mario Powers Up: How Nintendo Visionary Shigeru Miyamoto and Illumination's Chris Meledandri Plan to Super Smash Hollywood |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/features/super-mario-bros-movie-shigeru-miyamoto-interview-1235572488/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=March 21, 2024 |date=April 4, 2023}}</ref> It was voted the sixth worst film of all time by [[RiffTrax]] in 2012,<ref name="RiffTrax: Mario">{{cite web |title=Worst Movies of All Time Top 10 |url=https://www.rifftrax.com/worst-movies-of-all-time-top-10 |publisher=[[RiffTrax]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=2012}}</ref> and ''[[IGN]]'' ranked it among the "best worst movies ever made" in 2021.<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies"/> Author [[David Bodanis]], in his 2020 book ''The Art of Fairness'', called ''Super Mario Bros.'' "the worst movie ever made".<ref>{{cite book |last=Bodanis |first=David |title=The Art of Fairness: The Power of Decency in a World Turned Mean |date=November 2020 |publisher=[[Abrams Books]] |isbn=9781647003869 |chapter=Directors |quote=The result was ''1941'', and while it's not the worst movie ever made—not when ''Super Mario Bros.'' is still available—it's definitely a contender.}}</ref>

In addition to scathing reviews, ''Super Mario Bros.'' was a [[box-office bomb]], and Morton and Jankel were "[[Blacklisting|blacklisted]]" as directors in Hollywood.<ref name="SyFy: Mario"/> In a 2007 interview, Hoskins said: "The worst thing I ever did? ''Super Mario Bros.'' It was a fuckin' nightmare. The whole experience was a nightmare. It had a husband-and-wife team directing, whose arrogance had been mistaken for talent. After so many weeks their own agent told them to get off the set! Fuckin' nightmare. Fuckin' idiots."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hattenstone |first=Simon |date=August 3, 2007 |title=The Method? Living it out? Cobblers! |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2007/aug/03/2 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161216193111/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2007/aug/03/2 |archive-date=December 16, 2016 |access-date=December 13, 2016 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> In a 2011 interview, he was asked, "What is the worst job you've done?", "What has been your biggest disappointment?", and "If you could edit your past, what would you change?" His answer to all three was ''Super Mario Bros.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenstreet |first=Rosanna |date=June 17, 2011 |title=Q&A: Bob Hoskins |url=https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2011/jun/18/bob-hoskins-interview-neverland |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110021801/http://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2011/jun/18/bob-hoskins-interview-neverland |archive-date=November 10, 2013 |access-date=December 13, 2016 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The film made Nintendo wary of licensing its works to film studios,<ref name="Sony">{{cite news|last=Vary|first=Adam|title=Sony Pictures Lands 'Mario Bros.' Movie Rights From Nintendo, Leaked Emails Show|url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/adambvary/sony-nintendo-mario-bros-movie#.duwkpjZgV|access-date=December 11, 2014|website=[[BuzzFeed News]]|date=December 11, 2014|archive-date=December 12, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141212093710/http://www.buzzfeed.com/adambvary/sony-nintendo-mario-bros-movie#.duwkpjZgV|url-status=live}}</ref> and it did not license ''Mario'' again until it collaborated with [[Illumination (company)|Illumination]] for ''[[The Super Mario Bros. Movie]]'' (2023) three decades later.<ref name="SyFy: Mario"/><ref name="terrible10"/> [[Seth Rogen]], who voiced [[Donkey Kong (character)|Donkey Kong]] in the 2023 film, called ''Super Mario Bros.'' one of the worst films ever made and what "made me realize that movies, like, could be bad. That never occurred to me until that moment."<ref>{{cite web |last=Malkin |first=Marc |title='Super Mario Bros. Movie' Star Seth Rogen Calls Original 1993 Adaptation 'One of the Worst Films Ever Made' |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/columns/super-mario-bros-seth-rogen-slams-original-movie-1235574029/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=March 21, 2024 |date=April 5, 2023}}</ref>

=== ''North'' (1994) ===
{{Main|North (1994 film){{!}}''North'' (1994 film)}}
[[File:Rob_Reiner_LBJ_Library_2016_-_DIG13955_105.jpg|thumb|Actor/director [[Rob Reiner]] (pictured in 2016) made the [[family film]] ''[[North (1994 film)|North]]'' (1994), which was panned by critics to the point that [[Roger Ebert]] famously declared he "hated, hated, hated this movie" on the [[film review]] show ''[[At the Movies (1986 TV program)|Siskel and Ebert at the Movies]]''.]]
The [[Rob Reiner]] film ''[[North (1994 film)|North]]'' is an adaptation of the novel ''North: The Tale of a 9-Year-Old Boy Who Becomes a Free Agent and Travels the World in Search of the Perfect Parents'' by [[Alan Zweibel]], who also wrote the screenplay and has a minor role in the film. ''North'', which stars [[Elijah Wood]] in the title role and also marked [[Scarlett Johansson]]'s film debut, was a critical and commercial failure, earning only $7,138,449 worldwide despite its budget of over $40 million. It was widely criticized for its plot, its cast of insensitive characters, lack of humor and portrayal of numerous ethnic stereotypes (especially Alaskan Inuit). It has a 14% approval rating at [[Rotten Tomatoes]].<ref>{{cite web |title=North Movie Reviews, Pictures – Rotten Tomatoes |work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |url=https://rottentomatoes.com/m/north/ |access-date=March 7, 2011}}</ref> [[Roger Ebert]] gave it zero stars and wrote, "I hated this movie. Hated hated hated hated hated this movie. Hated it. Hated every simpering stupid vacant audience-insulting moment of it. Hated the sensibility that thought anyone would like it. Hated the implied insult to the audience by its belief that anyone would be entertained by it."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://siskelebert.org/?p=493|title=Worst of 1994 – Siskel and Ebert Movie Reviews|website=siskelebert.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://siskelebert.org/?p=5388|title=The Client, Lassie, It Could Happen to You, North, Barcelona, 1994 – Siskel and Ebert Movie Reviews|website=siskelebert.org}}</ref> He continued saying "''North'' is a bad film – one of the worst movies ever made",<ref name="northebert">{{cite web |last=Ebert |first=Roger |author-link=Roger Ebert|title=North movie review & film summary (1994) |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/north-1994 |website=[[RogerEbert.com]] |date=July 22, 1994 |access-date=April 8, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> and it is also on his list of most hated films.<ref name="eberthated"/> Both Ebert and [[Gene Siskel]] named ''North'' as the worst film of 1994.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Official Site of Gene Siskel |work=Cmgww.com |url=http://www.cmgww.com/stars/siskel/screening_room/thumbs_down.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090226070236/http://www.cmgww.com/stars/siskel/screening_room/thumbs_down.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 26, 2009 |access-date=March 7, 2011}}</ref> [[Mick LaSalle]] of the ''San Francisco Chronicle'' said in his review that "''North'' is director Rob Reiner's first flat-out failure, a sincerely wrought, energetically made picture that all the same crashes on takeoff. It's strange and oddly distasteful, at its best managing to be bad in some original and unexpected ways."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/1995/01/06/dd59113.dtl |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031113141403/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=%2Fc%2Fa%2F1995%2F01%2F06%2Fdd59113.dtl |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 13, 2003 |work=[[The San Francisco Chronicle]] |title=Rob Reiner's 'North' Is Distastefully Bad |last=LaSalle |first=Mick |author-link=Mick LaSalle |date=January 8, 2011}}</ref> [[Richard Roeper]] named ''North'' as one of the 40 worst movies he has ever seen, saying that, "Of all the films on this list, ''North'' may be the most difficult to watch from start to finish."<ref name="RichardRoeper"/> The film was nominated for the following awards at the [[15th Golden Raspberry Awards]]: Worst Picture, Worst Actor ([[Bruce Willis]], also for ''[[Color of Night]]''), Worst Supporting Actress ([[Kathy Bates]]), Worst Supporting Actor ([[Dan Aykroyd]], also for ''[[Exit to Eden (film)|Exit to Eden]]''), Worst Director, and Worst Screenplay ([[Andrew Scheinman]] and [[Alan Zweibel]]).

=== ''Dis – en historie om kjærlighet'' (''A Story About Love'') (1995) ===
{{Main|A Story About Love{{!}}''A Story About Love''}}
The Norwegian [[romantic film]] ''Dis – en historie om kjærlighet'' was directed by Aune Sand. The film follows different couples and their love stories around the world, in [[Cairo]], [[Normandy]], [[Oslo]] and [[New York City]]. ''Dis'' received universally poor reviews by critics, and has been called the most poorly reviewed Norwegian film in history.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Kristoffersen|first=Marius Vartdal|title=Hva Var I Veien Med Dis?|url=http://znett.com/2011/05/hva-var-i-veien-med-dis/|date=May 3, 2011|access-date=July 14, 2014|magazine=[[Z Filmtidsskrift]]|language=no}}</ref><ref name="osloby.no"/> Critic Harald Kolstad of ''[[Dagsavisen]]'' gave it a score of zero, refused to acknowledge ''Dis'' as a film, and claimed to have never seen anything worse.<ref>{{cite news|last=Pedersen |first=Brent Erik |title=Hedrer Dagsavisens kritiker |url=http://www.dagsavisen.no/kultur/hedrer-dagsavisens-kritiker/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140617125554/http://www.dagsavisen.no/kultur/hedrer-dagsavisens-kritiker/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 17, 2014 |access-date=July 14, 2014 |newspaper=Dagsavisen|language=no }}</ref> ''[[Aftenposten]]'' referred to the film as "the largest turkey" and "the most reviled film",<ref name="osloby.no">{{cite news|title=Norges største kalkun flyr igjen|url=http://www.osloby.no/article199599_2.ece|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120814005215/http://www.osloby.no/article199599_2.ece|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 14, 2012|date=June 28, 2012|access-date=July 14, 2014|newspaper=Aftenposten|language=no}}</ref> and ''Total Film'' included it on its list of the 66 worst films ever made.<ref name="TotalFilm"/> Despite being a critical disaster it became a commercial success, gaining [[cult film]] status with a following akin to ''[[The Rocky Horror Picture Show]]'', with fans embracing its "so bad it's good" qualities.<ref name="osloby.no"/> Director Aune Sand insists that ''Dis'' is a masterpiece.<ref>{{cite news|title= Slakter norsk film|url=http://www.dagbladet.no/kultur/2005/07/20/437937.html|access-date=July 14, 2014|newspaper=Dagbladet|language=no}}</ref>

=== ''Showgirls'' (1995) ===
{{Main|Showgirls{{!}}''Showgirls''}}
[[File:Paul Verhoeven.jpg|thumb|Director [[Paul Verhoeven]], whose ''[[Showgirls]]''<ref name="2024lineup"/> earned a record 13 [[Golden Raspberry Award]] nominations, was the first person to attend the ceremony and [[List of people who have accepted Golden Raspberry Awards|accept the awards in person]].<ref>{{Cite news |last= Persall |first= Steve |title = 'Showgirls' gets razzed | newspaper = [[St. Petersburg Times]] |page = 2B |date = March 25, 1996}}</ref>]]
Hype for [[Paul Verhoeven]]'s [[erotic]] [[Drama (film and television)|drama]] ''Showgirls'' focused on the sex and nudity in this [[NC-17]] French-American film with a $45 million budget, but the final result was critically derided. Much hype revolved around the film's star, [[Elizabeth Berkley]], who only two years before had starred in the lighthearted and chaste teen [[situation comedy|sitcom]] ''[[Saved by the Bell]]''. The film won seven [[Golden Raspberry Award|Razzie Awards]], a record at that time, and received 13 nominations, a record that still stands. It received an additional award at the [[20th Golden Raspberry Awards]], where it was awarded Worst Picture of the Decade. Kenneth Turan of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' called it, "a film of thunderous oafishness that gives adult subject matter the kind of bad name it does not need or deserve".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rottentomatoes.com/m/showgirls/reviews/#page=2&sort=source |title=Showgirls – Movie Reviews |website=Rotten Tomatoes |access-date=March 5, 2014}}</ref> Michael Dequina of TheMovieReport.com also criticized the film, claiming that it was "the best bad filmmaking Hollywood has to offer".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://themoviereport.com/movierpt1.html#showgirls |title=The Movie Report Archive, Volume 1 |work=TheMovieReport.com |access-date=November 18, 2013}}</ref> Adam White wrote in ''[[The Independent]]'' that it was "the worst movie ever made" but also a masterpiece.<ref name="showgirlsindy">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/showgirls-elizabeth-berkley-paul-verhoeven-you-dont-nomi-documentary-a9407086.html |title=Showgirls: The remarkable resurrection of the worst movie ever made |work=[[The Independent]]|last=White|first=Adam|date=March 18, 2020|access-date=April 17, 2020}}</ref> Stephen Lynch of the ''[[Knight Ridder|Knight Ridder/Tribune]]'' similarly named it the worst movie ever made, calling it "so bad it may be brilliant".<ref>{{cite news |title=Critic picks worst movies of all time |first=Stephen|last=Lynch|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=398&dat=20011003&id=oGhOAAAAIBAJ&pg=6912,5443994|newspaper=Bartow Press |date=October 3, 2001 |access-date=June 12, 2014}}</ref> Various sources have since included ''Showgirls'' in their respective lists of the worst films ever made, including: Rotten Tomatoes, ''Empire'', ''Screen Rant'', ''Vanity Fair'', and ''Flavorwire''.<ref name="Flavorwire"/><ref name="Screen Rant"/><ref name="italianvanity"/><ref name="sobad"/><ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever"/> ''Showgirls'' was also featured in Michael Sauter's ''The Worst Movies of All Time'' as well as ''The Official Razzie Movie Guide''. Despite being a critical failure and failing at the box office initially, ''Showgirls'' found success as a [[Camp (style)|camp]] [[cult film]], particularly among the [[LGBT community]], but whether the film was intended to be satirical remains subject to debate.<ref name="showgirlsindy"/> On the [[home video]] market, the film was [[MGM]]'s most profitable release for years.<ref name="showgirlsindy"/>

=== ''The Scarlet Letter'' (1995) ===
{{Main|The Scarlet Letter (1995 film){{!}}''The Scarlet Letter'' (1995 film)}}
A "freely adapted" version of the [[The Scarlet Letter|1850 romantic novel]] by [[Nathaniel Hawthorne]], directed by [[Roland Joffé]] and starring [[Demi Moore]] and [[Gary Oldman]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/os-xpm-1995-10-13-9510110375-story.html|title='Scarlet Letter' is Untrue to the Hawthorne Tale|last=Boyar|first=Jay|date=October 13, 1995|website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> The film met with universally negative reviews<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deseretnews.com/top/705/7/The-Scarlet-Letter-20-best-selling-books-that-werent-as-acclaimed-as-film-adaptations.html|title=20 best-selling books that weren't as acclaimed as film adaptations|last=Purdy|first=Alicia|date=May 26, 2012|website=[[Deseret News]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213092221/https://www.deseretnews.com/top/705/7/The-Scarlet-Letter-20-best-selling-books-that-werent-as-acclaimed-as-film-adaptations.html|access-date=September 26, 2018|archive-date=December 13, 2013}}</ref> and was a [[box-office bomb]], grossing $10.4 million against a production budget of $46 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Scarlet Letter (1995)|url=https://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=scarletletter.htm|website=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=November 12, 2020}}</ref> Multiple critics named the film the worst of 1995.<ref name="hicks">{{cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/1995/12/22/19211366/best-worst-movies-of-1995|title=Best & Worst Movies of 1995|last=Hicks|first=Chris|date=December 22, 1995|website=[[Deseret News]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sfgate.com/entertainment/article/So-Bad-You-Can-t-Hate-Them-Demi-Moore-s-3017177.php|title=So Bad You Can't Hate Them|last=LaSalle|first=Mick|author-link=Mick LaSalle|date=December 30, 1995|website=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|access-date=November 6, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thecoast.ca/halifax/worst-film/BestOf?oid=10515293|title=Worst Film 1995|website=[[The Coast (newspaper)|The Coast]]|access-date=November 6, 2020}}</ref>

Chris Hicks of the ''[[Deseret News]]'' argued that its deviation from the source material represents "Hollywood's arrogance in its purest form".<ref name="hicks"/> ''[[The Washington Post]]''{{'}}s Amy E. Schwartz reported that the "nutty" film was described by numerous reviewers as the worst they had ever seen.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/opinions/1995/10/24/even-hawthorne-would-have-laughed/765e3169-7ffb-4b1f-934d-5b2c3c1468f5/|title=Even Hawthorne Would Have Laughed|last=Schwartz|first=Amy E|date=October 24, 1995|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> Kevin Williamson of ''[[National Review]]'' observed a "combination of awfulness and inexplicability", and claimed that "any objective and authoritative analysis will reveal that the worst film ever made is Demi Moore's version of ''The Scarlet Letter''".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nationalreview.com/media-blog/i-hate-disagree-my-betters-kevin-d-williamson/|title=I Hate to Disagree with My Betters...|last=Williamson|first=Kevin|date=February 19, 2009|website=[[National Review]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> Sadie Trombetta of ''[[Bustle (magazine)|Bustle]]'' wrote that it "has earned an almost permanent spot on every 'Worst Movie of All Time' list",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bustle.com/articles/121305-9-books-that-should-never-have-been-made-into-movies|title=9 Books That Should Never Have Been Movies|last=Trombetta|first=Sadie|date=November 5, 2015|website=[[Bustle (magazine)|Bustle]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> while author [[Libby Fischer Hellmann]] noted that it is "widely cited as the worst film adaptation ever made".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.libbyhellmann.com/5-great-books-movie-stinkers/|title=5 Great Books That Were Movie Stinkers|last=Hellmann|first=Libby Fischer|author-link=Libby Fischer Hellmann|date=August 7, 2016|website=LibbyHellmann.com|access-date=November 6, 2020|archive-date=May 20, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520165056/http://libbyhellmann.com/5-great-books-movie-stinkers/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The film was nominated for seven [[Golden Raspberry Awards]], winning "Worst Remake or Sequel". Furthermore, Roger Ebert placed the film on his "most hated" list.<ref name="eberthated"/>

===''Bio-Dome'' (1996)===
{{Main|Bio-Dome{{!}}''Bio-Dome''}}
The 1996 comedy film ''Bio-Dome'' focuses on two moronic stoner best friends, played by [[Pauly Shore]] and [[Stephen Baldwin]], who accidentally get trapped inside of the Bio-Dome, a hermetically sealed ecological system whose owner is played by [[Henry Gibson]], after mistaking it for a mall while looking for a bathroom.

For [[MTV News]], Eric Snider wrote in 2008 that "nothing can account for...the movie ''Bio-Dome'', which is–and I do not make this assertion lightly–the worst crime ever perpetrated against humanity throughout all of recorded history". Snider went on to call it "quite bad" and "certainly one of the worst comedies" he had ever seen, criticizing Pauly Shore's performance as unfunny and the film's writing as stupid.<ref>{{cite web |last=Snider |first=Eric |title=Eric's Bad Movies: Bio-Dome (1996) |url=http://www.mtv.com/news/2759537/erics-bad-movies-bio-dome-1996/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710185442/http://www.mtv.com/news/2759537/erics-bad-movies-bio-dome-1996/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 10, 2022 |website=[[MTV News]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=June 19, 2008}}</ref> [[Syfy|Syfy Wire]]{{'}}s Cassidy Ward described ''Bio-Dome'' as "one of the best-worst movies of all time", stating that its plot "strains credulity", while Jon O'Brien of ''[[Inverse (website)|Inverse]]'' called it "one of the worst movies ever made" and wrote that it "has nothing to offer but unconvincing pratfalls...tumbleweed one-liners...and some unashamed sexism, too".<ref>{{cite web |last=Ward |first=Cassidy |title=Bio-Dome was a stoner movie flop, but Biosphere 2 was a real experiment |url=https://www.syfy.com/syfy-wire/bio-dome-biosphere-2-real-science-movie |website=[[Syfy|Syfy Wire]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=January 13, 2021}}</ref><ref name="inversekylie">{{cite web |last=O'Brien |first=Jon |title=How a '90s sci-fi comedy became one of the worst movies ever made |url=https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/bio-dome-movie-science-fiction-anniversary |website=[[Inverse (website)|Inverse]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=January 17, 2021}}</ref> It was described as "almost unwatchably awful" and "a baffling piece of work" by Charles Bramesco of ''[[Uproxx]]'', who wrote that it was a "perennial contender in the battle for the title of Worst Movie Ever".<ref>{{cite web |last=Bramesco |first=Charles |title=20 Years Later, The Pure Stupidity Of 'Bio-Dome' Remains Unmatched |url=https://uproxx.com/movies/bio-dome-20th-anniversary/ |website=[[Uproxx]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=January 12, 2016}}</ref> ''[[The A.V. Club]]''{{'}}s Nathan Rabin wrote, "Critics and audiences alike found the ''Bio-Dome'' to be an abomination unto the Lord, an affront to the gods of cinema, and also a very bad movie, bad enough to be considered the gold standard of crapitude in Shore's oeuvre", noting that it had the lowest Metacritic score of any movie, with 1 out of 100.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Rabin, Nathan|author1-link=Nathan Rabin |title=I Watched This On Purpose: Bio-Dome |url=https://www.avclub.com/i-watched-this-on-purpose-bio-dome-1798214668 |website=[[The A.V. Club]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en-us |date=August 27, 2008}}</ref> ''Bio-Dome'' was named one of the worst movies of the 1990s in a poll conducted by [[RiffTrax]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Jodi |title=Rifftrax Compiles The 20 Worst Movies Of The 90s: Disagree With Them, Won't You? |url=https://www.pajiba.com/seriously_random_lists/rifftrax-compiles-the-20-worst-movies-of-the-90s.php |website=Pajiba |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=January 21, 2015}}</ref>

[[Kylie Minogue]], who starred in the film as oceanographer Petra von Kant, called appearing in the film the worst decision of her career.<ref name="inversekylie"/> For his performance in the movie, Shore won the [[Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Actor]] at the [[17th Golden Raspberry Awards]], tying with [[Tom Arnold (actor)|Tom Arnold]] for his performance in ''[[Big Bully (film)|Big Bully]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=In film, these were worst of 1996 |url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/1997/03/25/in-film-these-were-worst-of-1996/ |website=[[Tampa Bay Times]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=March 25, 1997}}</ref>

=== ''Batman & Robin'' (1997) ===
{{Main|Batman & Robin (film){{!}}''Batman & Robin'' (film)}}
[[File:Btrjpg.jpg|thumb|The [[comic book]] [[superhero]] sequel ''[[Batman & Robin (film)|Batman & Robin]]'' (1997) was named the worst movie ever made by ''[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]]''.]]
''Batman & Robin'' is a [[superhero film]] based on the [[DC Comics]] character [[Batman]], the sequel to the 1995 film ''[[Batman Forever]]'', and the fourth and final installment of [[Warner Bros.]]' [[Batman in film#Tim Burton and Joel Schumacher series (1989–1997)|initial ''Batman'' film series]]. It was directed by [[Joel Schumacher]] and stars [[George Clooney]] as [[Bruce Wayne (1989 film series character)|Bruce Wayne / Batman]], [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]] as [[Mr. Freeze]], [[Uma Thurman]] as [[Poison Ivy (character)|Poison Ivy]], [[Chris O'Donnell]] as [[Dick Grayson]] / [[Robin (character)|Robin]], [[Alicia Silverstone]] as [[Barbara Gordon|Barbara Wilson]] / [[Batgirl]], and [[Michael Gough]] as [[Alfred Pennyworth]]. The film was largely criticized for its [[toyetic]] and [[camp (style)|camp]] approach, and Mr. Freeze's approach and [[one-line joke]]s.

{{as of|2017|June}}, [[review aggregator]] Rotten Tomatoes reports that 11% of critics have given the film a positive review based on 89 reviews, certifying it "Rotten" with an average rating of 3.7/10, and the critics' consensus: "Joel Schumacher's tongue-in-cheek attitude hits an unbearable limit in ''Batman & Robin'', resulting in a frantic and mindless movie that's too jokey to care much for."<ref>{{cite web |url = https://rottentomatoes.com/m/1077027-batman_and_robin/ |title = Batman & Robin | website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date = July 6, 2019}}</ref> By comparison [[Metacritic]] collected an average score of 28/100, based on 21 reviews.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://metacritic.com/movie/batman-robin |title = Batman & Robin (1997): Reviews | work=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |access-date=April 17, 2010}}</ref> [[Michael J. Nelson]], of ''Mystery Science Theater 3000'' fame, wrote of the movie in his book, ''Movie Megacheese'', "''Batman & Robin'' is not the worst movie ever. No, indeed. It's the worst thing ever. Yes, it's the single worst thing that we as human beings have ever produced in recorded history."<ref>{{Cite book |url = https://archive.org/details/mikenelsonsmovie00nels |url-access = registration |page = [https://archive.org/details/mikenelsonsmovie00nels/page/79 79] |title = Mike Nelson's Movie Megacheese |publisher = Harper Collins |isbn = 978-0-380-81467-1 |last1 = Nelson |first1 = Michael J |date = June 20, 2000}}</ref> ''Batman & Robin'' also came in first in an ''Empire'' poll of the 50 worst films ever.<ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever"/> Joel Schumacher apologized to disappointed fans on the 2005 DVD release of ''Batman & Robin''.<ref>{{cite AV media |people = Joel Schmacher |title = "Making of" Introduction | medium = DVD |publisher = Warner Bros. |year = 2005 }}</ref> In 2021, Clooney stated that he refused to let his wife, [[Amal Clooney|Amal]], watch the film, saying, "There are certain films I just go, 'I want my wife to have some respect for me{{'"}}.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zack |date=2021-10-05 |title=George Clooney Refuses to Show 'Batman & Robin' to His Wife: 'I Want Her to Have Respect for Me' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/george-clooney-refuses-show-wife-batman-robin-1234669477/ |access-date=2023-07-13 |website=IndieWire |language=en-US}}</ref> Clooney later made a [[cameo appearance]] as Bruce Wayne in the [[DC Extended Universe]] film ''[[The Flash (film)|The Flash]]'' (2023).<ref>[https://variety.com/2023/film/news/george-clooney-refuses-batman-movies-the-flash-cameo-1235844045/ George Clooney Says There's 'Not Enough Drugs in the World' to Get Him to Play Batman Again, Even After 'The Flash' Cameo - Variety]</ref>

=== ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' (''The Day and the Night'') (1997) ===
{{Main|Day and Night (1997 film){{!}}''Day and Night'' (1997 film)}}
The French [[romance film]] ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' was directed by philosopher [[Bernard-Henri Lévy]]. It follows a French author who fled to Mexico for a quiet life and an actress who is willing to seduce him to get a part in a film adapted from one of his books. Before its release, ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' was heavily promoted in many French newspapers and magazines.<ref name="ti">Jade Lindgaard and Xavier De La Porte, ''The Imposter: BHL in Wonderland'' (Translated by John Howe) London; Verso, 2012. {{ISBN|978-1-84467-748-1}} (p. 48-9).</ref> When the film premiered at the [[Berlin International Film Festival]] in 1997, hundreds of journalists walked out of the screening and those that stayed ridiculed it.<ref name="Plato">{{cite news |last=Dahlburg |first=John-Thor |title=The Film That Plato Didn't Make |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=March 28, 1997 |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1997-03-28-ca-42798-story.html |access-date=October 14, 2013}}</ref> Following its release, ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' was harshly criticized by the French media, with overwhelmingly negative reviews appearing in publications such as ''[[Libération]]'', ''[[Le Monde]]'' and ''[[Le Nouvel Observateur]]''.<ref name="ti"/> The film also did poorly commercially, with only 73,147 seats for ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' having been sold two months after its release.<ref name="ti"/> ''[[L'Humanité]]'' called it an "Absolute debacle" and [[Michel Houellebecq]] referred to it as the "most preposterous film in history".<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Tim |title=Public Enemies by Michel Houellebecq and Bernard-Henri Lévy – review |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2011/dec/08/public-enemies-houellebecq-levy-review |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=May 10, 2023 |date=December 8, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=The volcano a molehill |newspaper=[[L'Humanité]] |date=February 19, 1997 |url=https://www.humanite.fr/node/154931 |access-date=October 14, 2013}}</ref> ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' was considered the worst French film since 1945 by film magazine ''[[Cahiers du cinéma]]'', and its status as the "worst film in history" was discussed by the French version of ''[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slate.fr/story/27925/pire-film-du-monde-bhl-concurrence |title='Le Jour et la Nuit', pire film de l'histoire ... Vraiment? |date=October 3, 2010 |work=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]|access-date=December 19, 2013}}</ref> Likewise, English-language film site ''[[/Film]]'' described its status as "one of the worst foreign language movies ever made", and filmmaker [[Claude Chabrol]] selected it as one of the worst movies ever made.<ref>{{cite web |last=Thiellement |first=Pacome |title=Le film que BHL n'a pas compris (pourtant c'est son préféré !) |url=https://www.blast-info.fr/emissions/2023/le-film-que-bhl-na-pas-compris-pourtant-cest-son-prefere-6fAP-oVYSFuCqF6zPuXNlA |website=[[:fr:Blast (web TV)|Blast le souffle de l'info]] |access-date=May 10, 2023 |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Pearson |first=Ben |title=BBC Polls Critics, Releases 100 Greatest Foreign Films List |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/562029/bbc-polls-critics-releases-100-greatest-foreign-films-list/ |website=[[/Film]] |access-date=May 10, 2023 |date=October 30, 2018}}</ref> An original documentary, ''Anatomy of a Massacre'', was released with the ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' DVD, and focused on its intense negative reception and failure.<ref>{{cite news |title=BHL et la critique ciné, c'était le jour et la nuit |newspaper=[[20 minutes (France)|20 Minutes]] |date=October 11, 2010 |url=http://www.20minutes.fr/medias/607145-media-bhl-critique-cine-jour-nuit |access-date=October 14, 2013}}</ref>

=== ''The Avengers'' (1998) ===
{{Main|The Avengers (1998 film){{!}}''The Avengers'' (1998 film)}}
An adaptation of the popular 1960s [[The Avengers (TV series)|British TV series]] of the same name, ''The Avengers'' starred [[Ralph Fiennes]] as John Steed and [[Uma Thurman]] as [[Emma Peel]], with [[Sean Connery]] as their antagonist, Sir August de Wynter. It was directed by [[Jeremiah S. Chechik]]. ''The Avengers'' began to receive negative publicity after [[Warner Bros.]], the film's distributor, refused to allow any early press-screenings for movie reviewers.<ref>{{cite news |author-link=Godfrey Cheshire |first=Godfrey |last=Cheshire |url=https://variety.com/1998/film/reviews/the-avengers-sputtering-spies-steed-and-peel-lack-appeal-1200454676/ |title=The Avengers – Sputtering Spies: Steed and Peel Lack Appeal |work=Variety |date=August 17, 1998 |access-date=June 27, 2022}}</ref> After early test screenings, ''The Avengers'' was heavily edited by the studio.<ref name="NYTreview2">{{cite news |first=Janet |last=Maslin |author-link=Janet Maslin |url=https://www.nytimes.com/library/film/081598avengers-film-review.html |title='The Avengers': Shh! They're Trying Not to Be Noticed |newspaper=The New York Times |date=August 15, 1998 |access-date=January 27, 2015 }}</ref> On its release, ''The Avengers'' was savaged by film critics, with the ''[[Birmingham Post]]'' stating "''The Avengers'' is being slated by critics as the worst film ever made" and adding that one reviewer had joked the film was such a "turkey" that the makers should have handed distribution to the poultry chain [[Bernard Matthews Farms|Bernard Matthews]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Film-''The Avengers'' |newspaper=The Birmingham Post |date=August 19, 1998 }}</ref> Several reviewers disparaged ''The Avengers'' for lacking the wit and excitement of its source material.<ref name="rt2">{{cite magazine |url=http://www.radiotimes.com/film/cjykx/the-avengers |title=Review: The Avengers |first=Alan |last=Jones |magazine=Radio Times |access-date=January 27, 2015 }}</ref><ref name="db">{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/entertainment/not-so-excellent-avengers-insults-old-series-awful-film-debases-tv-inspiration-article-1.807212 |title=Not So Excellent Avengers |first=David |last=Bianculli |newspaper=[[New York Daily News]] |date=August 18, 1998 |access-date=January 27, 2015 }}</ref> [[Janet Maslin]] strongly criticized ''The Avengers'': "With pseudo-suave repartee that would make [[Austin Powers (character)|Austin Powers]] blush and with so many shades of ''[[Howard the Duck (film)|Howard the Duck]]'' that one scene depicts man-size pastel teddy bears sitting around a conference table, it's a film to gall fans of the old TV series and perplex anyone else. I can't remember another Friday morning show where I heard actual cries of "Ugh!" on the way out the door" and finished her review with, "At a pared-down, barely rational 100 minutes, ''The Avengers'' is short but not short enough."<ref name="NYTreview2"/>

David Bianculli said, "This ''Avengers'' film is so horrendously, painfully and thoroughly awful, it gives other cinematic clunkers like ''[[#Ishtar (1987)|Ishtar]]'' and ''Howard the Duck'' a good name."<ref name="db"/> Alan Jones in ''[[The Radio Times]]'' stated "The cult 1960s TV series gets royally shafted by Hollywood in this stunningly designed blockbuster that's stunningly awful in every other department ... Terrible special effects and zero chemistry between Fiennes and Thurman make this notorious disaster a total waste of everyone's time and energy."<ref name="rt2"/> ''The Avengers'' also shared a [[Razzie Award]] for "Worst Remake or Sequel" with the 1998 adaptations of ''[[Psycho (1998 film)|Psycho]]'' and ''[[Godzilla (1998 film)|Godzilla]]'' at the [[19th Golden Raspberry Awards]]. ''Total Film'' magazine later voted Fiennes and Thurman in ''The Avengers'' as "The Worst Movie Double Act Of All Time".<ref>{{cite news |title=Double disasters make it to top of the flops |newspaper=[[Western Mail (Wales)|The Western Mail]] |location=Cardiff |date=December 1, 2003 }}</ref> The film also appeared on Metacritic's list of the all-time lowest-scoring films.<ref name="Metacritic"/>

=== ''Fatal Deviation'' (1998) ===
{{Main|Fatal Deviation{{!}}''Fatal Deviation''}}
''Fatal Deviation'' is often credited as being the first [[martial arts film]] to be filmed in Ireland. It stars martial artist James Bennett and [[Michael Graham (singer)|Michael Graham]], who is best known for being a member of the boy band [[Boyzone]]. ''[[The Irish Post]]'' and ''[[Den of Geek]]'' write that it is a mainstay of worst film lists.<ref name="irishpost"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/fatal-deviation/looking-back-at-fatal-deviation-irelands-only-martial-arts-film|title=Meet Fatal Deviation, Ireland's only martial arts film|last=Lines|first=Craig|date=November 4, 2015|access-date=June 7, 2019|work=[[Den of Geek]]|archive-date=June 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190607211617/https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/fatal-deviation/looking-back-at-fatal-deviation-irelands-only-martial-arts-film|url-status=dead}}</ref> Luke McKinney of [[Cracked.com]] called it the worst film ever made, writing: "There are so many things about making a movie that Jimmy doesn't know, that you could replace film school with this movie alone—just screening it once for students and asking them to list all the things it did wrong. Anyone who doesn't write 'everything' instantly fails."<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.cracked.com/article_18632_irelands-only-kung-fu-movie-is-worst-film-ever-made.html|title=Ireland's Only Kung Fu Movie (Is The Worst Film Ever Made)|last=McKinney|first=Luke|date=July 3, 2010|access-date=March 9, 2019|work=[[Cracked.com]]}}</ref> ''[[The Irish Post]]'' named it the worst Irish film of all time,<ref name="irishpost">{{cite web |url= https://www.irishpost.com/entertainment/definitive-ranking-7-worst-irish-films-time-158594|title= A definitive ranking of the 7 worst Irish films of all-time|first=Aidan|last=Lonergan|date= August 16, 2018|access-date= March 9, 2019|work= [[The Irish Post]]}}</ref> the ''[[Irish Independent]]'' wrote that it is "regarded as one of the worst films ever made" and ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' called it "one of the worst commercial movies ever made".<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.independent.ie/lifestyle/westlife-what-next-26785226.html|title=Westlife: what next?|date= October 22, 2011|access-date=March 9, 2019|work=[[Irish Independent]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Boehm |first=Simon |title=Ireland's First Martial Arts Movie Is Gloriously Bad |url=https://www.cbr.com/fatal-deviation-ireland-martial-arts-movie-cult-classic/ |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |access-date=July 13, 2022 |date=March 15, 2021}}</ref> ''[[Entertainment.ie]]'' placed it on its list of "10 So Bad They're Good Movies You Need To See Before You Die" and it was covered in ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]''{{'}}s ''Bad Movie Diaries'' column.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://entertainment.ie/cinema/movie-news/10-so-bad-theyre-good-movies-you-need-to-see-before-you-die-227463/|title=10 So Bad They're Good Movies You Need To See Before You Die|last=Lloyd|first=Bryan|access-date=March 9, 2019|work=[[entertainment.ie]]|date=March 12, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2018/07/bad-movie-diaries-fatal-deviation-1998.html |title=Bad Movie Diaries: Fatal Deviation (1998)|last1=Vorel|first1=Jim|last2=Lowe|first2=Kenneth|access-date=June 7, 2019|work=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]|date=July 31, 2018}}</ref>

=== ''Parting Shots'' (1999) ===
{{Main|Parting Shots{{!}}''Parting Shots''}}
The British [[black comedy]] ''Parting Shots'' was the last film directed by [[Michael Winner]]. It starred rock musician [[Chris Rea]] as a man who, after being told he has only six months to live, begins murdering people who have wronged him. [[Andrew Collins (broadcaster)|Andrew Collins]] took a very negative view of the film: "''Parting Shots'' ... is going to set the course of British film-making back 20 years. It is not only the worst British film produced in this country since ''[[Carry On Emmannuelle]]'' (quite a feat in itself), it is a thoroughbred contender for the crown of Worst Film Ever Made."<ref>Andrew Collins, "How to Shoot a Real Turkey" ''[[The Observer]]'', March 28, 1999. ''Observer Screen'', p.6.</ref> In an interview about the film, Charlotte O'Sullivan, the [[The Independent|''Independent'']]{{'}}s film editor, claimed ''Parting Shots'' was "the worst film I've ever seen". O'Sullivan also criticized it for glorifying vigilantism: "It's Michael Winner and you know, he doesn't have any sense of irony. He seems to be saying it is okay to go and kill people."<ref>"Winner's Turkey has a bad aftertaste". ''[[The Sunday Herald]]'', May 2, 1999 (p.7)</ref> The journalist [[Miles Kington]] later claimed "''Parting Shots'' ... was directed by Michael Winner and despite the glittering cast, was possibly the worst film ever made."<ref>Miles Kingston, "One or two plots to occupy my declining years". ''[[The Independent]]'', May 3, 2005, (p.30).</ref> I. Q. Hunter listed ''Parting Shots'' as one of the candidates for "the Worst British film ever made".<ref name="iqh"/> ''Parting Shots'' was also featured in a poll of ''Empire'' magazine readers' "50 Worst Movies Ever" poll.<ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever"/>

=== ''The Underground Comedy Movie'' (1999) ===
{{Main|The Underground Comedy Movie{{!}}''The Underground Comedy Movie''}}
''The Underground Comedy Movie'' is based on a [[cable access]] show from 1988. Director and lead actor [[Vince Offer]] constructed the film out of a series of tasteless, [[low culture|lowbrow skits]]<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eXCwEb1qfcA The Bizarre Scandals of TV Commercial Stars - wavywebstuff on YouTube]</ref> (including [[Gena Lee Nolin]] loudly using the restroom and a superhero named ''Dickman'' who dresses in a giant [[human penis|penis]] costume and defeats his enemies by squirting them with [[semen]]). In 1999, Offer filed a suit against [[20th Century Fox]] and the co-directors of ''[[There's Something About Mary]]'' (1998), [[Farrelly brothers|Bobby and Peter Farrelly]], claiming that 14 scenes in ''Mary'' were stolen from his film.<ref name="ewol">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/article/1999/06/11/underground-comedy-movie-2/|title=Movie Review Underground Comedy Movie|date=June 11, 1999|access-date=December 3, 2019|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last=Gleiberman|first=Owen|archive-date=November 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105184521/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,273701,00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Farrellys released this statement: "We've never heard of him, we've never heard of his movie, and it's all a bunch of baloney."<ref name="ewx">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/article/1998/10/16/monitor-269/|title=Monitor: Celebrity news for October 16, 1998|last1=Karger|first1=Dave|first2=Suna|last2=Chang|date=October 16, 1998|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=December 3, 2019|archive-date=November 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105184053/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,285287,00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Lawrence Van Gelder]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' referred to it as a "wretched film" and stated that "''The Underground Comedy Movie'' stands as a monument to ineptitude and self-delusion."<ref name="nytvangelder">{{cite news|url=https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/library/film/052899comedy-film-review.html|title=Lawrence Van Gelder's review of ''The Underground Comedy Movie'' |last=Van Gelder |first=Lawrence |author-link=Lawrence Van Gelder |work=[[The New York Times]]|date=May 28, 1999 |access-date=December 19, 2013}}</ref> [[Rod Dreher]] of the ''[[New York Post]]'' said it "may be the least amusing comedy ever made".<ref>{{cite news|last=Dreher|first=Rod|author-link=Rod Dreher|title='Comedy' is Really Buried by Its Trash|work=[[New York Post]]|date=May 28, 1999}}</ref> Dave Shulman of ''[[L.A. Weekly]]'' described it as a "serious contender for the single worst movie ever made",<ref>{{cite web |title=Critic's Corner S-Z |url=http://thestinkers.com/critics3.html#Underground%20Comedy%20Movie |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010412233933/http://thestinkers.com/critics3.html#Underground%20Comedy%20Movie |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 12, 2001 |website=[[Stinkers Bad Movie Awards]] |access-date=July 9, 2022}}</ref> while Stinkers Bad Movie Awards co-founder Mike Lancaster said that it was the worst film that he had ever paid to see.<ref name="Lancaster"/> [[Nathan Rabin]] covered the film in his column detailing terrible films and stated that: "nothing I've covered for this column was quite as soul-crushingly, brain-meltingly terrible as ... ''The Underground Comedy Movie'''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nathanrabin.com/happy-place/2018/9/4/this-looks-terrible-the-underground-comedy-movie-1999|title=This Looks Terrible! The Underground Comedy Movie (1999)|last=Rabin|first=Nathan|author-link=Nathan Rabin|work=nathanrabin.com|date=September 4, 2018|access-date=February 23, 2019}}</ref> Thom Bennett at ''[[Film Journal International]]'', wrote "Anyone offended by unbearably bad films, jokes that are not funny and wasting 90 minutes of their lives is, as promised, guaranteed to be offended. In fact, to even call this mess a comedy is giving it far too much credit", and "''The Underground Comedy Movie'' may well be the worst film I have ever seen."<ref name="fji">{{cite web|url=http://www.filmjournal.com/filmjournal/esearch/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1000697847|title=Underground Comedy Movie, The|last=Bennett|first=Thom|work=[[Film Journal International]]|access-date=March 7, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105184223/http://www.filmjournal.com/filmjournal/esearch/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1000697847|archive-date=November 5, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Writing in ''[[Central Western Daily]]'', Peter Young said, "I am pretty sure that I can declare this The Worst Film I Have Ever Seen."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.centralwesterndaily.com.au/story/1386763/comedy-film-best-kept-underground/|title=Comedy film best kept underground|last=Young|first=Peter|work=[[Central Western Daily]]|date=March 26, 2013|access-date=March 6, 2018}}</ref>

==2000==
=== ''Battlefield Earth'' (2000) ===
{{Main|Battlefield Earth (film){{!}}''Battlefield Earth'' (film)}}
[[File:John Travolta Battlefield Earth signing.jpg|thumb|[[John Travolta]] during ''[[Battlefield Earth (film)|Battlefield Earth]]''{{'s}} promotional tour]]

''Battlefield Earth'' is based on the first half of [[L. Ron Hubbard]]'s 1982 [[Battlefield Earth (novel)|novel of the same name]], and stars [[John Travolta]], [[Barry Pepper]] and [[Forest Whitaker]]. It was criticized for its script, acting, overuse of [[Dutch angle]]s, dialogue, several inconsistencies, and plot holes. The film has a 3% rating at Rotten Tomatoes,<ref>{{Rotten Tomatoes|qid=Q811023|title=Battlefield Earth}}</ref> where it is included in the top 100 worst-reviewed movies of all time.<ref name="rt100worst"/><ref name="rottenworst">{{cite web |url=https://rottentomatoes.com/guides/worst_of_the_worst/ |title=The worst of the worst pictures |website=Rotten Tomatoes |date=September 21, 2009 |access-date=January 17, 2011 |archive-date=November 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101123212257/http://www.rottentomatoes.com/guides/worst_of_the_worst/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Roger Ebert predicted that the film, "for decades to come will be the punch line of jokes about bad movies",<ref name="BEarth">{{cite news |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/battlefield-earth-2000 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |title=Battlefield Earth movie review (2000) |date=May 12, 2000 |access-date=October 11, 2020 |last=Ebert |first=Roger |author-link=Roger Ebert}}</ref> and placed it on his "most hated" list.<ref name="eberthated"/> Nathan Rabin covered the film as part of his ''My World of Flops'' column for ''[[The A.V. Club]]'', calling it "a fiasco that occupies a distinguished place high atop the pantheon of widely reviled crap" and said, "A legendary disaster well before it finished completion, ''Battlefield Earth'' hit theaters with a 'Kick Me' sign on it so massive it could be detected from outer space."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.avclub.com/my-year-of-flops-case-file-66-battlefield-earth-1798212540 |title=My Year OF Flops Case File #66: Battlefield Earth |last=Rabin |first=Nathan |author-link=Nathan Rabin |website=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=September 11, 2007 |language=en-US |access-date=January 27, 2019}}</ref>

The film ultimately won nine [[Golden Raspberry Awards]], including Worst Picture, Worst Screen Couple (John Travolta and "anyone on the screen with him"), and a special award in 2010 as the Worst Picture of the Decade.<ref name="30thRazzies">{{cite web |title=Razzie Noms for Worst Picture of the Decade |work=Razzies.com |url=http://www.razzies.com/history/09NomPOD.asp |access-date=February 2, 2010}}</ref> This was the most Razzies won by any film in the history of the awards at the time,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.razzies.com/history/07release.asp |title=Golden Raspberry Award Foundation |work=Razzies.com |access-date=November 18, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130321103846/http://www.razzies.com/history/07release.asp |archive-date=March 21, 2013}}</ref> a record it held until ''[[Jack and Jill (2011 film)|Jack and Jill]]'' surpassed it with 10 wins in 2012.<ref name=RazzieWin>{{cite news |title=Adam Sandler movie Jack and Jill sweeps Razzie awards |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-17582458 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=April 2, 2012 |access-date=May 17, 2012}}</ref> Listing the film as one of the worst decisions in movie history, ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' quipped that, "If Earth sticks around long enough for the Golden Raspberry Awards to hand out a 'worst movie of the century' at their 2100 ceremony, it'll probably win that, too."<ref name="50decisions"/> The movie appeared on Metacritic's list of the all-time lowest-scoring films,<ref name="Metacritic"/> and is on the [[Movie Review Query Engine]]'s (MRQE) 50 Worst Movies list,<ref name="MRQE50">{{cite web |url=https://www.mrqe.com/lists/50_worst_movies |title=50 Worst Movies |work=[[Movie Review Query Engine]] |access-date=April 17, 2019}}</ref> as well as worst film lists from ''Screen Rant'', ''Vanity Fair'', ''Flavorwire'', ''[[Digital Trends]]'' and the ''New York Daily News''.<ref name="Flavorwire">{{cite web|url=http://flavorwire.com/477608/the-50-worst-movies-ever-made/view-all |title=The 50 Worst Movies Ever Made|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330132846/https://www.flavorwire.com/477608/the-50-worst-movies-ever-made/view-all |first=Jason |last=Bailey |date= September 17, 2014|access-date=November 19, 2025|archive-date=March 30, 2019 |work=[[Flavorwire]]}}</ref><ref name="Screen Rant"/><ref name="italianvanity"/><ref name="digitaltrends">{{cite web|url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/movies/worst-movies-ever-made/|title=10 Worst Movies You Can Watch|work=[[Digital Trends]]|last=Nicol|first=Will|date=May 10, 2017|access-date=July 28, 2017}}</ref><ref name="NYDN">{{cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/worst-movies-made-gallery-1.3678697|title=The worst movies ever made|last=Lisi|first=Brian|work=[[New York Daily News]]|date=December 5, 2017 |access-date=March 14, 2018}}</ref> ''Empire'' named it the second worst movie ever made after ''[[Batman & Robin (film)|Batman & Robin]]'' and ''[[The Register]]'' listed it as the worst movie ever made.<ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever"/><ref name="battlefieldregister">{{cite web |title=Battlefield Earth ruled worst film Ever |work=[[The Register]]|last=Haines |first=Lester |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2012/04/20/worst_movie/ |access-date=April 5, 2018 |date=April 20, 2012}}</ref> Pepper and Whitaker both expressed regret for their involvement in ''Battlefield Earth'', while film screenwriter [[J. David Shapiro]] later apologized for making "the suckiest movie ever".<ref>{{cite web |last=Dembrow |first=Dylan |title=15 Things You Didn't Know About The Disastrous Battlefield Earth |url=https://screenrant.com/battlefield-earth-movie-worst-trivia-facts-secrets/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |date=January 28, 2018 |access-date=December 5, 2020}}</ref><ref name="battlefieldregister"/>

===''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' (2000)===
{{main|Titanic: The Legend Goes On{{!}}''Titanic: The Legend Goes On''}}
''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' (also known as ''Titanic, mille e una storia'', ''Titanic: La leggenda continua'' and ''Titanic: The Animated Movie'') is an Italian animated [[mockbuster]] about [[Sinking of the Titanic|the sinking]] of the {{RMS|Titanic}}. It features a similar romantic storyline to [[Titanic (1997 film)|James Cameron's 1997 film]], but also has a number of talking animals (most notably, a [[rapping]] dog).<ref name="screenrantanimated">{{cite web|date=January 15, 2017|title=12 Worst Animated Movies of All Time|url=http://screenrant.com/worst-animated-movies-all-time/|access-date=January 7, 2022|work=[[Screen Rant]]|archive-date=January 8, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220108225848/https://screenrant.com/worst-animated-movies-all-time/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Reviews condemned the quality of the animation and criticized the plot for being insensitive to the memory of the victims of the ''Titanic''.<ref name="screenrantanimated"/>

''[[Total Film]]'' named ''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' as "officially the worst film ever made", after it topped a list of the 66 worst films ever.<ref name=TotalFilm/> An article from ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]'' also described it as one of the worst films ever made, but notes that it "[lacks] the cult following that other bad films often acquire", stating: "''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' is too heinous for such fond pleasures."<ref>{{cite web |last=Mattson |first=Kelcie |title=I Watched the Animated Titanic Musical So You Don't Have To |url=https://collider.com/titanic-animated-movie/ |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=May 3, 2024 |language=en |date=September 11, 2023}}</ref> Critic Tim Brayton said that "It is one of the most surreally bad films I have ever encountered", adding: "For sheer mesmerising grotesqueness, there's almost nothing I can name that beats it, and no fan of bad movies can say that their life is complete till they've been exposed to it."<ref>{{cite web |title=Titanic: The Animated Movie |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/titanic_the_animated_movie |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |access-date=January 28, 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Brayton |first=Tim |title=Titanic: The Legend Goes On... (2000) – Movie Review |url=https://www.alternateending.com/2020/05/titanic-the-legend-goes-on-2000.html |website=Alternate Ending |access-date=January 28, 2022 |date=May 20, 2020}}</ref> ''Total Film'' also included the film on a list of the worst kids' movies, describing it as being "widely considered one of the worst animated films ever made",<ref name="kidsmovie"/> while Spanish film magazine ''[[Fotogramas]]'' selected it as one of the 20 worst films ever made.<ref name="fotogramas"/> ''[[Screen Rant]]'' included it on a list of the 12 worst animated films of all time, and it topped a ''Showbiz Cheat Sheet'' list of the top 10 worst animated films ever, with author Will Roberts commenting that "[any] list of the worst animated films of all time begins with ... ''Titanic: The Legend Goes On''".<ref name="screenrantanimated"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cheatsheet.com/entertainment/worst-animated-movies.html/|title=10 Worst Animated Movies of All Time|work=Showbiz Cheat Sheet|last=Roberts|first=Will|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=January 28, 2022|archive-date=January 22, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122103918/https://www.cheatsheet.com/entertainment/worst-animated-movies.html/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, ''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' became the lowest-rated film on [[IMDb]]'s Bottom 100 list.<ref>{{cite web |last=Renzetti |first=Jackie |title=Not Your Cameron's 'Titanic' |url=https://mndaily.com/223181/arts-entertainment/not-your-camerons-titanic/ |newspaper=[[The Minnesota Daily]] |date= April 16, 2014|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>
